texts: Whisper not "tomorrow" to the restless hour, for what the heart means to do, let it do now before the moment slips by.

Write me a doha for someone who keeps putting off the one important task on their list, reminding them that what is meant for tomorrow should be started this very hour, before the chance quietly leaves.
need a doha that kicks me to start my assignment right now instead of tomorrow lol
do it now
I have been telling my sister for two years that I will call our estranged uncle next week, and last night she said, you have said next week since 2022.
Compose a Kabir style couplet that says what you plan to do tomorrow you should do today, and what you plan today you should do this moment, since delay slowly eats the best intentions of anyone.
Tomorrow is a promise made by the idle, O friend; today alone is in thy hand, so use it.
doha pls: stop delaying, do it today. i always say ill start monday and never do
My gym membership has run for eleven months and I have been three times, always planning to begin properly next week, and my wife just stared at me when I said it again.
today, not tomorrow
I keep telling myself I will study tomorrow and then tomorrow comes and I do nothing, so write a doha that tells me what is to be done later must be done now, no more waiting.
My father wanted to apologise to his brother for a decade, always when the right occasion came, and the right occasion never did, which I think about whenever I put off a hard conversation.
The hour of "someday" never arrives; only the step taken now makes a beginning.
plz write something about stop procrastinating, like just begin
begin today
At the crossroads of my career I kept telling my friend I'd decide after the holidays, and a swan paddling on the pond nearby seemed to say it never waits for the perfect season.
crossroads, swan, act now
doha w a swan and a crossroads, about doing it today and not waiting for tomorrow
At the crossroads the swan chooses and glides on; tomorrow's shore is never reached by those who linger.

Write a Kabir style doha where a traveller stands dithering at the crossroads while a swan has already set off across the water, teaching that what must be done should be done now before the chance is gone.
I kept saying I would tell my mother I loved her next time we spoke, but my tongue stayed tied for years, and now I do not want to wait one more call.
Please write a doha about the tongue that postpones kind words and sayings until tomorrow, reminding us to speak what is in the heart today because the moment for it passes quicker than we think.
doha about saying it today, my tongue freezes whenever i want to say sorry
tongue, say it now
O tongue, why delay the sweet word? Speak this hour, for the hush of tomorrow may keep it forever.
The lotus opens when the light calls, not when it chooses to; so open thy heart this day, not tomorrow.
lotus, now not later
Write a doha in which the lotus does not wait for a better morning to bloom but opens with the first light, teaching the one who always postpones his work to start this very day.
doha about a lotus blooming as soon as light touches it, no delay. i need that energy for my project
My teacher once pointed at the lotus pond in our school and said the flowers don't ask whether tomorrow will be better, they just open, and I still put off my homework.
stop postponing
My brother has been saying for nine years that he will finish his half-written novel when life gets calmer, and last month he turned forty.
doha on not putting things off til later pls, i have a bad habit
I want a doha in the Kabir spirit which says that tomorrow is uncertain but today is in our hands, so whatever good we plan to do, do it at once, because delay is the enemy of every plan.
What the heart says tomorrow, the hands must do now; for the hour that is spent can never be asked back.
I have owed my friend a visit for four years because I was always busy, and last week he moved abroad, so now I tell everyone to stop saying later.
Write a couplet on how people say they will do good deeds later, when they have time, yet life flows on and the chance disappears, so the wise act while they are able to.
never later
Say not "later" to the open hour, for she turns her face from the one who hesitates.
doha pls. do the thing today not later, my to-do list is a graveyard
Write a doha where a man walks through the market meaning to buy what he needs tomorrow, kicks a stone, and finds that tomorrow the chance is gone, so what is to be done must be done now.
At the market I saw a woman put back a good price on cloth saying she'd come tomorrow, and later a stone fell on the stall and it was all closed, so now I don't postpone anything.
In the market of days the bargain is struck now; tomorrow the stone is in the path and the stall is gone.
doha idea market and stone, if u dont buy it today its gone, i mean act on things now
market, stone, now
doha with a crow and a lion about doing today what you want to do, the crow just acts while the lion thinks too long
The crow seizes the morsel while the lion ponders; do your deed this hour, for hesitation starves.
My manager mulled over the proposal for months like a lion circling, while a smaller rival like a crow just grabbed the client the same afternoon.
crow, lion, act now
Write a doha in which the crow does at once what it intends, while the lion sits and postpones his hunt until the day is gone, teaching that action today beats strength with delay.
leaf, oil press, now
My uncle at the oil press told me the leaf that falls today will not rise tomorrow, so I should send my application before the deadline instead of tinkering with it forever.
doha with a leaf and an oil press about doing the work now not later, thx
The oil press turns, a leaf drifts down; what is yours to do will not wait on the wind of tomorrow.
Write a doha about the oil press that must be run today to get oil, and the fallen leaf that cannot go back up, showing that tasks postponed are lost and work should be done now.
The loom waits not for the weaver's mood; one row woven today is worth a hundred he will promise tomorrow.
weaver's loom, start now
doha about weaver's loom and not delaying the work, i need to stop saying tomorrow
Compose a doha in which the weaver sits at his loom the very moment the light comes, never saying he will begin tomorrow, so that a procrastinating mind may learn to start the work now.
My grandfather sat at his loom every dawn without fail and used to say a day he put off was a day's weaving lost, and that is why I now open my laptop at six.
The hour that is now is the only hour that is ours; the rest is only a promise.
My friend kept saying he would propose to his girlfriend after the next promotion, and then the next, and she finally married someone who asked sooner.
today is yours
Please write a doha for a young person who keeps saying they will start life properly once everything is perfect, reminding them that the perfect moment never comes and today is the only time given.
can u gimme a doha on how u should do stuff now cuz later never comes
doha with a thief and a crossroads, the thief of time is putting stuff off, i keep losing days
crossroads, thief of time
At the crossroads waits the thief called "Later", and he steals the hours of those who linger.
I stood at the crossroads of two job offers for three weeks saying I'd decide tomorrow, until both were given away, and my brother said delay is a quiet thief.
Write a doha where the thief waits at the crossroads and steals from every traveller who lingers, teaching that procrastination robs us of the day and what must be done should be done at once.
Write me a doha about a man who constantly says I will start saving, I will start exercising, I will start learning, and never does, and show that what is done now is worth more than a hundred plans.
something short like a doha on starting right now. been procrastinating on my taxes for weeks
start now or never
Plans are only breath unless they are begun; leave nothing to the later hour, but do it now.
My mother has had a lump on her arm checked for six months because she keeps saying it can wait till after my cousin's wedding, and I want her to go this week.
Write a doha where the heron watches the shallows while the net hangs idle, and the owner says he'll cast it tomorrow, teaching that opportunity passes and work delayed is work lost.
The heron strikes at once, the net lies folded; the one who says "tomorrow" gathers only empty water.
My uncle's net stayed untouched in the shed all week while he said the heron was no threat to his pond, and by Saturday the pond was empty.
doha with a heron and a net about acting today, not waiting around
heron, net, act now
doha for me, i keep telling myself ill call my mom later, then forget
Last Diwali I told my father I would visit for the weekend after my deadlines, and then the deadlines kept coming, and now I've decided to take the next bus.
do good today
Kind deeds fade by evening, so gather them this morning, ere the hour forgets.
Write a doha reminding us that kindness and goodness we intend to show others should be shown today, since the hour of chance passes quickly and no one is promised another.
I kept pushing off the hem on my daughter's dress, saying I'd stitch it tomorrow, and the day of the school function came with a loose thread and no time at all.
Compose a doha in which a single loose thread, left alone until tomorrow, pulls apart the whole cloth, so that a small task postponed grows large and the sensible mend it at once.
thread, do it now
doha w thread in it about not delaying, like fix the small thing now before it unravels
One loose thread, mended today, saves the garment; left for tomorrow, it unravels the whole weave.
Write a Kabir style doha for a student who has months to prepare but spends each day in leisure thinking there is plenty of time, then panics at the end, reminding him to begin now.
I once watched my cousin leave his thesis for the last fortnight, working through five nights without sleep, and now I begin even the dull tasks on the first day.
no delay
doha on starting early, deadline stress is killing me
The long day of "plenty of time" ends in a hurried dusk; begin while the morning is still young.
doha with scales and about doing good things right now, the scales of time tip and then its too late
Write a doha in which the scales weigh each day exactly the same, and the one who puts off his work for tomorrow finds the balance tilted against him, for time once gone is never regained.
The scales of the hours tip quickly, O friend; what you hold back for tomorrow is already weighed and lost.
scales, now not later
The scales my grandmother used to weigh lentils grew a little off each season as she kept postponing getting them fixed, and I realize now she lost money on every sale.
doha w a blind man in it - the one who keeps delaying is like him, cant see time slipping away
blind man, wasted days
The blind man cannot see the hours pass, nor can the one who says "tomorrow"; both walk past their chance.
I helped an old blind man cross the street this morning and he said, nothing waits for me, son, so do what you can today, which made me feel awful about my pending work.
Write a doha comparing the person who always postpones to a blind man who cannot see how quickly the days are passing, and urging that what is worth doing be done this very day.
The moneylender counts his diamond twice but never sells; wise is he who spends the hour today.
My uncle, a moneylender, kept a diamond locked away waiting for a better price for years, and when he finally went to sell, prices had crashed, so I act at once now.
Write a doha about a moneylender who hoards his diamond and says he will make use of it tomorrow, but the day never comes, teaching that value unused today is wasted and good deeds delayed are lost.
moneylender, diamond, now
doha w a moneylender and a diamond: use what u have today, dont wait for a perfect time
My grandfather always said he would build us a palace of a home someday, and he died with only the plan in his pocket, so I am beginning my own small life right now.
Write a doha about a king who keeps promising a palace to his people tomorrow, yet never lays one brick, teaching that action now is worth more than a grand plan postponed again and again.
palace of tomorrow
doha about a palace people dream of but never start building, i wanna do things now
A palace dreamed on tomorrow's soil rises not; one brick laid today is worth a thousand sighs.
can u write a doha on do it now, im a chronic procrastinator
I would like a doha to put up on my wall that tells me whatever work is waiting should be done at this moment, without excuses, because the one who keeps delaying ends with nothing in his hands.
now, now, now
The present moment waits at thy threshold; welcome him with deeds, for he will not knock twice.
Every New Year I make a list of resolutions that I tell myself I will start from the next month, and by December nothing has changed, and my wife has stopped asking.
doha w a bridge: build it today, dont wait or the gap gets wider

Write a doha about a man who delays building a bridge until the next season, and finds the water risen and the work harder, teaching that what is done now is easy and what is deferred grows difficult.
Lay the first plank of the bridge this morning, for the floods of tomorrow widen every gap.
bridge, build today
My cousin postponed patching things up with his friend until the rift felt unbridgeable, and my father said a bridge built early is a short one.
Our neighbour has been meaning to repair her relationship with her daughter since the day they argued, and she keeps waiting for the perfect moment to call, which has not come in six years.
stop delaying
doha pls, about how if u wanna do something do it right now, got a bad habit of waiting
Say not "tomorrow" to thy heart's good wish; the present hour is the only one that obeys.
Write me a Kabir doha for the lazy-minded who always have a reason to start later, explaining that whatever is to be done should be done at this very moment because the next hour is not yours.
Write a doha where the mosque call is heard at dawn and the dew is still on the ground, telling the sleeper not to wait until noon, for what must be done is best done while the morning is fresh.
doha w mosque and dew, wake up and do it now, mornings go fast
While the dew still clings and the mosque stands hushed in the dawn, rise and begin, for the noon dries all excuses.
Every morning the mosque near our building wakes the whole street while the dew is still on the grass, and my neighbour says that is when to start your work, not after lunch.
mosque, dew, begin now
Write a doha for a person who has a difficult conversation to have with someone they love and keeps delaying it, saying the best moment to make things right is now, before the distance grows wider.
My husband has been avoiding paying the electricity bill for three months because he says he'll go to the office next week, and today they cut our supply and he finally went.
doha about doing hard things first thing, not tomorrow
The hard thing delayed grows heavier by the hour; face it today while thy strength is fresh.
do the hard thing today
Why wait for the perfect season, O seeker? The deed done now is already perfect.
I wanted to start learning guitar after I got a good job, then after I moved cities, then after my wedding, and now I'm forty and have never touched one.
Please write a doha about people who wait for the perfect conditions before beginning anything, and show that the right time is always now and that the wise begin with whatever they have.
plz a doha about not waiting for perfect timing, just start
start, don't wait
doha w a sword in it: the sword rusts if u dont use it, same with ur plans, do it today
My grandfather's old sword hung on the wall unused for sixty years, rusting while he kept planning to polish it, and my father says do not let your own talents rust the same way.
sword, use it now
Write a doha about a warrior who keeps his sword sheathed until tomorrow's battle and finds it rusted, teaching that skills and good intentions must be used today or they decay with delay.
The sword that sleeps in its sheath till tomorrow wakes to rust; strike thy good work now.
O wavering heart, what is not begun now is already lost, and "tomorrow" is a promise that never keeps its word.
doha about doing stuff now, like seriously just do it
I told my kids I'd teach them chess this weekend, then the next, and last week my eldest said, Dad, you always say next time.
Compose a doha that says the person who says I will do it later is cheating himself, because the thing postponed is the thing never done, and only the work begun today bears any result.
now or never
Open the door this very hour, O friend, for the guest of opportunity does not stand outside forever.
A salesman waited outside our door for an hour yesterday while I told my wife I'll sign up for the course next week, and she said that is exactly the problem with you.
Write a doha about a door that stands open for just a short while and the man who says he will walk through tomorrow, only to find it shut, teaching that chances are used now or lost.
doha with a door - if u dont walk thru today its closed tmrw. i keep missing chances
open door, go now
The door of the old furnace room swung open and shut as the smith kept saying he'd fix the leak tomorrow, and the whole stock cooled and was spoiled by morning.
furnace, door, act now
Strike while the furnace glows and the door stands open; cold iron laughs at "tomorrow".
doha w furnace and a door, about acting when the time is hot, not later
Compose a doha in which the furnace is hot and the door is open, and the smith who postpones his hammering until tomorrow finds the metal cold, teaching that every task has its moment and it is now.
skeleton, do it now
doha w a skeleton: u keep saying later but later is just bones lol, do it now
Write a doha in which a skeleton lies where a man once said he would do good tomorrow, showing that the days of delay turn to nothing and only deeds done today are real.
At the anatomy lab our professor pointed at the skeleton and said the owner probably meant to finish many things tomorrow, so don't leave your thesis for next semester.
The skeleton keeps no calendar and no promises; whatever thou meanest to do, do it while thy hands are warm.

Write a doha where the spinning wheel keeps turning every day while the lazy man says he'll climb the mountain tomorrow, teaching that the day's work is done today and distant goals are reached by daily action.
doha w a mountain and spinning wheel, begin the climb today not someday
mountain, spinning wheel, today
My great aunt spun yarn on her wheel each day even as the mountain loomed over the village, and she told me never to put off the first step of any climb.
The spinning wheel turns today, the mountain waits for no one; take thy first step, O dreamer.
Write a Kabir doha for a young man who has a fine idea but wants to wait until he is older, richer and more skilled before he begins, reminding him that the first step is best taken today.
Not when the omens align, nor when the means are full, but when thy heart says now, begin.
My roommate has had a business idea since college, and he says he'll start when he has saved enough, while his rival with half the idea launched last month and has customers.
first step, today
doha about starting my dream project today instead of waiting till im ready
grindstone, work today
Write a doha where the grindstone must be turned each day to get flour, and the man who says he will grind tomorrow goes hungry tonight, teaching that today's work cannot be saved for later.
My mother turns the grindstone first thing every dawn and calls it a sin to leave the day's work for the next, and I still leave my dishes for the morning.
doha with a grindstone: do the days work today or the flour doesnt come, you get it
The grindstone grinds the grain of this day only; tomorrow's hunger is not fed by today's idleness.
doha: stop saying ill do it later, ive got stuff piling up
today, do it today
For two years I've said I'd get my driving licence after the busy season, and my son passed his test last week at eighteen, which made me feel quite small.
Write a doha for someone whose unfinished tasks are piling up higher every week, telling them that what is put off today doubles tomorrow and the only way to lighten the load is to start now.
The piled-up "laters" grow into a wall by evening; break the first piece of it this morning.
lion, act now
The zookeeper told us the lion sleeps most of the day, but the moment it sees something it needs, it acts without a second's delay, which I wish I could learn for my work.
Write a doha about a lion who does not say he will hunt tomorrow but springs the instant he must, teaching people who delay everything that decisive action today beats a hundred stored-up intentions.
doha with a lion: lions dont wait til tomorrow, they act. i need that vibe
The lion does not whisper "tomorrow"; he leaps, and the hour is his. So rise, O drowsy heart.
paras, use it now
doha w the paras, u hold it today but dont use it, then its gone
My grandfather had a rare skill with herbs and said he'd teach me later, and he died before he did, so I treat every chance to learn as a paras I must grab today.
The paras of the alchemists lies in thy palm this hour; touch thy work to it now, for it fades with the morrow.

Write a doha about someone who discovers the legendary paras of the alchemists but says he will use its magic tomorrow, only to lose his chance, teaching us to use every treasure of time in the present.
A thousand "tomorrows" are only one idle sigh; one deed done now is a living thing.
I told my friend I'd help him move flats on Saturday and then on Sunday and finally he hired movers, and I realised my habit of putting everything off is hurting people.
do it today
doha pls on act now stop waiting, im trying to quit being lazy about my goals
Please write a couplet for the man who is always just about to begin, telling him that the time for beginning is not later but at this moment, for the deed must be started to bear anything at all.
churn, priest, today
The priest at our village used to churn the curd himself every dawn and told the boys that if the churn is left idle till tomorrow the butter is lost, so work today.
The priest churns on, the butter gathers; leave the churn idle till tomorrow and all the day's cream is lost.

Write a doha about a priest who sits idle beside the churn and says he will begin tomorrow, teaching that spiritual or worldly gains come only from today's effort and none from promises for another day.
doha w a priest and a churn - the work isn't done unless u start churning now
Write a doha in which a man finds the paras of the alchemists and plans to use it tomorrow, but the delay turns his fortune to dust, teaching that every chance must be seized this very day.
The paras gleams in thy hand, but only the hour that is now can work its alchemy.
doha pls, about the paras, when u have a chance use it today
My uncle found an offer that could have changed his career, a real paras, but he kept saying he'd reply after the holidays, and the offer went to someone else.
paras, seize today
The palace is built brick by brick today, never by the "tomorrow" of a dreamer's sigh.
doha w a palace in it, i keep planning my dream life but never start building it

Compose a doha about a prince who dreams of a great palace and says he will lay its foundation tomorrow, though each day he delays, the dream recedes, teaching that work begun today builds all greatness.
My cousin has drawn the plans for his dream palace of a startup for ten years, and last week a school friend with half his plan launched it, so I told him to begin today.
palace, begin today
Write a doha for a person who thinks of reconciling with an old friend but waits for the friend to call first, reminding them that pride is a delay and the right moment to reach out is today.
Let not pride keep the hour: the hand extended now is warmer than the hand extended too late.
doha about calling an old friend today instead of overthinking it
It was my best friend's birthday last month and I kept saying I'd call tomorrow because I felt awkward after our fight, and now it's been four years of silence.
call them today
The milk spoils by evening when left uncared for; do thy work this morning, for the day is short.
I left the milk out on the counter saying I'd put it away after the call, and by the evening it was sour, and my wife said that's you with every task, always after.
Write a doha in which the milk must be boiled the moment it is fresh or it spoils by night, teaching a procrastinating mind that all things need doing at the proper time, which is today.
milk spoils, act now
doha with milk in it, if u dont deal with it today it goes bad, like my tasks

Write a doha about a diamond lying untouched beside a grindstone because the owner says he'll cut and polish it tomorrow, teaching that unfinished work and wasted chances do not shine until begun now.
The diamond waits unpolished beside the grindstone's rest; a gem unworked today is a pebble tomorrow.
doha w a diamond and a grindstone, you gotta polish talent now, not someday
diamond, grindstone, today
My friend's daughter has a rare singing talent like an uncut diamond, and she keeps saying she will practise seriously after her exams, and the grindstone of daily work never starts.
Write a doha that says do not wait until the shroud and sandalwood are brought to make peace with those you have wronged or do the good you intended, because what is delayed may never be done.
I waited until the day of my uncle's funeral, with the sandalwood laid beside the shroud, to apologise for our fight, and it was too late, so now I say sorry the same day.
doha w a shroud and sandalwood in it - if u wanna say sorry do it now not at the end
sandalwood, shroud, forgive today
Do not wait for the shroud and the sandalwood to speak your tender word; say it while the ears can hear.
The swan leaves the market of delay at dawn, for the day is short and tomorrow's sellers are gone.
At the market I saw a swan-necked vase for sale and the buyer said he'd come back tomorrow, and a clever man took it, which is what happens whenever I put things off.
Write a doha where the swan departs the market early before the crowd arrives because he does his business at once, while the one who delays finds the best goods gone, teaching to act now.
doha w a swan and a market - the early swan gets the good stuff, so act today
swan, market, now
My father keeps saying he will see a specialist about his heart next month, but his cough has lasted since January, and I want to drag him to the clinic today.
doha about booking that appointment today, no more postponing
Compose a Kabir style doha saying the good intentions of tomorrow are only dreams, that today alone is real, and that those who act immediately are the only ones who get anything done in life.
no more delays
Of all the hours, the best is the one that is now; let thy hand not wait on the lazy "later".
I'd love a doha for a young man who sleeps till noon and idles the rest of the day, telling him that the hours of life are not given to be slept away and that work waits for no sluggard.
stop sleeping, start working
doha pls for my lazy brother who does nothing all day lol
O sleeper, the hours of the day slip through thy fingers while thou dreamest; wake and take up thy work.
My cousin has been jobless for two years, not because there are no jobs but because he cannot get up before one in the afternoon, and my aunt cries every evening about it.
The milk of the morning is wasted on the sleeper; the lazy sit with empty hands while the diligent are fed.
milk, lazy sleeper
doha w milk - the lazy guy sleeps in and misses the fresh milk, the early ones get it. thats me every day
Our milkman comes at five, and my lazy brother is never awake to take it, so every day my mother gets it and he complains there is nothing left for breakfast.
Write a doha about a man who sleeps away the whole morning while the fresh milk is taken by the early risers, teaching that laziness loses what diligence gains and the idle are left with nothing.
lazy days wasted

Please write a Kabir-style doha about those who eat and sleep their lives away and never do the real work they were meant to do, so that they reach the end of their days with nothing to show for them.
My father retired after thirty years with no hobby, no friends, no plans, and spends all day on the sofa half asleep, and I am afraid of becoming like him.
They eat, they sleep, they rise again to eat; the days go by like a pilgrim who never set out.
doha on wasting life sleeping and doing nothing, ive been in a rut for a year
doha w a tree and a forehead mark: the lazy guy puts on the mark and sleeps under the tree all day instead of working
The man at our village square wears the forehead mark of devotion but snores under the big tree all afternoon while his fields lie neglected, and the villagers shake their heads.
tree, forehead mark, idle
Write a doha about the idle man who wears the forehead mark of a pious person and sleeps all day under a tree, while his work remains undone, teaching that appearances do not excuse laziness.
He wears the mark upon his brow and sleeps beneath the tree; the work is never done, and the day is lost.
doha w a leaf and a priest: the priest lies lazily on a leaf bed doing nothing while others work. u know the type
Our priest says he's meditating, but I have seen him lying on a mat of leaves in the afternoon sleeping, while his wife carries all the water and does all the work.
leaf, priest, idle
I'd love a doha about a priest who rests lazily on a bed of leaves all day, calling it contemplation, while real work and real prayer go undone, teaching that idleness is no virtue.
The priest lies idle on his bed of leaves; the world goes on working, and the sleeper wakes to a day already gone.
Write a doha for my friend who has big dreams but never gets out of bed to chase them, telling him that dreams without work are nothing and the lazy man's plans never go beyond his sleep.
dreams need work
My nephew wants to be a famous musician but he hasn't practised for a month and just says he is waiting for inspiration, and his mother says inspiration doesn't come to people who stay in bed.
doha for someone who dreams big but never works
The sleeper's dreams are many and rich, and none of them comes true; only the worker's hand turns dream to deed.
doha w a door - lazy guy sees opportunity knocking at the door but is too lazy to get up and open it
door, lazy man
Opportunity knocks upon the door; the sluggard turns over in his sleep and the knocker goes away.
Write a doha about a lazy man who hears a knock on his door and does not rise to open it, so that the chance of a lifetime passes on, teaching that laziness shuts every door.
A recruiter came to my brother's door with a job offer, and he told his wife to say he was out because he didn't want to get dressed, and the offer went to the next flat.
doha w a needle: the lazy tailor wont even pick up the needle so the shirt stays torn, lazy ppl and small tasks
My uncle is too lazy to use a needle, so his shirt has had a torn pocket for two years, and he says it is not worth the trouble, though he complains about it daily.
The needle lies untouched, and the torn is left torn; the lazy hand is rich in excuses and poor in mending.
needle, lazy hands
Give me a doha about a lazy person who cannot be bothered to pick up a needle for the smallest mending, so that little problems grow large, teaching that laziness turns small repairs into great ruin.
The lazy man sits at the water well and sighs, yet will not draw the water; the ocean of the world offers him nothing.

Write a doha about the lazy man who sits idle beside the well and the ocean wishing for water, but will not lower a bucket, teaching that a man who does not work is thirsty even where there is plenty.
doha with a well and the ocean - lazy guy is beside plenty of water but too lazy to draw it
My neighbour lives by the sea with a well in his yard, and in summer he complains he has no water to bathe because he won't walk to fetch it, and his wife says the problem is laziness.
well, ocean, idle thirst
traveller, sand, rest

Write a doha about a traveller who lies down to rest in the sand and falls asleep, and so never reaches the destination, while the one who kept walking arrives, teaching that laziness makes one fall short of the goal.
doha w a traveller sleeping on the sand when he should keep going, thats me and my goals
On our trek my friend kept resting on the sand every ten minutes and finally slept an hour, a lazy traveller, and we reached the camp at midnight because of him.

The rainbird cries to the clouds as though its voice could bring the monsoon; sing the pride of a little song.
doha about a rainbird who thinks it summons the rain
Write a couplet for the king who surrounded himself with flatterers until he forgot that kings too are only people, and who believes all praise is simply the truth being told, never a favour paid.
When my grandfather's old business partner became wealthy, he stopped inviting us over and started inviting only those who flatter him.
The courtiers' praise is honey, and the king drinks until he can no longer tell his face from his name.
flattery, swollen head
doha on how praise goes to people's heads
He lifts his head so high that he never sees what lies beneath his own feet; sing his stumble.
doha about how pride always comes before a fall
A guy at work mocked the new intern for making errors, and the very next day he made the biggest one of the year in front of everyone.
pride, fall, folly
I want a doha that says the loudest boasters are often the first to fall, because they stop looking where they are walking and stop listening to the ones who might have warned them.
Our village headman sits under the old tree and boasts that the boat he has just bought is the finest, though he has never rowed one.
boat, tree, vanity
Write a doha about the man who sits under the shade of a tree and boasts of owning a boat, though he has never crossed the water, and who laughs at every real sailor who passes by.
doha about a guy bragging about his boat under a tree
Under a spreading tree he sails an imaginary boat, and calls himself captain of waters he fears.
The bee, drunk on its own honey, mistakes the philosopher's stone for a pebble; sing the pride that cannot see its fortune.
bee, philosopher's stone, pride
doha about a proud man who has a bee buzzing around his philosopher's stone and doesn't care
Compose a verse about the man who owns a philosopher's stone yet buzzes like a proud bee about his small honey, bragging about what he has made, never wondering what is truly priceless.
My neighbour has a talent that could change lives, but he swats everyone away like a bee and boasts of the philosopher's stone he thinks he found.
Compose a doha about the proud man who is dazzled by his own gold and thinks he floats above the world like a lotus, though his roots are in the same mud as everyone else.
He wears gold as a crown and thinks himself a lotus; yet the pond knows his roots are the same mud.
gold, lotus, proud
My rich cousin looks down on us with his heavy gold chain and calls himself above it all, as if he did not grow up in the same village.
doha on a gold-loving rich man who thinks he's a lotus above the mud

Compose a verse about the man who sits at his mirror each morning admiring his reflection and rehearsing speeches about his own greatness, who believes that if the world cannot see it, then the world must be blind.
Mirror, mirror, you flatter the one who stares too long; sing of the face that has forgotten the world.
My roommate checks his hair in every shiny surface and talks about how girls always notice him.
pls write about a vain guy and a mirror
mirror, vanity
leaf, forest, vain
doha about a leaf in the forest thinking it's the best of the leaves
One green leaf in the forest boasts of its shade, though the wind is already counting its days.
Write a verse about a single leaf in a vast forest that brags it is the greenest of all, forgetting the forest breathes through all its leaves together and that autumn will not ask its opinion.
My little niece thinks she is the greenest leaf in the whole family forest, and nobody can say otherwise.
Cut not the thread of any life, for what you sever your hand cannot mend.
My cousin laughed as she crushed a spider hanging on its thread, and I went quiet, wondering whether any life should be taken so lightly.
doha on not hurting small creatures, thread of life
Compose a doha about the fragile thread that holds every living creature to life, from the smallest insect to the largest beast, and about how one who respects it will never cause pain to any being.
thread of life, no harm
doha on an elephant and a bell, being gentle with big animals
The elephant walks to the sound of the bell, mighty yet gentle; strength that harms none is the truest.
Please write a doha about the elephant who carries great strength and yet never hurts a creature, and the bell that calls to prayer, showing that real devotion means harming no living being.
elephant, bell, no cruelty
I saw a mahout beat his elephant while the bell for evening prayer was ringing, and I thought what kind of prayer is that.
The heron stands in holy stillness yet waits to take a life; what is the use of piety that kills?
doha on heron and traveler, pretending to be holy while killing
A traveler I met on the road prayed loudly at every halt, but ate the flesh of every creature he could find, and I wondered about his devotion.
heron, traveler, no killing
Compose a doha about the heron who stands as if in prayer, waiting to seize a living creature, and the traveler who prays but kills, showing that holiness without mercy for life is only a pretence.
doha on moneylender who is kind to animals but cruel to people, arrow
moneylender, arrow, no harm

Write a doha about the hunter who shoots an arrow at an innocent deer and the moneylender who gives to the poor but ignores the creatures that suffer, showing that true mercy extends to all that breathe.
The arrow flies, the animal falls; the moneylender gives alms but spares not the weak creature.
A moneylender in our town feeds the poor but organises hunting trips with his friends, and I would like him to hear a verse about it.
do not kill animals
The life in you is the life in every creature; to harm another is to wound your own self.
My daughter refused to eat meat after she saw how the chicken was killed, and I was moved by her sensitivity.
doha on why ppl shouldnt eat meat
Please write a doha about how the same life breathes in all creatures, and how the person who knows this cannot bring himself to kill a living thing for his own appetite or pleasure.
Compose a doha about the cruelty of killing an innocent animal merely for the pleasure of eating, and how the one who does so carries the pain of that creature into his own future.
At the festival they slaughtered a goat in front of everybody, and the way it looked at us stayed in my mind for weeks.
doha on animal sacrifice being wrong
Whose cry goes unheard when the innocent is led to sacrifice? Remember it is a life, as yours is.
mercy to animals
The net is cast and the innocent are caught; what pleasure has he who takes life for sport?
net, cruelty to creatures
Write a doha about the hunter's net which traps small birds and animals that have done no harm, and about how the one who weaves it traps his own soul in the cycle of cruelty and suffering.
doha on traps and nets cruelty
Some men in our area set a net for birds to sell and eat them, and I could not sleep after seeing the helpless creatures struggling.
My grandfather never harmed even an ant and used to carry insects out of the room gently, and I try to follow his example.
harm no creature
He who spares the smallest life is greater than he who conquers a thousand lands.
doha on compassion to insects

Please write a doha about how the person who is careful not to harm even the smallest of creatures has learnt the deepest lesson of religion, and about how his gentleness blesses all who live near him.
The moneylender sold seeds to farmers and then insisted on killing every bird that ate them, and I wished for a verse about leaving them in peace.
doha on seeds and birds, share with creatures
Sow your seed for all who hunger, bird and beast alike; the harvest of mercy is richest.

Write a doha about how a farmer who sows his seed should leave a share for the birds and the animals that also need to eat, rather than killing them, since all living things have a claim on the harvest.
seed, moneylender, no harm
swan, door, gentleness
doha on a swan at the door, never hurt a guest creature
The swan comes to the door of the kind and leaves unharmed; peace is the shelter of the gentle.
A swan wandered up to our door one evening, and my father shooed away the neighbour's boys who wanted to throw things at it.
Compose a doha about the swan that comes to a stranger's door seeking shelter, and about how the person who protects rather than harms it has shown the very meaning of kindness to all life.
The parrot held captive and the fly on the wall each hold a life as dear as yours; spare them.
doha on a parrot and a fly, all lives matter
Please write a doha about the parrot kept for amusement and the fly swatted in annoyance, to remind us that each life holds the same fear of death as our own, and no creature is too small for mercy.
My brother keeps a parrot and swats every fly without a thought, and I told him all lives are as precious to themselves as his is to him.
parrot, fly, spare them
doha on not eating meat, been vegetarian for a year
I stopped eating meat after I visited a farm and heard the animals cry, and now I eat in peace.
Write a doha about the person who gives up eating flesh out of pity for the animals, and about how his table becomes a place of peace where no creature has suffered for his pleasure.
no flesh, no cruelty
Where no creature cried for the meal, the meal itself is blessed.
doha on a lion and a thread: even a king of beasts should be gentle
lion, thread, mercy
Compose a doha about how even the lion, king of beasts, could hold his claws if he realised that life hangs by a thread for every creature, and about how humans, who can reason, should do much more.
A lion at the zoo paced in his small space, and I realised that all life hangs by a thread and that even a lion deserves freedom.
The lion's claws could spare, the thread of life is thin; teach, O Lord, the mighty to be gentle.
The inn near the old bus stand serves roasted meat to travellers, and I felt sick thinking of the ashes of those who died and the ashes of the animals killed.
inn, ash, no killing
Write a doha about the inn that serves the flesh of slaughtered animals to its guests, and about the ash that is the end of both man and beast, showing that all life returns to the same dust.
doha on inn serving meat, ash is the end for everyone
Both man and beast end as ash; why then, O host, do you serve one to the other?

Compose a doha about the crow who steals and the thief who steals, and the man who kills the crow in anger, showing that violence answers nothing and hurting a creature for a petty fault is the greater wrong.
doha on killing a crow for stealing, just wrong
A thief stole from our neighbour and the crowd beat him half to death, and the same people threw sticks at the crows that came, and it was dreadful to watch.
crow, thief, no violence
The crow takes a crumb and is stoned; the thief takes a purse and is beaten; where is mercy in any of this?
doha on being gentle toward every living thing
My child asked why we shouldn't step on ants, and I tried to explain that every creature has its own small life.
Walk gently on the earth, for beneath your feet are lives as dear to themselves as yours.

Please write a doha about the gentle person who walks the earth without trampling the small, speaks without wounding the weak and eats without taking life, showing that such a life is a continuous prayer.
no harm, no cruelty
stop animal cruelty
doha on people who beat their animals
The blows you give your servant beast return in kind; every blow is a debt unpaid.
My neighbour whips his bullock daily to make it pull a heavier load, and it breaks my heart to watch.
Compose a doha about the carter who beats the oxen that pull his load and calls it work, showing that cruelty to a voiceless creature is a sin that follows the doer through the years.
Compose a doha about sandalwood, which perfumes even the axe that cuts it and harms no creature, and about how the gentle person too gives fragrance to the world by refusing to harm any living being.
sandalwood, no harm
Sandalwood harms none, perfumes all; let me too live and leave a fragrance of mercy.
My uncle spent his life carrying injured animals to the shelter and his gentle ways were as fragrant as sandalwood for everyone.
doha on being gentle like sandalwood, hurting none
When the helpless are slaughtered, the Lord weeps; those who feast upon their flesh eat the tears of mercy.
At my cousin's wedding, a dozen goats were killed for the feast, and the bleating still echoes in my mind.

Please write a doha about the guilt of those who feast upon animals killed for their pleasure, and about how food obtained without cruelty is the only food that nourishes both the body and the spirit.
doha on killing animals for feasts
no blood on our plate
cage, free the birds
The cage may be gilded, yet the captive sings only of the sky; set him free, and be free yourself.
Write a doha about how every creature kept in a cage for the entertainment of others pines for the open sky, and how one who sets it free earns a blessing greater than any pilgrimage.
doha on freeing caged animals
I bought a caged bird at the fair just to set it free, and its first flight made me happier than I've been in months.
Compose a doha about the bitter gourd that hurts no creature and the rainbird that thirsts for rain, to teach that simple, bloodless food and a gentle nature make for a life that harms no one.
doha on bitter gourd diet and rainbird, living without harm
The rainbird drinks only clean rain and the bitter gourd harms no life; let simple food keep us gentle.
bitter gourd, rainbird, mercy
My grandmother grows bitter gourd and eats only what grows from the earth, and the rainbird that visits her garden is never driven away.
The lotus pond had a fisherman who netted every creature in it, and the pond, once alive with fish and flowers, was soon empty.
The lotus blooms where the fish may swim in peace; a pond emptied by cruelty bears no flowers.
doha on lotus and fish, killing fish ruins the pond
lotus, fish, spare them
Write a doha about the lotus pond where fish swim without fear and the fisherman who empties it with his traps, showing that the one who destroys life destroys also the beauty and peace around him.
Compose a doha about how a snake, though feared and driven away, takes life only when it is in danger, whereas man kills for pleasure and appetite, and the wise know which is the greater danger.
We found a snake in the courtyard and my father moved it gently away with a stick instead of killing it, saying it has as much right to live as we do.
snake, spare the creature
The snake bites in fear but man kills for pleasure; judge, O Lord, which is the cruel one.
doha on not killing snakes
The traveler who kills for his meal on the road has eaten his journey's reward; spare the life and gain the road.
A traveler stopped at our village, killed a hen for his supper, and I asked him how a person who walks the road to God can stain his hands with blood.
Please write a doha about the traveler who kills along the way for his meal, and how the weight of every life taken adds to the burden he must carry to the end of his journey.
doha for a traveler who eats meat on pilgrimage
traveler, spare the life
Compose a doha about the physician who heals the sick but kills animals to prepare medicines, and how the thread of one life cannot be cut to lengthen another, for all are bound by mercy.
The physician cuts a thread of life to mend another; is that healing, or only the shifting of pain?
The physician my family goes to makes medicines from the bodies of animals, and I've been wondering whether a cure that costs another life is any cure at all.
physician, thread, no killing
doha on animal-based medicine, no harm
doha on weaver's loom and silk, silkworms get killed
The silk weaver at his loom told me proudly how many worms are killed in making each saree, and I was horrified by the cost of beauty.
Please write a doha about the weaver whose loom makes beautiful cloth at the price of countless tiny lives, and about how true beauty is that which is woven without cruelty to any living being.
The loom weaves beauty, but if a life is the price, the beauty is a burden on the weaver's soul.
loom, silk, no cruelty
The net that takes the life of the free is woven of sin; cast it away and weave kindness instead.
Compose a doha about the net spread by the hunter to capture innocent creatures, and about how his trap is first of all a trap for his own soul, which cannot escape the consequence of its deeds.
doha on hunters setting nets
Poachers set nets in the wetlands near our village, catching all kinds of birds, and a friend and I broke them open at night.
net, spare the innocent
doha on a mountain, a mullah, not hurting animals for festival
From the mountain the cleric's call goes out; may it carry mercy to the creatures that suffer on festival day.
On the festival day, the cleric near our mountain village preached against killing animals unnecessarily, and many in the congregation listened.
Compose a doha about the cleric who tells his people from the mountain slope that sacrificing animals does not please God, because the Merciful One cherishes every living creature he has made.
mountain, cleric, no sacrifice

Please write a doha about the one-string lute whose single note stays in tune with all living things, and how the one who plays it with a gentle heart will never hurt another creature even in thought, word or deed.
My music teacher plays the one-string lute and will not even swat a mosquito, saying the same breath is in all.
doha on gentle musician who doesn't hurt anything
lute, gentle to all
One string, one note, one breath in all that lives; let not my hand silence another's song.

Compose a doha about the elephant, who is hunted for his tusks and chained for display, and about the cruelty of man who destroys such a noble being, showing that mercy is the sign of true strength and nobility.
elephant, hurt not
doha on being kind to elephants
The elephant in chains remembers the open land; free him, and you will be freed from your own cruelty.
I saw a chained elephant at a fair, swaying in distress, and I wished I could say something to all who passed it by.
doha on a tilak wearing man who eats meat and still calls himself holy
Please write a doha about the man with a sacred forehead mark who churns butter at dawn but eats meat at night, showing that religion lies in mercy toward all living beings, not in marks and rituals.
The mark on the brow, the churn at dawn, but blood on the plate by night; is that devotion?
forehead mark, churn, mercy
My uncle wears a big tilak and churns butter every morning but cannot go a day without meat, and I have long wondered how he squares it.
The peacock that wandered around our colony was hunted by some boys for the cremation ground feast, and I stopped them, shaking with anger.
doha on peacock killed for food, shamshan feast
peacock, cremation ground, spare life

Compose a doha about the peacock whose beauty delights all and who is hunted for a feast, and about the cremation ground where all feasts end, showing how foolish it is to take a life that cannot be restored.
The peacock dances in the rain and is hunted for the feast, yet the cremation ground awaits both hunter and prey.
Sandalwood gives fragrance to the axe, yet the sword takes lives for sport; which is the nobler path?
My grandfather, once a soldier, laid down his sword after the war and spent his later years planting sandalwood and saving injured animals.

Write a doha about the sword that takes life and the sandalwood that perfumes even the axe, to remind us that the noblest warrior is the one who puts down his weapon and uses his strength to protect the weak.
sword, sandalwood, mercy
doha on sandalwood and sword, peace beats war
Compose a doha about the elephant, gentle giant of the wild, and the swan who glides through the water harming none, showing how the strongest and most beautiful of beings live in peace with all.
The elephant and the swan harm none and are loved by all; such is the nobility of the gentle.
doha on elephant and swan being peaceful
elephant, swan, gentle ones
A swan and an elephant share the water at the sanctuary I visit, and I am always moved at how peacefully they coexist.

Please write a doha about the person who cannot bear to see any creature suffer, who will not take the life of even the smallest being, and who finds in that tenderness the heart of religion and peace.
I felt sick watching how the animals were treated at the slaughterhouse I passed on my way to work, and I have not eaten meat since.
doha on not eating animals, saw a slaughterhouse
hurt no living being
The one who feels the pain of the smallest creature has felt the pain of God.
The temple authorities in our town sacrifice a goat every year at the festival and say it pleases the deity, and I find it very hard to accept.
Write a doha showing that the Lord who lives in the temple cannot be pleased by the blood of an innocent animal, since He created and loves every creature, and true worship is gentleness toward all.
temple, no sacrifice
doha on animal sacrifice at the temple
The Lord who made the goat is not pleased by its blood; bring Him a heart that harms none.
doha on how an arrow hurts every living thing, hunting is cruel
arrow, mercy
Please write a doha about the arrow that flies from the hunter's bow and pierces an innocent creature without cause, and how the wounds it makes in the animal also wound the soul of the shooter.
My neighbour proudly hangs the heads of deer he shot with his bow on his wall, and every time I visit I feel uneasy.
The arrow wounds the deer, and the wound returns to the hunter's own heart.
doha on a thorn in the paw of an animal, helping not hurting
Compose a doha about the thorn that pierces the foot of a creature in the wild and the kind person who removes it gently, showing that a heart which feels the pain of another can never harm him.
The thorn that pricks the beast's foot pricks the heart of the kind; so dear is the creature to the tender.
I found a stray dog limping with a thorn in its paw and gently pulled it out, and the dog licked my hand, and I knew right then why I never wished to hurt any animal.
thorn, help the creature
From the boat I saw fishermen throwing back the small catches to die on the shore, and I felt sad for the dying creatures.
boat, no killing
Write a doha about the boat that sails across the water carrying traps, and the people on it who destroy the life of the waters for profit, showing that a seeker must cross life without harming it.
The boat crosses the water and leaves no wound; so should the seeker cross life, harming none.
doha on boat voyage harming no life

Compose a doha about the tortoise, which is hunted for its shell and sacrificed in temples, and about the temple that has forgotten mercy, showing that the place of worship is empty when cruelty is permitted inside.
The tortoise bears its shell upon its back, yet is slain at the temple; what god delights in such offerings?
At the temple near my aunt's village, a tortoise was killed as an offering, and the horrified child in me still cries about it.
doha on tortoise and temple, no sacrifice of animals
tortoise, temple, spare life
The priest preaches mercy in the morning and feasts on flesh at night; what is the worth of such a sermon?
The priest in our community gives talks about non-violence in the morning, but I saw him at a feast eating meat, and I lost faith.
doha on priest who preaches ahimsa but eats meat
priest, hypocrisy, no killing
Compose a doha about the priest who tells others to be kind to all creatures but eats the flesh of slaughtered animals himself, showing that true teaching must be lived, and not merely spoken aloud.

Please write a doha about the thief who steals a life from an innocent animal, and the one who steals goods from a neighbour, saying both are robbers, and the river of mercy cleanses neither until they repent.
The thief who broke into our shed was chased off, yet the same crowd killed a stray dog by the river that was only hungry and posed no harm.
doha on killing a hungry dog by the river, cruelty to creatures
thief, river, spare life
The thief of goods is hunted, the thief of lives goes free; the river of mercy asks for justice for both.
Every life holds the same breath as yours; to take it lightly is to scorn the Giver of breath.
respect all life

Write a doha about the breath that moves in every living being, which the wise recognise as the same in all, so that they cannot bring themselves to cause pain to another any more than they would to themselves.
doha on respecting all forms of life
After I watched my child hold a dying bird with such tenderness, I understood what it means to honour a life.
I tied a thread around a stray kitten's neck to lead it along, and my teacher told me that even gentle threads can hurt a creature that wants to run free.
The thread that binds a free creature binds also its keeper; let go, and you both shall breathe.

Compose a doha about the thread that ties a wild creature against its will, and how the person who respects the freedom of every living thing lets it go and finds the thread on his own heart loosening too.
doha on not tying up animals
thread, set them free
Write a doha about the date palm which gives sweet fruit and shade to all without killing anything, as an example of the gentle life that takes nothing from any creature and gives much to every one.
My grandmother lives off the dates and grains of her small land, never touching meat, and her life has been the gentlest I know.
The date palm gives its sweetness without taking a life; blessed is the table that is spread this way.
date palm, gentle food
doha on plant-based food and date palm, no killing
Compose a doha about how violence in word, thought or deed always returns to its source, and the person who has made peace with all living beings sleeps soundly, eats gently and dies without fear.
He who harms none fears none; his sleep is sweet and his death is gentle.
After I gave up hunting, a strange peace came over me, and I sleep better than I have in years.
doha on peace that comes from not harming anyone
harm none, fear none
doha on moth dying near a bulb, saving insects
Every night I carry out the moths that circle the glare so that they do not die in it, and my family teases me but I feel good.
Please write a doha about the moth that circles the glare and dies, and about how the compassionate person protects such little lives, knowing that no being is too small to be loved by the Creator.
The moth flies to the glare and dies, and the kind hand lifts it away; blessed is the hand.
moth, spare small lives
fish, water pot, spare life
doha on a fish in a water pot, set it free
Write a doha about the fish kept in a pot of water for display, which longs for open water, and how the kind person lets it go and frees himself from the guilt of keeping a free being captive.
The fish in the pot of water dreams of the open stream; set it free, and free your own soul.
My kids kept a fish in a pot of water in the kitchen, and when I explained how it suffers, they carried it to the stream and let it swim away.
The fly on the wall and the snake in the grass alike dread death; where is your mercy for them?
fly, snake, harm none
My mother never kills a fly or a snake that wanders into the courtyard, only gently shoos it away, and I try to do the same.
Compose a doha about the fly and the snake, creatures that are most often killed in fear or disgust, and how the person who has learnt gentleness spares them and lets them go on their way.
doha on not killing flies and snakes
The fish vendors near the harbour was full of dying creatures gasping for air, and as I walked past I felt I should say something.
fish, spare them
Please write a doha about the fish gasping for air on the vendor's table, and how the one who sees its struggle and turns away from eating it has learnt the most important lesson of compassion.
doha on fish gasping on the table, pity them
The fish gasps on dry land as you would gasp in water; feel its pain, and spare it.
speechless joy, date palm
The date palm gives its sweetness to the mouth that cannot speak of it; such is the joy the soul has tasted.
Eating a date from the palm in the quiet evening, I felt a joy so sweet and deep that I could not say a word about it to anyone; please write a doha about a delight that cannot be told.
doha with a date palm about a joy too sweet to describe
My grandfather ate the first date of the season under his date palm and just closed his eyes and smiled, unable to tell us how good it was.
doha with a forest and a diamond, a joy beyond words
forest, diamond, speechless
We hiked into the forest and my daughter found a tiny sparkling diamond-like pebble in the path and her face just lit up without a word.
In the forest I found a diamond and a joy that has no words; the voice is still and the heart is sweet.

Walking in the forest at dawn I found a diamond-bright drop of morning water and my heart filled with a gladness I could not name, one that no teacher had prepared me for; write a doha about this wordless joy.
The spinning wheel hums, the cloth sheet grows, and the weaver has a joy he cannot give a name to.
After weeks at her spinning wheel my mother finally finished a cloth sheet and sat with it in her lap, smiling silently.
At my spinning wheel I wove a cloth sheet and felt such a quiet gladness that I forgot to speak for hours, and so I ask for a doha on the sweetness of an inner joy that words cannot catch.
doha with a spinning wheel and a cloth sheet, speechless inner joy
spinning wheel, cloth sheet, joy
doha about a yogi who tasted a joy he could not describe
When the yogi came out of his long meditation he said nothing for hours, only smiling, because the sweetness he had tasted had no words, and I want a doha for that kind of silent joy.
An old yogi came down from the cave and sat smiling for a whole day, and when we asked what he had found he could only laugh.
The yogi tasted what the voice cannot tell, and his silence was the sweetest speech of all.
the yogi's silent joy
too sweet to tell
There is a joy so sweet that when I try to speak of it my words fail, and I can only smile; can you write a doha that captures the wordless sweetness of a joy once tasted?
After the meditation retreat I could not explain to my friends what I felt, I just kept smiling like I had a secret.
He who has tasted cannot say, and he who can say has not tasted; so the joyful keep silent.
doha: a joy so sweet no words can tell it
doha: the joy I tasted cannot be told, I can only smile
unspeakable joy
Ask him how it tasted, and he only smiles; the joy is true but the voice cannot carry it.
Tell me in a doha how a person who has once tasted a deep inner joy can only smile when asked about it, unable to explain, like a mute person who has tasted something delicious.
When I came back from the pilgrimage everyone asked me how it was and all I could do was smile and shake my head.
After years of struggle I felt, just for one evening, a perfect quiet happiness that I have never been able to describe to anyone.
Oh the sweetness of it, I have no words, only a quiet joy that fills me from within and makes everything else seem small; please write a doha for the one who has tasted it and cannot tell.
joy beyond telling
chat style doha about a joy so sweet that you cant explain it
What I tasted I cannot tell; my joy is a secret that even I have no words for.
My physician found nothing wrong with me, but at the crossroads on my way home I felt a joy so large that I stopped and laughed out loud.
doha with a physician and a crossroads, a joy too sweet for words
The physician told me to rest, but at the crossroads I felt such a sudden sweetness of joy that I stood speechless, healed in a way that no medicine could do; write a doha about it.
The physician has no cure for this sweet disease; at the crossroads I tasted a joy I cannot tell.
physician, crossroads, joy
In the boat with a bitter gourd on my plate I tasted sweetness, and the voice was silent.
boat, bitter gourd, joy
doha with a boat and a bitter gourd, a joy without a reason
On a small boat the cook served bitter gourd and my father, who hates it, just smiled the whole time without saying why.

doha about the same soul in an elephant and a bee
elephant, bee, same soul
I watched an elephant and a bee in the garden and had a quiet feeling that the same unborn one looked out of both their eyes.
My friend's son was pronounced gone yet his mother insisted that something of him was still entirely unharmed, and I could not tell her she was wrong.
never dies, never born
Please compose a doha for the one who asks whether anything in a person truly survives, telling him that the self is neither born nor destroyed and that only its appearances come and go.
doha about the part of us that doesn't die

prayer beads, inn, wayfarer

doha on prayer beads, an inn, and who I really am
Write a doha on the Self that is not the prayer beads nor the inn where it spent a night, the Self that was before both, that remains after both, and is never the thing it touches.

The tortoise folds into its shell, and who can say what lives within; so the Self lives within and is not the shell.
tortoise, hidden Self

Write a verse on the tortoise that draws in its limbs and shows no sign of life, and on the Self within us that draws itself inward and is found unchanged, unborn, and undisturbed by the world outside.
doha about a tortoise and the true self
My grandmother, slow as a tortoise in her last year, kept insisting she was the same inside as she was at twenty.
doha on the self as what a touchstone can't change
touchstone, true self
Rub me on the touchstone of sorrow, and what shows is not me but the colour of the world; I remain.
Every test life gave me, from exams to heartbreaks, I faced with the sense that my real self was like a pure thing rubbed on a touchstone, always passing.
Write a doha about the Self, which is like pure metal that the touchstone rubs without leaving any mark, unalterable, unbreakable, and always itself no matter how it is tested by life.
doha on the temple with the true self inside us
temple, the real dweller
Write a verse about the temple of this life where the dweller within has never been created, never carved, and never installed, for the Self is unborn and always there.
Inside the old temple I felt that the quiet in me was older than every carving in the place and would outlast them all.
Stones are carved for the temple and the god is said to dwell there, but the dweller was never built and never brought in.
A diamond may be locked in a vault, a door may be barred, but the Self is never behind any door.
door, diamond, deathless self
Compose a verse about the Self within that cannot be shut behind a door and that is more precious than any diamond, because it is beyond price, beyond loss, and has no beginning.
Every time I locked my diamond ring in the drawer I realized how little the things I protect resemble the one who protects them.
the soul is the door and the diamond, can i get a doha about it
Write a verse on the peacock dancing in its brilliant colours and the seed asleep in the soil, both carrying the same deathless Self which does not begin with the form and does not end with it.
peacock, seed, one Self
doha about the peacock and the seed and what stays
The peacock dances in the monsoon, yet the dancer within the dance is unborn, and every seed holds that same dancer.
I watched a peacock dance in the field where my father had planted a single seed, and I felt the same invisible presence in both of them.
Seeing a forgotten cloth sheet at the crossroads, I thought the one who wore it, and indeed every one of us, is more than any covering.
At the crossroads, a cloth sheet lies in the dust; the wearer has moved on, unharmed.
crossroads, cloth sheet, soul

Write a doha about the cloth sheet spread at the crossroads that the Self has no need of, since the Self was never cold, never covered, and never born, and does not need protection from anything at all.
doha on crossroads and a cloth sheet but about the soul
needle, the unpierced Self
When the doctor's needle went into my arm I strangely felt that whoever was feeling it was not harmed at all.
doha on the soul and the needle
A needle may pierce the cloth but never the one who wears it; the Self cannot be wounded.
Compose a doha about the Self which no needle can pierce, no knot can bind, and no craft can mend, for it is whole in itself and has never been torn or sewn.
doha on the soul that doesn't come or go
My friend said at his father's funeral that his father was not gone, he simply was not in sight, and I found myself believing him.
Write a verse about the Self which never arrives and never departs, which remains where it always was while forms come and go around it.
no birth, no death
Not born in the dark, not buried in the day, the quiet one within is neither coming nor going.
I saw a crow pecking near the old man's shroud and felt, sharply, that the person we all knew had never been in that thing.
shroud, crow, what lives on
doha about the soul when the shroud and the crow come
Write a doha about the shroud and the crow that wait at the end of every body, and the quiet Self that has already left both behind, never to be touched by cloth or by claw.
The shroud is wound around the form and the crow waits near; but the one who lived in it is far beyond.

Deeper than thought, older than memory, the watcher sits awake while the whole dream passes by.
whats the thing in me that watches my thoughts? doha
the inner witness
Write me a verse about the silent presence that watches every thought, every emotion, and every day pass, which is never itself a thought, an emotion, or a day but the one who is aware of all.
Waves rise and fall, the ocean stays; so lives the Self beneath the rise and fall of lives.

ocean, the endless Self

doha: soul is like the ocean, never ending

doha about the river that is the soul, flowing on

river, ever-flowing Self

Write a verse on the arrow that hurts the form and the cuckoo that sings from it, with the unborn Self beyond both, untouched by the arrow's wound and the cuckoo's song alike.
doha on the arrow and the cuckoo and the soul
arrow, cuckoo, one Self

swan, oil press, pure Self

ageless, unborn
At my grandmother's ninetieth birthday she laughed like a girl and said that inside she was still exactly sixteen and always had been.
who is it that never grows old in me? doha

untouched by joy, sorrow

Beyond the pairs of joy and sorrow, beyond the gain and loss, lives one who was never touched by either.
doha on the self that isn't moved by joy or pain

doha on a lock and a fly, but about the soul

Locked in a waiting room for hours with a fly buzzing, I felt a freedom in me that no lock could ever have kept.
No lock holds the one who is everywhere, and the fly that buzzes at the window is not even noticed by the sky within.
lock, fly, the free Self
soul vs ego, who am i, doha pls
In the middle of my busiest week, I paused and wondered about who was actually doing all these things, and for a moment I felt perfectly empty and perfectly full.
Not the doer but the ground of doing, not the sound but the silence from which all sound arises, and to which it returns.
the ground of being
Write a doha about the soul as the one who is not the thinker of thoughts, nor the doer of deeds, nor the sufferer of pains, but the ground on which all of those appear and disappear.

One Self in a thousand faces, one breath in a thousand lives, one dreamer in a thousand dreams.

one Self in all
something about the soul being the same in everyone

indestructible Self

doha on the soul that nothing can destroy

seed, the unborn

doha on the self being free of any rope
rope, the unbound Self

doha with prayer beads about being born again and again

doha with a fish and a stone about being reborn again and again

lion, many births

well, sandalwood, rebirth

doha with a well and sandalwood about births and deaths repeating

doha with dew about being born again and again

doha with a cuckoo and a rainbird about coming back again and again

house, yogi, rebirth

doha about the endless cycle of birth and death, we should use this life
cycle of births

many lives, one chance
doha about coming back again and again and this being our chance to stop

doha about birth and death repeating over and over

doha with a potter and clay about being born again and again

potter and clay, rebirths

doha with milk and a diamond, born again and again until we are free

Write a doha in which a beggar and a musk deer both wander through life after life in search of what they carry within, and in this rare human birth one of them may finally turn inward and be free

ash, prayer beads, rebirth

Write a doha where the washerman washes cloth by the water again and again while the bell rings the hours, as the soul is washed in countless births until it is clean enough to stay free
Write a doha about a water well from which the same water is drawn and spilled over and over, as the soul is born and dies in an unbroken round, and the rare human birth that can break it
well, endless births

thorn, rebirths
doha with a thorn about coming back again and again until it's pulled out

doha with a physician about births and deaths again and again
physician, endless rebirths

doha about not wasting this human birth or we come back again

doha about being born again and again and how to stop

births without end

yogi, one-string lute, rebirth

shroud, blind man, rebirths
