doha about being born again and again, do your best in this life
many lives, one chance
Please write a doha in which the soul arrives and departs in life after life like a tired guest, and say that the human body is the rare chance to do the work that ends the repeated returning
After my grandmother's death I dreamed she told me that she is glad to have had one more human life, and that I should not waste mine; I want a doha for the dream
philosopher's stone, milk, rebirths
Write a doha in which milk turns to curd to butter through many changes, as the soul passes through many births, and the philosopher's stone of the human body is the last step to freedom
doha with a philosopher's stone and milk, being born again and again
My uncle kept a philosopher's stone legend and a jug of milk by his bed, and said that a soul too is made again and again, like milk made into curd, before it is ready
Milk becomes curd, curd becomes butter, and the soul becomes the human, who alone can find the philosopher's stone
The palace in our town changes owners every generation, and an old man there said that souls also move from body to body like that, and that this one body is our best chance
palace, endless births
The soul occupies a palace for a lifetime and leaves it empty, and moves to a new one, until it finds the home that does not change
Write a doha in which a soul moves from one palace-like body to another, life after life, and finally, in the human birth, learns that the only home worth seeking is the one that never needs leaving
doha with a palace about coming back again and again
My cousin is expecting and the whole family says our grandfather has come back, and I wonder what each soul is doing here and how many times it has done this before
Please write a doha that tells how each soul returns to the world after death, how birth and death keep turning, and how the rare human body should be used for freedom and not wasted
One is carried out and another carried in, and the great turning of births goes on without a pause
doha about how we keep coming back after dying
births and deaths
river, birth after birth
doha with a river about being born again and again
The river returns as rain and the rain returns as river, and the soul returns as body, until it learns the way home
Write a doha in which a river flows to the sea and rises again as rain, again and again, as the soul passes through birth after birth, and the human body is the one chance to stop the circle
We scattered my father's ashes in the river and my aunt said he will come back, and I thought about how many times we each have been through the river
When my daughter was born I felt that I was meeting someone I had known for many lives, and I want a doha to remind us both to make this life count

Please write a doha that says the soul has circled in birth and death countless times and has been wasted in each, and this human life is the rare chance, so let the reader seek truth before it is lost
rare human birth
The soul has travelled through a million forms to reach the shore of the human, and standing there it may either sleep or cross
doha about not wasting this human birth, we dont get another
doha with a grindstone and a mirror, about births and deaths going round
grindstone, mirror, rebirths
The grindstone turns and the mirror reflects the turning, and the soul sees in the human glass that it has been round before
Write a doha in which the grindstone keeps turning and the mirror shows the face of one who has been born many times, and say that this human birth is the chance to stop grinding the same grain again
I looked in my grandmother's mirror next to the grindstone and she said I looked just like someone from her previous life; I want a doha about coming back and not wasting this chance
doha with a tree and a winnowing fan about being born again and again
tree, winnowing fan, rebirths
The tree sheds and regrows, the winnowing fan sifts and returns, and the soul is sifted through birth after birth until it is light enough to rise
Please write a doha in which a tree drops its leaves and grows them again, while the winnowing fan separates the grain, as the soul is sifted through many births until this human life can free it
My grandfather sat under the tree each autumn with the winnowing fan and said that we are winnowed again and again until the chaff of desire is gone; I want a doha for him
palanquin, rebirth cycle
The palanquin carries a bride in one life and a corpse in another, and the soul inside never stays in either
My aunt was carried in a palanquin at her wedding and her last journey was in a different kind of carriage, and I felt the cycle is much shorter than we think
doha with a palanquin about being born again and again
Write a doha in which a palanquin carries a bride in one life and a body in another, as the soul changes its form again and again, until in the human birth it chooses to walk out of the procession
The dew is born at dawn and gathered in a net of spider silk, and the soul is caught in the net of birth and rises, only to fall again
dew, net, rebirths
doha with dew and a net about being born again and again
Please write a doha in which the dew is trapped in a net and falls and forms again each morning, as the soul is caught in the net of births, and this human life is the chance to cut it
I watched the dew on a spider's net this morning and thought how each drop will fall and form again, and how this life is the one in which to break the net
A skeleton was found under a tree, and the old man said it has been round before; make a doha about the return of souls and not wasting this life
The tree stands over the skeleton and the skeleton lies under the tree, and the soul between them passes through both again
skeleton, tree, rebirths
Write a doha in which a tree grows from the place where a skeleton lies, and that skeleton once belonged to a soul that has been born many times, and may be freed in the human body
doha with a skeleton and a tree, about being born again and again
many lives, one chance
The round of endless births turns slowly, and the human life is a pause in which the soul may step off
My father's death and my son's birth came in the same winter, and I couldn't help thinking that all of us are going around in some great circle
doha about the circle of birth and death and using this life right
Please write a doha in the voice of Kabir that says the circle of births has no beginning and has no end for the heedless, but the person with a human body who seeks the truth can step out
Write a doha where the tongue repeats the sorrows of countless births and the soul cries out in its many bodies, and say that this human birth is the chance to speak the Name that ends the returning
tongue, rebirths
The tongue has tasted a thousand births and called for a thousand mothers, and only the human tongue can call the Name
My grandmother says her tongue has said the Name in many lives and she hopes this one is the last; she repeats it with every breath
doha with a tongue about births and deaths coming again and again
Write a doha in which a potter and clay shape a pot that breaks and is reshaped many times, like the soul taking body after body, until this human form is the pot that holds the nectar
doha with a potter and clay about birth and death going round
At the potter and clay shop in our lane the same clay gets used for new pots over and over, and my grandfather said we are like that; I want a doha for him
potter and clay, rebirths
The potter and clay make a thousand shapes from one lump, and the soul too has been a thousand vessels
The thief of desire steals the soul back to the world each time it nearly escapes, and so it returns birth after birth
doha with a thief about being born again and again
thief, rebirths
A thief took my neighbour's savings on the day his grandson was born, and the old man laughed and said that it's a thief who brings us back each time too, the thief of desire
Write a doha in which the thief called desire steals the soul back into a new womb each time it nears release, and say that in this human birth the soul must catch the thief
doha about people shouting their prayers on loudspeakers like God is deaf
Why climb up and shout the call to prayer at the top of your voice, as though the Lord were deaf and could not hear the whisper of a sincere heart in the dark?
shouting at a deaf God
Every dawn the loudspeaker at the end of our lane wakes the whole colony, and my newborn cries. I keep thinking God surely hears quieter things. Doha?
Is the Beloved so hard of hearing that He needs a thundering voice to find you?

Write about those who chant at the top of their voices beside the cremation ground, waking the dead with their noise, as if the Lord were deaf, while a cloth sheet covers the silent one who now hears only silence.
At the cremation ground near us, a group chanted so loudly that people walking past covered their ears, and a cloth sheet over the body lay perfectly still. Doha on that?
doha: cremation ground, cloth sheet, shouting prayers
cremation ground, cloth sheet, shouting
The cloth sheet lies silent on the cremation ground, but the living shout as if the Lord were farther than the grave.
The sun rises in silence and the pearl forms in silence, yet man shouts to the heavens as though the Lord were deaf.
sun, pearl, shouting prayer
A doha about the quiet sun rising and the quiet pearl growing in the oyster, both done without a sound, while we scream our prayers and call it devotion, as though the Lord could not hear silence.
doha: the sun rises quietly and pearls grow quietly but people pray with loudspeakers
I woke at sunrise to the sound of loudspeakers while wearing my mother's pearl earrings for a wedding, and thought how gentle the morning could have been. A doha?

Compose a verse about the chakor bird, which gazes at the sky in silent longing, and the cloud passing without a sound, while men below shout their chants as though God were deaf to the quiet of devotion.
chakor bird, cloud, shouting
A chakor bird sat silent on our roof while a cloud drifted and the neighbours' loud jagran carried on until three in the morning. I felt the bird knew more about God. A doha?
doha: the chakor bird and a cloud are silent but people shout their prayers
The chakor bird gazes without a word, the cloud passes without a sound, and man shouts at a Lord who is not deaf.
Why do you shout your prayers from the roof of your house, as though the Lord were deaf, when He dwells in the quiet room of your own heart and hears every breath you take?
house, loud prayer
The man in the house next to ours holds his devotional singing with a microphone at midnight every Thursday, and we can't sleep. A doha for him?
The house trembles with the noise of praise while the Beloved waits in the silence of the heart.
doha: shouting prayers inside the house through a mic, is God deaf?
deaf God, loud chants
A doha for those who think the Lord can only hear them if they chant until their throats are raw, shouting the holy names in the streets as though a whisper had never reached the divine ear.
My uncle's chanting group practises at full volume every evening, and the dogs howl along. He says God must be woken up. What would Kabir say?
He shouts the Name until his voice cracks, as if the Lord had wandered far from his ear.
doha pls about shouting your chants at God
doha: loud prayer at the bier and the spinning wheel quietly turning, who is closer to God
bier, spinning wheel, shouting
At my uncle's last rites the reciters chanted so loudly beside the bier that my aunt could not hear her own grief, while in the corner her spinning wheel stood silent. A doha?

A doha on the loud chanting around the bier and the spinning wheel that turns without a sound, honest work done in quiet being nearer to the Lord than the thunder of those who shout as if He were deaf.
Beside the bier they shout, beside the spinning wheel there is silence; which is nearer the Lord?
Please write a doha on the man who raises his voice in prayer in the early dawn, loud enough to wake the whole neighbourhood, who believes that the Lord is far away and must be reached by shouting.
loud dawn prayer
doha: god is not deaf, stop shouting prayers
My grandmother, who prays in a whisper, says her prayers have never needed anyone's microphone. She was reacting to a loud religious event in the park. A doha?
A whisper in the heart travels farther than a shout across the town.
Louder and louder rises the prayer, but God, who sits within, is not deaf; only the shouting heart is.
A doha on how the man who shouts the loudest in his devotions is often the most deaf to the cries of the poor and sick around him, though he believes the Lord must be addressed in thunder.
shouting man, deaf heart
write a doha: the loudest prayer is the emptiest
Our local religious leader has the loudest voice at every festival and yet ignored the old woman who was crying outside his gate. What would Kabir say?
loud chants, quiet God
The drum beats, the voices rise, and the Lord sits unmoved in the silence behind them.
doha: God is quiet, people are loud, funny contrast
Last night's festival procession blasted music until two in the morning, and the sick old man next lane could not sleep. Doha for him?
A doha on the festival crowds whose drums and chants shake the street for hours, who believe that the louder the sound, the nearer the Lord, though the Lord has always been found in stillness.
A group of young men in our colony shout slogans of faith through a megaphone every evening, and I think their God must be quite far if they need that. Could you write a doha?
Write a doha on the folly of thinking that a loud voice makes a strong faith, as the Lord who hears the footsteps of an ant has no need of the thunder of men.
Is the Lord an old man who cannot hear, that you must storm the sky with your voice?
doha on megaphone prayers and how silly it is
megaphone faith
The wedding at the palace hall next to our colony played religious chants on loudspeakers until the early hours, and the bride's father was sleeping on the stairs, tired. A doha?
doha: palace wedding with loud chanting all night, pointless
Write a doha about the rich man's palace where chanting is played at full volume to announce his piety to the neighbours, though the Lord hears only the whisper of a poor man's honest prayer.
In the great palace the chanting shakes the walls, and the Lord, quite unmoved, waits in the quiet.
palace, loud chanting
My friend turned up the volume of his devotional songs until the whole block could hear, and said it was an offering. I said, 'To whom?' A doha for that exchange?
Turn down the voice and turn up the heart, and the Beloved will hear you from the next room.
Please write a doha on those who believe that raising the volume of their devotion makes it holier, forgetting that the Lord listens not to the loudness of the voice but to the honesty behind it.
volume is not devotion
doha: turning up the volume on prayer doesn't make it holier
The ocean roars and the bitter gourd grows silent; man shouts his prayers but remains bitter within.
The bitter gourd soup my mother made was served with loud chanting from the neighbours and a wedding, near the ocean, and I thought, what is all this noise for? A doha?
doha: ocean roars but prayers should be quiet, bitter gourd people shout
ocean, bitter gourd, shouting
A doha on how the ocean roars in its depths and yet is calm in its soul, while the man who shouts his chants beside it remains as bitter as a bitter gourd, deaf to the silence of the Lord.
Write a doha about the bee that hums softly as it goes about its work among the flowers and finds sweetness, and the man who shouts his prayers for hours and finds no sweetness at all in the Name.
doha: bee hums quietly and still finds honey, loud prayers dont work
A bee kept humming over the flowers in my garden while the neighbours' loud religious music played, and I felt the bee was more devoted than the whole crowd. A doha?
The bee hums low and finds the honey; the man cries loud and finds the noise.
bee, shouted prayers
A doha about the one who shouts his prayers from a mountain top, hoping the Lord will hear better, though the Lord is as near in a quiet valley, or in the pain of a thorn, as on any peak.
mountain, thorn, shouting
On a trek up a mountain, a group shouted their chants from the summit, and I had a thorn in my foot and I prayed quietly. Mine felt closer. A doha?
doha: you can shout from a mountain or feel a thorn, God is quiet
Shout from the mountain top or sit with a thorn in the foot, the Lord's ear is the same.
A verse about the bee that does not shout when it finds a flower and the man who shouts to find his Lord, as though the Lord were far away and deaf and the bee closer to Him than man.
bee, shouting prayer
My friend said he would out shout anyone with his prayer, and just then a bee landed on his arm and he went quiet. Doha for that moment?
doha: bee is quiet, man is loud with his prayers
The bee is quiet in its devotion, and the man is loud in his; one of them gets honey.
doha: a thread of silent prayer is stronger than a loud chant
My aunt stitches in silence, thread by thread, and calls it her prayer, while the neighbours shout their chants all day. Doha for her?
A doha on the fine thread of a quiet prayer, spun without a sound in the heart, which reaches the Lord more surely than the loud chorus of voices that men raise in their hundreds.
thread, silent prayer
One quiet thread of prayer from the heart is worth a thousand voices thrown at the sky.
shouting, as if deaf
Why does the man in the street shout his hymns at the sky as if God were hard of hearing, and the Beloved who knows his every thought were sitting at the far end of a crowded hall?
My cousin's religious group parades through the streets at night with drums and microphones, and I thought, does their God have bad hearing? A doha?
doha pls: the God is not deaf, why shout
Do you call a friend who sits beside you from across the town?
He calls to the Lord from rooftops, though the Lord sits in the ear of his own heart.
roof-top shouting
doha about shouting hymns from the rooftop
A doha about the man who stands on his roof at dawn and shouts his devotion over the town, as though the Lord were somewhere far over the horizon and could not hear the quiet one beside him.
The man across from us stands on his terrace each morning with a loud speaker for his devotional songs, and it wakes the entire street. A doha for him?
At the funeral, the loud chanting did not let us hear the potter's quiet words about his late father, who made clay wares for fifty years and wore a shroud like a simple man. A doha?
A doha about the potter who shapes clay in silence and the shroud that wraps the dead without a sound, set against the noisy shouting of men who believe that the Lord is deaf to a quiet heart.
doha: potter and clay are silent, shroud is silent, but men shout prayers
potter and clay, shroud, noise
The potter shapes the clay in silence, the shroud is folded in silence, but man storms heaven with his voice.
In the evening my neighbour recites his prayers at the top of his voice so that everyone will know how holy he is. Honestly, it seems more like a performance. A doha?
He prays aloud so the street may hear, but the Lord needs no audience.
Write a doha on the person who raises his voice in prayer so that all around him can hear and admire, who is praying not to the Lord but to the crowd that listens.
prayer for the crowd
doha: praying loud so others can hear
forehead mark, temple, loud
A doha on the one with a bright forehead mark who shouts his chants at the temple gate for all to hear, though the Lord within the temple is neither deaf nor impressed by the volume.
doha: loud chants at the temple and a big forehead mark, show off
The man with the biggest forehead mark at our temple has the loudest voice during aarti, and the elderly worshippers move away because of it. A doha?
The forehead mark is bright and the voice is loud, but the Lord sits in the quiet corner of the temple.
The weaver in our lane works silently at his loom all day, but the man across the way shouts the holy names with his hoarse tongue so loudly that the weaver can barely think. A doha?
The loom is silent as it weaves, but the tongue that shouts has woven nothing.
A doha on the loom that makes cloth without a word and the tongue that shouts holy names without a thought, with the Lord's blessing falling on the weaver's quiet work and not on the noise.
doha: weaver's loom is quiet, tongue is loud, who is closer to God
loom, tongue, loud prayer
doha: lion roars but doesn't shout prayers, humans do
The lion roars because it is a lion; man roars at the Lord because he is afraid.
A doha about the lion whose roar comes from its true nature, and the man whose shouted prayers come from his fear, trying to wake a Lord who was never asleep and could never be deaf.
lion, shouting prayer
The lion at the zoo roared and the whole crowd went quiet, while the people shouting prayers at the nearby festival went on. I thought, that lion is more honest. Could you write a doha?
loud devotion, empty heart
Louder and louder the praise, emptier and emptier the heart.
doha on loud prayer and empty hearts
The family that organises the neighbourhood religious event is the one that never visits the sick, and they have the biggest speakers. A doha?
A doha about the volume of devotion in the street that grows louder every year while sincerity in the heart grows quieter, and the Lord who hears the heart is not moved by the noise.
prayer beads, loud prayer
doha: prayer beads in one hand and a loudspeaker in the other lol
A doha about the person who rolls prayer beads and chants at full volume, so that all the neighbours know how many rounds he has done, though the Lord knows only the silence in his mind.
Mr. Verma sits on his balcony every morning with prayer beads, chanting so loudly that the whole building knows when he has finished. Doha for him?
The prayer beads turn, the voice thunders, and the heart sits silent behind both.
A crow cawed loudly on our window sill during the loud chanting from the next street, and my daughter said, 'Is the crow also praying?' A doha for her?
A doha on the crow which caws as loudly as it can at the dawn without pretending to be holy, and the man who shouts his prayers with equal volume and calls it devotion.
The crow caws at the dawn and the pious shout at the dawn; the crow at least is honest.
doha: crow caws loud and people shout prayers loud, same noise
crow, loud prayer
doha: quiet prayer is better than shouting
Be still, for the Lord is not far.
silence is prayer
When my grandfather was ill, we all sat in silence at his bedside and prayed quietly, and it felt more powerful than any of the loud festivals we had attended. A doha?
A doha that teaches how a silent prayer from the depth of the heart is heard more clearly than any shout from the street, because the Lord listens to sincerity and not to loudness.
doha: a tree grows silently, but we shout our prayers
The tree grows in silence and gives shade to all; man shouts at heaven and gives nothing.
There is a big old tree in our park where an old man sits and prays silently, while a loud religious group sets up their speakers right next to him. A doha for him?
tree, silent prayer
A doha on the tree that grows without a sound and bears fruit for all who come, and the man who shouts his chants beneath it and bears nothing, as if the Lord could only be reached by noise.
pls doha: why do people shout prayers over loudspeakers all morning
I'm a night shift worker and every morning at five I'm woken by loudspeakers from both the religious places near my flat. Is there a doha that might make them think?
A doha on the peaceful dawn that is broken every day by loudspeakers shouting from all corners, making men believe they have honoured the Lord when they have only disturbed His creation.
loudspeakers at dawn
Dawn is sacred because it is quiet; why drown it in your shouting?

Write about the pilgrims who shout their cries of praise for hours on the road until their voices go hoarse, thinking that exhaustion makes devotion deeper, while the Lord asks for only a calm and true heart.
Hoarse with shouting, empty of silence, they march toward a Lord who stands within them.
The pilgrim group that passed through our village chanted so loudly and for so long that the children had to cover their ears, and some were hoarse by evening. A doha on that?
hoarse pilgrims
doha: pilgrims shouting until hoarse, God doesnt need that
cleric, loud call, deaf
Write a doha asking the cleric who climbs up to give the call at the top of his voice whether the Lord is deaf, and whether the One who made the ear needs shouting to hear.
doha: the cleric shouts from above as if God is deaf, kabir style
Every morning the cleric of the neighbourhood calls out so loudly that even the dogs cannot sleep. I thought of Kabir's question about whether God is deaf. A doha?
O cleric, why do you shout aloud? Is the Lord deaf, who made all ears?
The Hindu mandali in our area, the prayer hall nearby, and the street procession all compete at the same hour for who is loudest. I think the Lord would prefer silence. A doha?
doha: competing noisy chants at the same time, funny
competing noise
Three voices shout at once to one Lord, and He hears only the silence beneath.

A doha on the competition between those who shout their hymns, each louder than the last, as if God were a prize for the loudest voice and the Lord were on the side of whoever has the biggest speakers.
Our milkman hums softly while delivering milk each dawn, and I thought his tune was a better prayer than the loud ones from the neighbouring street. A doha about this?
A doha on the quiet humming of a milkman delivering milk at dawn, more devotional than the shouting that fills the streets from morning to night, because the Lord hears honest work and a calm heart.
doha: milk man hums quietly, better than shouting hymns
The milkman's hum is a prayer without words; the shouting prayers are words without prayer.
milk, quiet song, loud prayer
parrot, crow, loud chants
doha: parrot repeats loud chants, crow caws, God hears neither but hears the heart
The parrot repeats the Name, the crow cries it out; neither of them is deaf, and neither knows what it says.
A doha on the parrot who repeats loud chants without understanding them and the crow who caws all day, to show that the one who shouts without understanding is no wiser than a bird.
My neighbour's parrot repeats the loud chants of the family all day, and the crow outside joins in. Everyone thinks it is hilarious and holy at once. Doha?

A doha on the voice trained to rise above all others in the praise of the Lord, a proud, practised voice, that thinks itself holy for its power, and the Lord who prefers the broken voice of the humble.
The Lord prefers the cracked voice of the humble to the polished thunder of the proud.
At our community event the man with the best voice for chanting sang for an hour, then ignored the shy old man who whispered a prayer in the corner. A doha?
proud voice, humble whisper
doha: Lord prefers the humble whisper to the trained voice
Before dawn, my neighbour started his daily chanting at full volume again, so I turned up my own music to drown him out, and then felt silly. A doha for both of us?
doha about two people competing to be louder at dawn, God hears neither
noise at dawn
A doha on the neighbours who each raise their voices louder to drown the other out, calling it devotion on one side and annoyance on the other, while the Lord waits in the silence they both ignore.
Voice against voice, noise against noise, and the Beloved waits for the quiet between.
A peacock called from the field outside while the loud chanting went on in the colony, and I thought the peacock sounded closer to God. A doha for that?
The peacock calls when it feels the rain, not to impress; man shouts to impress the Lord.
A doha about the peacock which cries out only when its heart is full of the coming rain, and the man who shouts his chants every day whether or not his heart is full or empty.
doha: peacock calls from feeling, we shout from habit
peacock, honest voice
The annual religious festival in our town had speakers every fifty meters, and the whole town was sleepless for three nights. A doha on that?
speakers everywhere
A speaker on every corner, and still the Lord is not heard above the quiet of his own creation.
A doha on the festival that fills the town with speakers and amplifiers until nobody can hear himself think, as if the Lord were deaf and needed the whole town to be deafened too.
doha: festival with speakers everywhere, no peace
stone, deaf, shouting
doha: shouting at a stone god or a deaf God, same thing
A doha on the one who shouts his prayers at a stone image, believing it will hear him better, though both the stone and his raised voice are equally deaf to the quiet need of the heart.
Shout at the stone and the stone will not answer; shout at the sky and the sky will not answer; whisper to the heart and the Lord replies.
I saw a man shouting his prayer at a stone and it struck me that he was shouting at a deaf thing, as if the real God were deaf too. A doha?
noise, not worship
Noise is not worship; the heart's hush is.
My son asked why the people in our building chant so loudly if God is everywhere, and I was stumped. Can you write a doha to answer him?
doha: why people shout prayers when God is everywhere
A doha that explains to a child that the Lord is present everywhere and in everyone, and so does not need to be called with shouting, as one speaks softly to one who stands beside you.
doha: thief breaks in during loud chanting and nobody noticed
thief, loud chanting
The thief slipped through the noise of devotion, for those who shouted loudest heard least.
During last night's loud religious event, a thief broke into three flats and nobody noticed because of the noise. A doha for that?
A doha on the thief who walks unnoticed into the home of the loud devotee, whose noisy chanting covers all footsteps, so that he who shouts for the Lord loses what the Lord gave him.
doha: boat in the stream is quiet, we shout our prayers
A doha on the boat that glides across the water in silence, carrying its passengers safely, and the men on the shore who shout their prayers to the Lord as if the quiet voyage could not be heard.
boat, silence, loud prayer
The boatman rows across the lake in silence while the pilgrims in the boat shout their chants, and the boatman smiled at me and shook his head. A doha?
The boat moves in silence across the water; the pilgrims in it shout at the heavens.
pearl, loud shout
doha: pearl forms in silence, shouting doesn't make you holy
A doha on the pearl which forms slowly in the dark of the oyster without a single sound, and the man who shouts his devotion to the world and has nothing of its patient glow within.
My grandmother wore a pearl necklace every day and prayed in silence, and she said loud prayer is like polishing a pebble to look like a pearl. Could you write a doha?
The pearl grows in silence; devotion too.
The lion roars to the woods and the bell rings to the sky, but the Lord answers the hush of the heart.
A doha on the ringing of the bell and the roaring of the lion, loud things that fill the air, which are no nearer to the Lord than the silent whisper of a sincere devotee.
bell, lion, loud prayer
A lion statue stood at the entrance and the bell rang loudly over the heads of the chanting crowd, but a small girl in the corner prayed in silence. A doha?
doha: bell and lion are loud but the Lord hears silence
fish, silent prayer
The fish in the water makes no sound, and it lives in the Lord's own element; why does man shout?
doha: fish are silent in water but we shout our prayers on the bank
A doha on the silent fish gliding through the water that gives it life, and the man on the bank shouting his prayers to the Lord who is as close to him as the water to the fish.
My friend's pet fish swims silently in its bowl all day while his family's loud prayers shake the room. He said the fish was holier. Doha?
A doha about the bitter gourd that grows quietly on its vine and does not boast of its use, and the loud devotee who shouts of his piety every day yet is as bitter in speech as the gourd.
The bitter gourd grows without a word; the shouting man grows bitter with his own noise.
doha: bitter gourd quietly grows, loud prayers make people bitter

bitter gourd, shouting

doha with a seed and a spinning wheel, wake up before death comes
seed, spinning wheel, wake up
O drowsy soul, the day of leaving is near, and the hour you wasted will never return: rise, rise
My friend's father promised every year that next year he would take a trip, and he died in March; I want a doha that wakes me from my own endless next year
Kabir cried that the sleeping soul will lose the chance to cross the world, so please write a doha in the same urgent voice telling the heedless to wake before death comes and the chance is gone
wake up now
doha that says wake up now, death is coming
Write a doha in an urgent voice that tells the sleeper to stop decorating his house and wake up, because death is already at the gate, and nothing he has built can answer when he is called
doha about a house, wake up and do the real work before death comes
You paint the walls of your house and death is painting your name on a different wall: wake, wake
house, wake up
My cousin spent years renovating his house and then collapsed on the stairs of it, with half the rooms unfinished; I want a doha that wakes people from that kind of sleep
A moth flew round my grandmother as she lay, and as the forehead mark on her brow faded, I realised how I have been wasting the days she gave me; wake up, I told myself
doha with a forehead mark and a moth, wake up before death comes
Write a doha in an urgent voice in which a moth circles a flame and a person with a forehead mark sleeps in prayer without meaning it, and the voice tells him to wake now before death comes
forehead mark, moth, wake
The moth leaps toward the flame and the forehead mark is only paint: wake, wake, for death is real
death is near
My colleague jumped up at the news of an accident down the road and went quiet for the rest of the day, saying it could have been any of us; I want a doha that does that for everybody
Kabir called the careless to wake up before death put its hand on them, so write a doha in his urgent voice telling the reader to open his eyes this moment because the hour is nearly spent
doha that warns people to wake up right now before death takes them
Rise, you who sleep! The hour of leaving is nearer than the hour of waking
doha with a heron, wake up before its too late
The heron stands still and the water-dwellers watch it, and death stands still too: wake, wake, before it strikes
Write an urgent doha in which a heron stands patient at the water's edge while the sleepers below do not stir, telling all who sleep to wake because death waits as still as a heron
A heron stood in our pond for an hour, perfectly still, and nobody noticed until it struck; I thought of death, which stands as still as that, and I want a doha that wakes the sleepers
heron, wake up now
Sand falls through the glass of days and the sleeper sleeps on: wake, wake, for the last grain is falling
Write a doha in an urgent voice telling the heedless that the sand is running out in the glass of their lives, that death is the last grain, and that they must wake and act before it falls
My uncle had a sand clock on his desk, and last year after his heart attack he said now I see how fast it falls; I want a doha that wakes people before their last grain
sand, wake up now
doha with sand, wake up before the last grain falls
Write a doha in an urgent voice in which a moneylender counts his coins under a tree while death stands behind it, and the voice shouts at him to wake from his greed and do something that matters
moneylender, tree, wake up
doha with a moneylender and a tree, wake up before death comes
Under the tree the moneylender counts his coins, and death counts his breaths: wake, O fool, before the count is done
The moneylender who sat under the tree in our village counted coins until the day he died, and the coins stayed under the tree; I want a doha that shakes the next moneylender awake
At the funeral of my school friend, I stood there thinking that I'm next in some years, and that I've been dozing through everything; I want a doha that wakes up all the other dozing people
Write an urgent doha telling all who sleep in comfort that death is closer than they think, the call to wake has sounded for years, and today is the last day to answer
doha that tells everyone to wake up before death comes, loud and urgent
The sleeper dreams of a long road, and death is on the threshold: wake, wake, there is no time
wake up, now
The bee gathers honey under the stars and you are asleep: wake, O drowsy one, before the night of death
bee, stars, wake up
doha with a bee and stars, wake up before death comes
Write an urgent doha in which a bee works through the night under the stars while a person sleeps, telling him to wake and work before death ends the season of work
I watched a bee keep working under the stars as I lay on my cot, and then I got a call that my uncle had died; I want a doha that wakes me up and everyone like me
The cuckoo cries and the moneylender sleeps on his coins, and death sits on the bed: wake, wake
cuckoo, moneylender, wake up
Write an urgent doha in which a cuckoo calls while a moneylender sleeps on his coins, telling him to wake because death has come to take him from them
My neighbour the moneylender slept soundly on his money while a cuckoo called outside his window every morning, and then he was gone; I want a doha that wakes people like him
doha with a cuckoo and a moneylender, wake up before death comes
When the call came about my uncle's accident, I was in the middle of an argument about a tiny thing, and I felt my tongue freeze; I want a doha that wakes people from such petty sleep
The tongue is busy with idle talk, and death is busy at the threshold: wake, O sleeper, speak the true word now
tongue, wake up now
Write a doha in an urgent voice that tells the sleeper to use his tongue for the Name instead of idle talk, because death will soon still it for ever and the time for the Name will be gone
doha with a tongue, wake up before death shuts it
A parrot nearby keeps calling the old man's name, but he has been dead a week, and I felt it call me too; I want a doha that wakes up the sleepers
parrot, wake up
doha with a parrot, wake up before death comes
The parrot repeats the master's name in the empty rooms, and the voice cries: wake, wake, while the name is still yours
Write a doha in an urgent voice in which a parrot repeats borrowed words while its owner sleeps, and the voice tells him to wake and speak his own truth before death silences him
The skeleton in the field grins at the sleeper: wake, for you too will be bare, and soon
At the museum I stood beside a skeleton and suddenly could not breathe, thinking about my wasted years; I want a doha that gives everybody that jolt
Write a doha in an urgent voice in which a skeleton speaks to the sleeper, saying that it too slept once, that it too thought there was time, and that the sleeper must wake now before he joins it
doha with a skeleton, wake up before you end up like it
skeleton, wake up now
Write an urgent doha in which a river flows on while a person sleeps on the bank, telling him to wake and cross before death carries him away and the chance is lost
doha with a river, wake up before death comes
My uncle slept on the riverbank every afternoon for years, and the river rose one night and took everything; I want a doha for people who nap in the path of something bigger
river, wake up now
The river runs on while you sleep on its bank, and death is the flood that wakes no one: rise, rise now
doha on a thief with sweet words, hovering like a fly around victims
A smooth-talking man sold my mother a worthless policy; he buzzed around her like a fly, was extremely polite, and next day vanished like a thief.
thief, fly, false smile
The thief wears a smile as sweet as a friend's greeting, and the fly of false friendliness follows the scent of trust.
Please write a doha about how a thief who speaks sweetly is far more dangerous than one who breaks in at night, because a fly of false friendliness hovers around until he finds your weakness.
doha on people with two faces, nice to ur face and nasty behind
Could you write a doha about the person who wears one face for the crowd and another in private, smiling and flattering while he plans harm, so that nobody can ever really trust a word he says?
One face for the crowd, another for the hour of plotting; the double-faced man deceives even himself.
My business partner praised me at the meeting and then quietly took my clients the next week, and I am still stunned.
two-faced, can't trust

Compose a doha for the cheat who wears a mask of devotion, speaks of fire and holy vows, and rides in a palanquin while he robs the villagers who trusted him, showing that the cunning are always found out.
The preacher who arrived in a palanquin, speaking fiery words about charity, left our village with all its donations and not a word of thanks.
He rode in a palanquin and spoke words of fire, yet the cheat's pockets were full of the poor man's trust.
palanquin, fire, cheating preacher
doha on a fake holy man in a doli with fiery speeches who cheated everyone
honeyed words, bitter aim
A man at the bus stand was so kind to my grandfather, offered him tea, and walked off with his wallet.
Please write a doha about how people who speak the sweetest words to your face are often the ones with the worst intentions, and how we must look at their deeds and not just their talk.
Sweet is the voice of the deceiver, yet bitter is the purpose it hides.
doha for ppl who are super nice but turn out to be frauds
doha on cheating someone, it always comes back
The fraud thrives for a season; but trust, once betrayed, never returns to the betrayer's hands.
I'd like a doha about how the person who cheats another gains a small profit now but loses a name, friendships and peace of mind for life, so that in the end he is the poorest of all.
fraud ruins the fraud
My cousin cheated his friend on a land deal and now no family in our town will let him sit at their table.
Can you write me a doha about how the cheat who adds salt to the true weight of his goods fools the poor buyer, but cannot fool his own conscience, which keeps count of every falsehood until the end?
The vendor mixed salt in the spice he sold me and swore it was pure, and I trusted his smiling face.
doha on someone who cheats with salt in the goods
The cheat sprinkles salt in the pure grain, but the account of his lies is kept elsewhere.
salt, cheating trader
swan, fire, false saint
The swan wears white and the fire hides in the ember; deceit too puts on a spotless outer robe.
A man dressed in spotless white like a swan came to our colony, and by the time the fire from his tall promises died down, our savings were gone.
doha on a fake swan with fire inside, a cheat dressed pure
Write a doha about the man in snow-white garments who looks like a gentle swan but whose fire of greed burns the trusting, showing that trickery can wear the most innocent colours.
A pearl of speech on the lip, a plot in the mind; the deceiver dazzles with words but starves the trusting.
Could you write a doha about the pearl-like words of a flatterer that dazzle the ear but hide plans to take advantage, so that the wise listener tests every sweet phrase before accepting it?
pearl words, false heart
My new neighbour kept showering us with pearl-like compliments until she had borrowed all our savings, and now she does not answer the phone.
doha on flattery as a pearl that hides a lie
He smiled at me all through the party and told everyone I was his best friend, but I later found he had applied for my job behind my back.
doha on friends who stab u in the back
Compose a doha about the false friend who laughs with you at the feast and plots to ruin you, showing that one must judge a person by his actions in hard times and not his words in good times.
His smile is a cover and his words are soft; behind both the traitor lays his plan.
false friend, hidden plan
The man who sold us the plot of land swore on his mother, but all we found was a bundle of ash and paperwork that meant nothing.
doha on fraud that turns into ash in ur hands
Compose a doha showing that the profit of deceit turns to ash in the hands of the cheat, no matter how clever the scheme, because falsehood has no roots and cannot hold anything for long.
The wealth of fraud turns to ash in the hand; only honest gain remains.
ash, fraud's reward
At the cremation ground the cheat finds his fine speech meaningless, for no lie can bribe the final hour.
My uncle cheated dozens of people in his lifetime, and at the cremation ground I could see no one who truly mourned him.
cremation ground, liar's end
Write a doha showing that the cheat who builds his life on lies finds only an empty cremation ground at the end, where nobody weeps for him because he never gave anyone a reason to trust him.
doha on frauds ending up alone at the cremation ground

Write a doha about the person who speaks sweet and smiling words while secretly nursing harmful intentions, and how such pretence may fool people for a short while but is always revealed by the quiet test of time.
doha on fake niceness and hidden bad intent
Our landlord was so warm when we signed the lease, and the minute we moved in he started inventing charges to squeeze more money from us.
Behind the courteous greeting hides a cold purpose; let me learn to read the face behind the face.
smiling deceiver
hey doha on liars who cheat the innocent
I want a doha saying that trickery may win a battle but lose the war, because whoever deceives others must keep inventing more lies to cover the first, and soon he is trapped by his own falsehoods.
cheating never pays
My classmate copied my work and then told the teacher I copied his, and I stood there too shocked to even speak.
One lie needs seven more to stand; the cheat builds on weakness and calls it strength.
doha on soft cotton words hiding a nasty plan
The cotton trader spoke so gently while weighing my bale, yet he somehow got away with a fifth of what I brought.

Please write a doha about the person who speaks soft as cotton and promises everything, but whose real purpose is to take advantage of your trust, so that the careful ones learn to weigh actions rather than words.
Soft as cotton are his promises, yet each one hides a hook for the unwary.
cotton words, cheating
The glass that imitates a diamond may fool the eye, but never the jeweller's test; so the false are found.
My cousin bought a so-called diamond ring on a street corner for a bargain, only to find a piece of glass, and the seller was gone.
fake diamond, fraud
doha on fake diamonds and scammers

Could you write a doha about a cheat who sells glass pretending it is a diamond, showing that honest worth lasts while false shine fades, and the deceiver's fortune disappears when the buyer finally sees the truth?

Compose a doha about how a snake that charms with a gentle swaying motion is far more dangerous than one that hisses openly, just as the flatterer with a pleasant manner is to be feared more than the honest enemy.
doha on smiling people like snakes, can't trust them
snake, false friendliness
My supervisor greets everyone warmly while quietly reporting each of us for small slips; he moves like a snake in the grass.
The snake that bows and sways has fang beneath its grace; beware the smiling visitor.
My boss walks into the meeting with a roar like a lion, then turns into a lamb when the director is around, and cheats all of us when it suits him.
Compose a doha about a man who is a lion to those below him and a mouse to those above, showing the fraud of a person who changes faces to suit his advantage and deserves no trust from anyone.
A lion to the weak, a lamb to the strong; the double-faced man has no true face.
doha on bosses who act like lions to us but lick up to their seniors
lion, false front
trust no flatterer
My co-worker praised every idea I had and then presented them to the manager as her own.
Praise sung too sweetly is suspect; look for the motive behind the flattering song.
Write a doha showing that a person who cheats others by pretending to be a friend carries guilt in his own mind and can never rest, whether in company or alone, until he confesses and makes good.
doha about backstabbers who pretend to be friends
The rose is beautiful and the thorn beneath is hidden; the cheat's smile is the same.
My new boyfriend was so charming at the start, but a thorn of lies kept appearing, and after six months I found out he had been seeing someone else.
thorn, hidden harm
Compose a doha about how a pleasing face and gracious words often conceal a thorn, so that we must be careful before we trust a stranger, and learn to read behaviour rather than appearance.
doha on charming ppl who turn out to be thorns

Write a doha about the bitter gourd that looks like any other vegetable but turns the whole meal bitter once it is in the mouth, just as a deceitful person looks pleasant but sours every relationship he enters.
The bitter gourd wears the green of health and carries the taste of poison; so does the liar's friendship.
bitter gourd, false friend
doha on bitter gourd = fake friend
My brother-in-law looks decent enough but, like a bitter gourd, he turns every family meeting sour with his lies and schemes.
After he borrowed money pretending to have a sick child, we found out he gambled it all away on the same day.
Pity pretended, need counterfeited; the cheat's tears flow where truth has long since dried.
I'd like a doha about the man who pretends to be sick, poor or desperate to win sympathy and money from kind people, and about how his false tears cost the real needy their chance of help.
fake tears
doha on scammers who fake sob stories
doha on a thief who pretends to be honest
A man came to our colony claiming to be a retired officer, charmed everyone, and then one night our thief-like guest was gone with several valuables.
Compose a doha about the thief who lives among honest people in a good man's clothing, and about how the day his mask slips, the trust he took is lost forever and cannot be won back by apology.
The thief in the garb of the honest has the sweetest face; only time unmasks him.
thief, honest mask
The yogi in saffron near the ocean promised to double our money through prayers; we paid him gladly, and then he vanished like a wave.
yogi, ocean, fraud
doha on a fake yogi cheating ppl by the ocean
Write a doha about a fake yogi who sits beside the ocean pretending to meditate while he reads the pockets of the pilgrims who come to him, and how real holiness never asks for money in return.
The ocean is vast, but the fake yogi's greed is wider; his holy robes hide a hungry hand.
cheat, be careful

Please write a doha explaining that the swindler's greatest skill is to make the victim believe he is being helped, so that honest people must always check the claims of strangers before handing over their trust or their savings.
doha on scammers who act like helpers

The deceiver speaks of help while his hand reaches for your savings; guard your trust carefully.
fraud, fake smile
Beware the honeyed greeting, for the cheat's welcome is the first step in the plan to ruin you.

Compose a doha showing that those who say one thing and do another, praising principles in public and breaking them in private, carry a divided character that eventually brings them shame and loss of every honest friend.
doha on ppl who say one thing and do another
My uncle lectured us all on honesty for years and then we found out he had been cooking the accounts at work.
My neighbour came with a needle to mend my curtain, and while smiling like a snake, she made copies of my keys.
needle, snake, trickery
The needle seems gentle; the snake seems harmless; both are cruel to the one who trusts.
doha with needle and snake, helpful liars
Could you write a doha that says a person who pretends to help like a needle mending cloth while moving like a snake to harm you is the most dangerous of all, because he is trusted?
Beneath the pleasant word the cheat keeps his plan, and he who trusts too quickly pays too much.
After the agent assured me the car had never been in an accident, I found out it had been hit three times and repainted.
false promise
Write a doha showing that those who cheat do so because they lack the courage to earn honestly, and that the person who lives with deception will always be nervous about being found out in the end.
doha on liars who sell fake things
doha on cheating in exams, felt so guilty

cheating, guilty conscience

doha on a washerman who cheats ppl and a palace that is full of liars

Compose a doha about a washerman who returns the wrong garments and denies it, and about the palace where courtiers smile at the king while plotting against him, showing that cheating exists at every level of society.
palace, washerman, cheating
The washerman and the courtier both cheat; one in a lane, the other in a palace, and both shame their name.
The washerman mixed up our garments and swore he hadn't, while at the palace function the minister's smile hid some serious scheming.
Write a doha saying that the one who sets a trap for others is first to fall into it, so a clever man is not one who tricks others but one honest enough to avoid trickery.
traps catch trappers
He who plots another's ruin plans his own; the schemer is the architect of his fall.
doha on karma for people who play tricks
My co-worker tried to get me fired by spreading false stories, and he is the one who got dismissed last month.
false charm
doha on ppl who act kind just to use others
She was my best friend until she got the promotion, and then she did not return a single call, and I realised she'd been using me.
Friendship feigned for gain is no friendship; the self-serving smile hides a list of favours owed.

Please write a doha about the people who make friends only when they need something, flatter you in difficult days, and disappear when your fortune changes, showing that false friendship is simply a business of the heart.
Could you write a doha for the dishonest dealer who shortchanges customers a little every day and believes nobody notices, though in the end all those small thefts are repaid in full with interest?
The dealer in our area shortchanged us a little every month for years, and the day we discovered it, nobody would ever buy from him again.
doha on small daily cheating adds up
A little each day he takes from the trusting; but the account of years comes due in a single hour.
petty cheating
Smiling lips and scheming mind: the pair that has ruined more lives than open enemies ever could.

Compose a doha about the difference between an honest enemy and a hidden one, because the honest foe warns you of his intentions while the false friend comes smiling and strikes when you are least expecting.
doha on smiling backstabbers vs open enemies
hidden enemy, smiling face
I would rather face my rival at work than my so-called friend, who is sweet in public and leaks my mistakes to the boss.
doha on a cuckoo that lays eggs in other nests, a cheat
The cuckoo's song is sweet, but she leaves her young in a stranger's care; beware of music that hides a cheat.
Can you write a doha about the cuckoo who sings sweetly yet leaves her eggs in another bird's nest for them to raise, showing that a pleasing voice can hide a selfish and deceitful nature?
My sister has a lovely cuckoo-like voice, and she charms everyone, but she keeps leaving her responsibilities to other people.
cuckoo, sweet but selfish
doha on people who promise a lot but never deliver
Write a doha showing that the person who promises everything and delivers nothing is more harmful than an honest refusal, because he gives hope and then steals it, leaving the trusting one worse off.
Promises given in plenty, yet nothing follows; the faithless fill the air with sweetness and leave the soul empty.
empty promises
The contractor kept promising our roof would be ready next week for six months, taking more money each time, and nothing ever happened.
palanquin, false groom
The groom's family arrived with a grand palanquin and promises of a rich life, and only after the wedding did we learn it was all a pretence to take my sister's dowry.
Please write a doha about the family that arrives for the wedding with a palanquin full of show and promises but hides their greed, showing that pomp is often the cheat's finest costume.
doha on fake rich ppl at weddings in a palanquin, they cheat the bride's family
The palanquin is bright and the promises are brighter; but the bride finds the groom's family empty.
He made me believe that we were going to be partners, and I learnt only later that he never had the slightest intention of keeping his word.
His word was soft, his meaning hard; the trusting soul is the cheat's richest gain.

Please write a doha explaining that people who deceive in business never prosper for long, because the world is small and the news of one betrayal travels farther and faster than a hundred honest deals.
false partner
doha on business partner who cheated me
He builds his fortune on sand and draws his water from a well of lies, and the first rain exposes it all.
doha on a well and sand, a cheating moneyman who builds on sand
Compose a doha showing that wealth built on deceit is like a well dug in the sand, which seems promising at first but collapses at the first rain and leaves nothing for the cheat or his victims.
Our village contractor built a well on sandy ground to save money and cheated the whole panchayat, and the first rains swallowed it.
well, sand, fraud
The cloud of promises he spread over our village brought no rain, and by the time the farmers realised they were being cheated, the leader had gone.
A cloud that thunders but sheds no rain is the cheat's word, loud and empty.
cloud, false promises

Compose a doha showing that the false leader is like a cloud that promises rain and thunders loudly, but passes over without giving a single drop, leaving the farmers' fields dry and their hopes broken.
doha on politicians promising like clouds but giving no rain
doha on a fish caught by a fake bait, deceit
The fish takes the bait for food, not seeing the hook; so the trusting soul is caught by the cheat's kindness.
fish, bait, trickery
My aunt fell for an online scheme that promised high returns, like a fish swallowing bait, and lost all her savings.
Write a doha showing that as the fisherman tempts the fish with bait that hides a hook, a cheat tempts the simple with promises that conceal his purpose, and only the careful avoid the trap.
fish, bait, trap
They offered my father a free holiday in exchange for his bank details, and I told him the fish never sees the hook until it is too late.
The fish loves the bait and forgets the hook; the greedy are caught by the cheat's open hand.
Write a doha about how greedy people are caught like a fish by the bait of the cheat's promises, because they want quick profits and ignore the warning signs that careful people notice at once.
doha with a fish: greed makes u fall for scams

Compose a doha about people who show devotion with loud prayers and long vows while cheating their neighbours in business, showing that false piety is the worst form of dishonesty and cannot hide from the Almighty.
doha on religious ppl who cheat in daily life
cheating pious frauds
The man who leads prayers in our colony is the same one who sells the grain with a false measure; everyone knows but nobody dares to say.
His lips are wet with holy names, his hands are quick with false measures; the Lord sees both.

Write a doha about the temple trustee who collects donations in the name of God and uses them for his own luxury, showing that deceit in holy places is the most shameful and invites the heaviest reckoning.
temple, donation fraud
The trustee of our temple built a new car garage from the offerings, and the poor devotees who gave their last coins had no idea.
He took in the name of God, and spent in the name of self; the temple weeps for such guardians.
doha on a fraud who steals donations from the temple
doha on a pearl dealer who cheats with fake pearls
pearl, cheating dealer
A false pearl glitters in the dealer's palm; only a sharp eye separates the true from the fabricated.
I bought a pearl necklace on holiday for a high price and later learnt it was a cheap imitation.
Please write a doha about the dealer who sells false pearls at the price of true ones, with a sweet smile and a warm handshake, and how one false deal ruins a lifetime's reputation.

Write a doha about how a person who pretends to be poor to receive help, while hiding wealth, steals not only money but the kindness that the truly poor need, and eventually dries up the world's compassion.
doha on fake poverty to get sympathy
I gave money every week to a woman who said she had no food, and then I saw her get into a car and drive away.
pretending to be poor
The cheat who borrows poverty steals from the truly poor, and the kindness of the world grows cold.
Could you write a doha comparing the rainbird that sings of pure rain with a cheat who calls fake metal gold and promises a shower of wealth, showing how false hopes leave the thirsty with nothing?
doha on rainbird and fake gold, scam promises
A scheme promised to turn our small savings into gold within a season, like a rainbird promised rain, and the organisers vanished before the first month ended.
rainbird, gold, scam
The rainbird cries for rain, and the cheat cries gold; the thirsty believe both and are left dry.
cunning, honest heart wins
doha on how honesty beats trickery in the long run
My brother always took shortcuts and fooled people, while I stayed honest and poor, but today his customers are gone and mine stay on.
Honesty is slow yet arrives; trickery is quick and ends in ruin.

Please write a doha about how the trickster seems to win in the short run, but honesty and fairness prove far stronger over a lifetime, because people always return to those whom they can trust without doubt.
lies have short life

Write a doha saying that falsehood and cheating look strong for a day but cannot survive the truth, so a person who builds his future on deception builds on something that will not stand the first test.
My friend lied on his resume to get a job, and in the first month it all came apart in front of everyone.
Falsehood is quick to rise and quick to fall; only the true endures.
doha on lies not lasting long
pearl, fake pearl
My father, an honest jeweller, was cheated by a smooth stranger who gave him a counterfeit pearl in return for a real one.
Compose a doha about how a counterfeit pearl may look as radiant as the true one, but a person who deals in fakes loses the trust that no real pearl can ever buy back.
doha on someone swapping a real pearl for a fake
Counterfeit pearls pass from hand to hand, but the honest eye of time knows the true from the false.
doha on separating pearls from fakes with a winnowing fan
The winnowing fan blows off the chaff of lies; what remains is the honest pearl.

Write a doha showing that the winnowing fan of discernment separates the false from the true, as it does chaff from grain, and the pearl of honest dealing is what remains for the wise after the cheating is blown away.
After months of getting cheated by the sweet-talking sellers, I learnt to winnow out the honest ones like pearls from chaff.
winnowing fan, pearl, cheat
doha about how sharing what you have makes it grow
the more you give
Open your hand and abundance returns to you, for what is shared multiplies and what is hoarded decays.
I started sending half my bonus to a village school last year, and somehow my savings feel fuller than ever; I'd like a doha for that strange fact.
Please write a doha about the generous soul who gives freely to anyone in need, without counting, and who discovers that his own store never runs low, but grows in proportion to what he shares.

A bridge of mercy spans the gulf between rich and poor, and the swan crosses it with a gentle heart.
doha on swan and bridge for kindness to the weak
After the flood washed away the bridge, a farmer carried stranded children across on his back one by one, as gently as a swan.
bridge, swan, gentle pity

Write a doha about the swan that glides across the water with a gentle spirit and the bridge that links the poor to the rich, both teaching that mercy is the road on which the weak and strong may meet.
The yogi lays down his meditation to bind the wound of a stranger; the moth burns, but mercy gives light.

doha on a yogi who stops meditating to help someone in pain
yogi, moth, pity
Compose a doha showing that the true yogi is not one who sits unmoved in meditation while the moth struggles nearby, but one who rises to help every suffering creature without waiting to be asked.
Write a doha about how a ruler without mercy has no real kingdom, while a poor man who shares his last meal with a stranger rules the world, because pity enriches and cruelty impoverishes.
rule with mercy
doha on rulers who are kind vs cruel
Power is heavy without tenderness; the poor man's mercy is lighter than any royal command.
The old village head always put the poorest family's needs before his own, and when he died, the whole district wept for him.

My friend gives his weekends to the old and abandoned at the shelter, and I wish to tell him in a doha that this is the real religion.
doha for a volunteer who helps the old and sick
Blessed are the hands that tend the lonely; they carry the weight of Heaven's own love.
tend the helpless
doha on a sweet tongue and salt in the wound: how cruelty hurts and pity heals

salt, tongue, tenderness

When my friend was crying after her loss, my aunt's sharp tongue added salt to the wound, but a stranger's gentle word helped her.

forest, prayer beads, pity
doha on pilgrims who ignore a crying kid, forest, prayer beads

doha on being kind to ppl at work who are struggling

Look closely at each face that passes by; behind its quiet is a sorrow waiting for a kind word.

see their pain

cremation ground, lute, pity
Compose a doha about the lute player who plays at the cremation ground for a poor man's funeral without taking a coin, showing that mercy for the grieving is the music God loves most.
doha on kindness at a poor persons cremation ground, one-string lute

One thread of mercy mends a torn life; stitch the wounded to the world with kindness.
thread, pity for the poor

doha on a little thread of kindness to help the poor

doha on a potter who gives free pots to the poor, plus sandalwood vibes

potter, sandalwood, kind giving

doha on how a fire burns everyone's hut, we should help those who lost everything

fire victims, help them

jaggery, moneylender, mercy

doha on a moneylender who shows mercy and forgives a debt

doha on groom stopping his doli to help an injured elephant
palanquin, elephant, mercy

doha on temple visit, but helping poor ppl outside more important
temple, mercy first

doha on a sword that protects the weak vs one that hurts them

sword, protect the helpless

doha on standing by a kid who is being bullied

stand by the lonely

He who has once been wounded knows how to bind another's pain, and in that knowing lives the root of mercy.
kindness to patients
doha on how suffering teaches us to care for others

tenderness to the helpless
doha on being gentle with weak ppl

potter, jaggery, kindness

doha on a potter who gives jaggery to the poor children

dew, thief, soft heart

doha on a thief who felt pity and left food

kindness to strangers
doha on being nice to strangers who need help

doha with a musk deer and philosopher's stone about pity
musk deer, philosopher's stone, mercy

doha on kind ppl at crossroads helping lost ppl
crossroads, kindness

doha on bell and rainbird, pity for a thirsty creature
bell, rainbird, mercy
salt, mercy

doha on sharing salt and bread with the hungry

Let your tenderness reach those who have no one; the lonely are God's own guests.
My neighbour is a widow with no children, and I have started to take her out every week, because someone must care.
Could you write a doha about the loneliness of the old and the widowed and about how a visit, a call or a meal brought to them is a gift greater than anything money can buy?
doha on visiting lonely old ppl
care for the lonely
Where there is mercy, the cold of the world melts; let the weeping find a gentle ear.

Please write a doha about the way kindness warms the cold hours of a suffering person's life, and about how one who listens without judging and helps without being asked has already fulfilled the whole law.
listen to sorrow
When my friend lost her baby, I did not say anything wise, I just sat beside her for hours and held her hand.
doha on just being there for someone who is hurting

doha on bier and grindstone, helping poor families at funerals
bier, grindstone, mercy

mosque, cotton, kindness

doha on a mosque giving cotton blankets to the poor in winter

doha on helping a blind man cross the road
I watched a young boy gently lead a blind man across a busy street and refuse any reward, and I wanted to write a verse about it.
help the blind man
Please compose a doha about how guiding a blind man with patience and respect is better than a hundred sermons, since mercy to those who cannot see is the clearest vision a person can achieve.

After the rains the whole village shared its food with the families whose fields were flooded, and nobody asked who was rich or poor.
doha on clouds raining on everyone like kindness
cloud, mercy for all

doha on giving a pot of water to a thirsty stranger
On a hot afternoon I offered a pot of water to a tired labourer on the road, and the blessing in his eyes was worth everything.
A pot of water offered to the thirsty, in the heat of noon, has washed away a thousand sins.
pot of water, kindness
Write a doha about how a simple pot of water offered to a thirsty passer-by in the heat of summer is the cheapest and most precious charity, a deed that brings the giver more joy than a feast.
A man in my neighbourhood noticed a schoolchild without lunch each day, and quietly started leaving food for him without ever saying a word.
Quiet is the mercy that leaves a gift unsigned, and blessed is the hand that gives and hides.
doha on secretly helping someone in need
silent kindness

doha about a lover gone mad for God, dancing before a temple with his shadow
