Let the village laugh; I dance with my shadow before the temple, intoxicated, for the Beloved has stolen my sense.
My neighbors whisper that I have lost my mind, because every evening I sing loudly at the temple steps with my shadow stretching long, and I honestly don't care.
mad dancer, shadow, temple
I wrapped myself in rough cotton and wandered up the mountain singing the Beloved's name while the whole town called me crazy, and I laughed at their words; write a doha about that divine madness.
Rough cotton on my back and the mountain beneath my feet, I am mad, and the Beloved's name is my wine.
doha with cotton and a mountain, a man mad for God's love
My brother quit his job, wore plain cotton and walked up the mountain singing, and when family said he was mad he just grinned.
cotton, mountain, mad lover
They call me drunk and mad; I am, with the Beloved, who poured me a cup of milk and made the world a dream.
doha about a man mad for God who pours milk and ignores everyone's talk
They say I am drunk, and so I am, intoxicated on the Beloved so completely that I would sell all I own for a cup of milk to pour at His feet; compose a doha on this wild devotion.
My uncle gave away his land and now spends every morning pouring milk for the Lord and humming, and nobody in the village knows what to make of him.
mad with milk offering
mad with devotion
doha for a lover mad for the Lord who ignores what the world says
Let them call me mad; I have forgotten my name, my caste and my shame, and my only sanity is the Beloved.
I have lost all sense of shame and caution, dancing in the street with my hair loose, mad for the Beloved while the neighbors tut and stare; please write a doha for the madness of such a lover.
My aunt dances in the lane whenever she hears the Lord's name, her hair loose, and she says the people who laugh are the ones who are truly lost.
singing at the crossroads
doha with a crossroads, a lover mad with divine love, ignoring the crowd
There is a man who sings at the crossroads every dawn, drunk on devotion, and the whole neighborhood has stopped trying to make him sensible.
At the crossroads I stood singing in front of everyone, utterly drunk on the Beloved, and the crowd gathered and mocked, but I heard nothing; compose a doha about this blessed madness.
At the crossroads I sing, and the whole world laughs, and I am too drunk on Him to turn my head.
doha with a mirror and a shadow, a lover mad for the Beloved and happy
When I saw my shadow in the mirror I laughed and danced, I no longer cared who I seemed to be, mad as I am for the Beloved; write a doha on that gladly careless lover.
mirror, shadow, madness
I danced in front of the mirror in my room and saw my shadow dancing too, and I thought how mad I look, and how glad.
In the mirror I saw a madman, in the shadow a dancer, and neither cared what the world thought of the Beloved's.
The world calls it sense, I call it sleep; I woke in the Beloved's intoxication and cannot walk straight again.
drunk on the Beloved
My cousin has been walking around grinning for weeks like he has had too much to drink, and he says he is just in love with God.
a doha about the glorious madness of a lover who doesn't care what people think

Intoxicated with the Beloved I have left all sense behind and walk about like a drunkard, careless of how anyone judges me; please write a doha capturing that glorious, unashamed craziness of the lover.
doha with a beggar and a mirror, a lover mad for the Beloved and proud of it
The beggar and the mirror laugh together; I am the madman who traded all sense for one glance of the Beloved.
The beggar stands before the mirror and sees a king, and I stand before it and see a madman happy beyond reason, intoxicated with the Beloved; compose a doha about being mad in this way.
A beggar by the road looked into a mirror, laughed out loud and then shouted that he was drunk on God, and the crowd thought he was mad.
beggar, mirror, madman
careless lover
I do not care what anyone says about me anymore, I only know that the Beloved has made me wild, and my life is a happy folly; please write me a doha about lovers who are mad with devotion.
My friends think I have lost my mind since I started singing in the morning and giving my stuff away, but I have never felt saner.
doha about the madness of someone in love with God who ignores everyone
Call me a fool, call me mad, I have no ears for the world since the Beloved intoxicated me.
doha about a mad lover planting a seed at the cremation ground
Planting a seed by the cremation ground I laughed, mad with the Beloved, knowing that all of life is a game and he who is drunk on the Lord needs fear nothing; write a long doha for me.
seed, cremation ground, madman
The village madman sits at the cremation ground planting seeds and laughing, and the old people say he is the sanest of us all.
A seed in the cremation ground, a laugh on the lips, the madman plants his joy where others bury their dead.
I sit inside the cage of society's opinion, yet my heart burns with the fire of madness for the Beloved, and I will break out and dance while they watch; compose a doha about such wild love.
doha with a fire and a cage, a lover mad for God breaking free
fire and cage, mad lover
The cage of the world is shut but the fire inside breaks the bars; the madman dances out into the Lord's arms.
My family kept me in a cage of expectations but the fire of devotion got me out, and now I sing in the streets and they have stopped asking me to stop.
beads and cotton, discarded
I have lost the sense to count prayer beads and lost the shame to wear my cotton clean, because the Beloved made me wild; write a doha about how madness replaces the careful rituals of the proper.
I threw down my prayer beads and tore my cotton shawl; the Beloved's madness has made a ritual of my laughter.
My aunt counted her prayer beads for forty years in plain cotton, and then one day she threw them aside and started dancing, and nobody could stop her.
doha with prayer beads and cotton, a person mad for God and careless
jaggery and madness
doha with jaggery, a lover mad and drunk on divine sweetness
Jaggery is sweet, but the Beloved's wine is sweeter; I wander through the lanes mumbling nonsense, entirely mad.
Honey has no taste next to the madness of the Beloved's sweetness, and I wander about intoxicated with it, jaggery in my pocket and nonsense in my mouth; compose a doha on that wild bliss.
He eats jaggery all day and mumbles songs about God in the lanes, and the children call him mad and follow him anyway.
doha with a bitter gourd and a sword, a lover gone mad with the divine
A bitter gourd in my left, a sword in my right, I march mad into the world, for the Beloved has made me fearless.
Like a madman holding a bitter gourd in one hand and a sword in the other, I march into the lanes singing, and nobody dares stop me for I am mad with the Beloved; write a doha for me.
Our local madman walks about with a bitter gourd and an old sword singing devotional songs, and no one dares tease him.
bitter gourd, sword, madman
The snake coils, the bitter gourd stings the mouth, and the madman smiles, for the Beloved is everywhere.
A man in our village sat calmly next to a snake and ate a bitter gourd, saying he was too drunk on God to be afraid, and everyone called him crazy.
snake, bitter gourd, madman
They said I was mad to sit with the snake and drink the bitter gourd juice, but the Beloved has taken my fear and my sense away, and I smile; write a doha on this fearless, careless love.
doha with a snake and a bitter gourd, a lover mad for God and fearless
The musk deer runs mad for the scent, the singer plays his one-string lute; both of us are mad for the Beloved.
I play a one-string lute and run through the fields like a musk deer, and my friends say I have lost my mind, but I smile.
musk deer, one-string lute
doha with a musk deer and a one-string lute, a wild lover of the Beloved
The musk deer runs mad through the wild after the scent he carries, and I wander drunk with the one-string lute in my hand, mad for the Beloved; please compose a doha for this.
He left his house and his shop and now sits under the neem singing all day, drunk on God, and people say he has lost his mind.
I left the house, my name and my wealth; the madman of the Beloved needs no roof but His smile.
I left my house, my wife, my work, all to wander the streets singing for the Beloved, and they call me mad and turn their backs on me; compose a doha for the lover who ignores everyone.
doha about a man who left his house in madness for the Beloved
leaving the house, mad
My grandmother's loom-woven shawl flew behind her as she danced barefoot across the sand, singing out loud, and the village called her mad.
sand and loom shawl, madness
Barefoot on hot sand, my loom-woven shawl torn, I am mad, and the sky itself is my audience.
Walking on hot sand, with a loom-woven shawl flung over one shoulder, I shouted the Beloved's name to the sky, careless of all, and everyone said I was mad; please write a doha for me.
doha with sand and a loom, someone mad for the Beloved
I have no wish to be sensible, no desire to be careful, I want only to be mad for the Beloved and dance in the street like a fool and a lover, so write me a doha.
can u do a doha about a lover who is mad and happy about being mad
Let the sensible have their sense; I have the Beloved's madness and a heart that dances without a reason.
choosing madness
I've stopped caring about being proper, I just want to be silly and wild for what I love, and be called a fool for it.
They offered me milk and warned me of the snake, but I was too drunk on the Beloved to be afraid and laughed as I drank, a madman among the sane; compose a doha about this fearless madness.
milk and snake, fearless madness
A village madman once fed milk to a snake and sang to it, and while everyone ran he was just laughing, drunk on God.
doha with milk and a snake, a lover mad for God and not afraid
The snake bows to the madman and the milk turns to nectar, for he is drunk on the Beloved and fears nothing.
The beggar at the gate sings out the Beloved's name, utterly mad, and the passers-by cover their ears, but he does not care, for he is drunk on a wine no tavern sells; write a long doha for me.
the mad beggar
Our local beggar is happier than any of us, he sings all day, mumbles God's name and nobody can say if he's mad or holy.
doha about a beggar who is mad with divine love and ignores the crowd
The beggar sings, the people cover their ears, and he is drunk on a wine that no tavern has ever poured.
Shame fell first, then fame, and then the self; what remains is a madman and the Beloved.
doha for a lover mad for God, dropping shame and status
My college friend left everything for his path and he now laughs at everything we thought was important, like a person drunk in the morning.
madness of love
Please write a doha about the madness of someone so lost in love for God that they no longer care for fame, wealth, status or shame, and who dance without any embarrassment at all.
The bee loves the flower so mad that it forgets its way home, and my tongue is so mad with the Beloved's name that it cannot stop; compose a doha about that wild, drunken love.
bee, tongue, madness
doha with a bee and a restless tongue, a lover mad for the Beloved
The bee forgets the hive in the flower; my tongue forgets the world in the Beloved's name; both of us are mad.
My grandmother chants the name nonstop, her tongue never still, and hums like a bee, and the family has given up trying to quiet her.
doha about whirling in a mosque courtyard, mad for the Beloved
whirling at the mosque
They stare at the whirling madman in the mosque; he sees only the Beloved and spins as the world falls away.
In the mosque courtyard they stared as I whirled and laughed, but I was drunk and past all caring, mad with the Beloved, and let them think what they would; please write a doha on this blessed state.
A stranger started whirling in the courtyard of the mosque last Friday, arms open, laughing, and no one dared stop him.
My brother has been called a fool by half the village for the way he loves, but he is the happiest man I know.
The world mocks and the madman laughs, for what is mockery to one who has swallowed the Beloved?
doha about being a mad lover who is happy and doesn't mind mockery
Tell me in a doha how a lover gone mad with the Beloved no longer minds if the whole world mocks him, and how he is the happiest man alive despite everyone calling him a fool.
happy fool of love
A snake round his neck and a song on his lips, the madman is too drunk on the Beloved to feel fear.
The snake wrapped round his neck did not frighten the madman, for he was so full of the Beloved that he felt nothing, and the crowd ran off screaming; write a long doha of that careless intoxication.
A mad faqir came to our village with a snake around his neck singing love songs for God, and the children followed in awe.
doha with a snake around the neck of a lover mad with divine love
madman with a snake
doha with a door, a mad lover who knocks all night for the Beloved

Banging on the door of the Beloved in the middle of the night, I was called mad by the neighbors, but I banged again, drunk and shameless, till dawn; compose a doha about the lover who will not stop.
At midnight my son stood banging on the door shouting a bhajan, drunk on devotion, and the whole street opened their windows.
knocking at the door
doha about a mad lover who gives everything and doesn't care what people say
spinning, giving, mad
Spinning like a drunkard under the open sky, I gave away everything I owned, singing and laughing, and not one thing the world said touched me; please write a doha for the lover mad for the Beloved.
My uncle gave all his savings to a stranger, then spun around laughing, and the family thought he'd gone mad.
I gave away everything and spun until I fell; the world's opinion blew away, the Beloved's intoxication remained.
short doha about being crazy in love with God and not caring who sees
My mum says I used to be so careful about what people think, but now I'm a mad person singing out loud and she's weirdly proud.
I do not understand what they mean by shame; all I know is that when I think of the Beloved I laugh and cry and dance, and they call me mad for it, so write me a doha for that.
Shame and sense have both departed; the Beloved has settled in and the madman has no complaints.
no shame left
Our village madman talks to God out loud on the road and dances at any occasion, and the elders say he is the only one who is awake.
Mad at the funeral, mad at the wedding, the madman is drunk on a love that is neither gladness nor grief.
village madman

doha about the village madman who is drunk on the Beloved
doha with a water well and an ocean, a lover mad with divine love

water well, ocean, madness

reputation thrown away
short doha for a fool in love with God, past caring for opinion

doha with a bridge and a boat, a lover mad for the Beloved
bridge and boat, a madman

door, water well, mad cry

doha with a door and a water well, a mad shout for the Beloved

torn cotton, happy fool

doha with torn cotton, a happy fool mad for the Beloved

doha with an arrow and a spinning wheel, a man gone mad for the Lord

arrow and spinning wheel, madman
chat style doha, drunk on the Beloved, crazy and proud

confused with love
the lion and the madman

doha with a lion, a lover mad with divine love and past fear

doha with a beggar and a stone, a man mad and drunk for the divine

beggar on a stone

who is the madman?

doha about someone who is happily mad for God and laughs at their critics

mad and unashamed

My friends tease me that I'm crazy because I sing aloud and give my money away, but I've never been happier in my life.
doha about being a little crazy in love and not caring who knows
doha with a traveler dancing at a cremation ground, mad with God's love

traveler dancing, cremation ground

The lion looks at the madman and bows his head, for the Beloved looks out of both their eyes.

doha with a lion and a madman who sees the Beloved in everything
The lion behind the bars stares at the madman who walks up and bows to him, so drunk on the Beloved that he sees the Beloved in everything; compose a doha about this fearless madness.
bowing to the lion
losing all caution
I let go of my good name; the madman keeps no accounts, for the Beloved has paid every debt.
doha about a lover who lost all caution, mad for God

doha with a swan, a drifting lover mad for the Beloved

swan, mad drift

pearl and madness
doha with a pearl, a mad lover who dives into the Beloved

They tried to cure me, but the madman sang louder, for the Beloved had already taken his reason.
doha about being called crazy for loving God and loving it
they called me mad

doha with a cleric and a boat, a lover mad for God and singing

cleric, boat, mad singer

Mad, mad, mad for the Beloved, unashamed, unreasonable and happy, I want a long doha that celebrates a lover who has thrown away every rule of the world and lives free, wild with a single name.

totally mad
doha about a lover gone mad and loving it
My friend became so mad for God that he gave up his phone, his office and all his plans, and he says he has never been happier.
doha with a bee drunk on nectar, a lover drunk on the Beloved
The bee staggers drunk from flower to flower, and the madman staggers drunk through the world after the Beloved.
A bee drunk on nectar blunders about the garden and doesn't care what the flowers think, and I blunder about the world mad for the Beloved; write a doha about intoxicated love, please.
a drunken bee
I watched a bee stumble drunk through the flowers and thought of my uncle who stumbles through life just as happily, mad for God.

doha about how delicate this body is

fragile body, precious gift
body, borrowed and precious

doha on this body being temporary but valuable

traveler, touchstone, worn body

doha on the traveler's body slowly wearing out
body, cherish, not cling

doha on loving your body but not being proud of it

body, fire, inn

doha on how this body is just a temporary stay, fire inside it too

doha about how even a cleric's body grows old

cleric, aging body
thief, moth, fading body

fly, ageing body

doha on a body, the fly, and decay

bitter gourd, traveler, body

doha on body as a bitter gourd traveler?

doha on the palanquin and the bier, this body's two rides
bier, palanquin, this body's journey

weaver's loom, body woven

doha about this body as woven cloth from the weaver's loom

doha about the moon and my aging body

moon, waning body

spinning wheel, tired body

doha on this body as a spinning wheel winding down
doha on this body being strong as an elephant but with one door

elephant, door, body's end

doha on this body, a lotus on a seed of days
lotus, seed, body

doha on this body as a palace with a lock that does not hold

doha on this body: a bell and a needle

doha on this body as a river bank and the heron

beggar, salt, same body
doha on the beggar's body and this body of a king, salt

doha on a fly and sand, this body fading

cotton, body as clothing
doha about this body as cotton clothing for the soul

fragile, grateful for health

doha on how fragile this body is to illness
fly, body, temporary

doha on this body being temporary, with a fly

doha on cotton clothes and the date palm of this body

doha about this body as a churn, worn out by use

churn, body, tender care

doha about this body being a temple but not the god

body, temple, not the god
rare human body
doha about this body: precious but fading

Rare is this human frame, rarer still the wisdom to use it wisely before it fades.

doha on the swan leaving this body behind, beggar too

Compose a doha about this body as brief as a moth's life and as shifting as a cloud, lovely for a moment, and about caring tenderly for such a short-lived thing without grasping it.

gold, sandalwood, body

doha on gold and sandalwood, but this body is neither

doha on the moneylender who wants this body
moneylender, body, borrowed

doha on the mirror, shroud, and this body
mirror, shroud, body

doha on the chakor bird, a leaf, this body
chakor bird, leaf, body

doha on the shroud, prayer beads, and body
shroud, prayer beads, body

doha on the thief that steals our body bit by bit

thief, body, hidden loss

bitter gourd, body, outward show
doha on a bitter gourd body, nice outside

doha on feeling disconnected from my aching body
aching body, thank it

lotus, body, brief bloom

Looking at an old photo of my young self, I thought of how the lotus flowers in our pond bloom for only a few days.
doha on this body as a lotus, brief and lovely

body, nine gates
honestly just a doha about this body as a temporary dwelling place

tortoise, sword, body shell

The cleric at our fair stood in the open heat with a rope around his waist for the whole afternoon, took breaks behind the tent when no one looked, and took donations by evening. A doha?
cleric, rope, performance
Every Diwali my neighbour lights dozens of lamps outside his gate, invites everyone to see them, and puts out all but one the second the guests leave. Doha?
A doha about the one who lights a hundred lamps at the front for the neighbours to see, for his reputation of piety, while his heart remains dark, and the inner lamp that matters is not lit.
doha: lots of lamps for show, nothing lit inside
A hundred lamps burn at his gate, but inside him all is dark.
lamp, display, dark heart
He sits like a statue in prayer while the priest announces his piety, and the seed of true devotion has not even been sown.
A doha about the rich man who pays the priest to announce his donation and prayer loudly to the whole gathering, scattering seeds of grain for the cameras while his heart remains a barren field.
seed, priest, public piety
At our community meeting the priest called out the name of every donor and the rich man scattered seeds for the birds in front of the cameras, and went home and shooed away a hungry old man. A doha?
doha: priest announces the donation, rich guy throws seeds for photos, no real heart
The furnace roars in the potter's yard unseen; the beggar's show roars in the street to be seen.
A doha on the fake beggar who sits near the furnace outside the pilgrim's road and puts on a face of holiness, smeared with dust, to earn the coins of those who think he is a holy man.
furnace, beggar, performance
A beggar near the furnace on our road sits with his eyes closed in a holy pose when pilgrims pass, but chats with the shopkeepers when no one is there. A doha?
doha: fake beggar acting holy near the furnace for coins
cuckoo, dew, show
Our colony singer sings like a cuckoo at the event and weeps real dew when people applaud, but he is spiteful in the lane. A doha?
Dew on the cheek when the crowd is near, a cuckoo's song for the listener, and silence in the heart.
A doha on the performer with the voice of a cuckoo who sings devotional songs for the audience, with tears like morning dew when the applause begins, though nothing moves within.
doha: cuckoo voice and fake dew tears for the audience
ash, cuckoo, pretend
A doha on the one who smears ash on his body and sings sweetly like a cuckoo before a gathering, putting on a show of renunciation, while the real flame of devotion has never been lit in him.
Ash on his body and a cuckoo's tune on his lips, the stage is set but the heart is not.
The famous singer in our city smears ash on his forehead and sings like a cuckoo at every event, then charges a fortune and complains about the food. A doha?
doha: ash on the body and a cuckoo voice, all for the show
doha: fire ritual with the crow watching, people performing for the camera
fire, crow, performance
The fire is lit for the cameras, the crow watches from the wall, and the Lord is not invited.
At the public fire ceremony, the host kept looking at the cameras instead of the fire, and a crow stole the offering. A doha?
A doha on the fire ritual held in front of a crowd with elaborate gestures for the cameras, while a crow on the wall watches the false performance and takes the offering for itself.
A doha on the man carried in a palanquin up the mountain path in the robes of a pilgrim, who looks holy to the crowd but has never walked a single step of the penance himself.
doha: rich guy pilgrimage in a palanquin up a mountain, not a real pilgrim
palanquin, mountain, pilgrim
The politician went up the mountain in a palanquin carried by four men to be photographed as a pilgrim, and complained about the cold. Could you write a doha?
Carried on a palanquin up the mountain, he calls it a pilgrimage and the bearers call it work.
holiness for an audience
doha: people who pray only when someone is watching
My colleague closes his eyes and chants whenever the boss walks by, and the rest of the time talks about stock prices. Doha for him?
A doha on the person who prays only when watched, folding his hands the moment a visitor arrives, and forgetting the Lord the moment the visitor leaves, because his audience was never the Lord.
His prayers begin with the audience and end with the applause.
Seeds of charity thrown where the cameras can see them, and the harvest he wants is applause.
A doha on the donor who scatters a seed here and there before the crowd with a grand announcement, wanting his name sung, and who never plants anything that will grow when he is not looked at.
doha: donating a seed of kindness with cameras around, wanting praise
A man donated blankets at our colony event with a banner of his own face, and a seed of kindness is not hidden anymore. A doha?
seed, charity for show

A doha about the person who posts photographs of every act of worship and charity on the internet, counting likes as blessings, while the real act remains forgotten and the Lord is not the one liking the post.
posting piety online
doha: posting your prayers on social media for likes
My cousin posts a photo of himself praying every morning with a caption about gratitude, but he has not spoken to his mother in a year. A doha?
Prayer posted for the likes, a heart left on mute.
A doha on the proud man with the roar of a lion who recites holy words so everyone can hear his tongue's devotion, but whose devotion stops when the audience goes home.
doha: lion roars about his piety and the tongue says holy things for the crowd
lion, tongue, show
The lion of piety roars from the tongue and not from the heart.
The loud man at our gathering who holds forth like a lion about devotion speaks sweetly from his tongue to everyone's face, and cheats them in business. Could you write a doha?
The swan is white by nature; the washerman whitens the cloth for the crowd.
A doha about the washerman who dresses in a swan's white and stands in public with a holy face, looking pure to the crowd, though the dirt of his own mind has never been washed.
doha: washerman in swan white acting holy in public
swan, washerman, show
The washerman's son wears all white and acts serious at the public events, as if he were a swan among sparrows, but he's the first to gossip. A doha?
stone, forehead mark, display
doha: holy forehead mark, stone idol, performance for the crowd
My boss makes a show of kneeling in front of a stone image and applying a forehead mark whenever clients are around. A doha?
A forehead mark for the crowd, a stone to bow to, and no one to bow to in the heart.
A doha on the one who puts on the bright forehead mark and kneels before a stone idol in public with a loud flourish, so that all may see how pious he is, but never kneels in private.
He wears his holiness like a good coat, for show and when the weather asks.
holy for the crowd
A doha on the person who puts on holiness in front of the watchers as one puts on a coat, and takes it off the moment the guests go, wearing a different face in private.
A man in our locality acts devout only in front of the elders and the rest of the time is a gambler. Could you write a doha?
doha: acting holy just for the people who watch
The moth burns without an audience, and the pious burns with one.
An actor in our drama group played a devout moth in a play, and the audience wept, but offstage he is always pretending. Doha idea?
moth, devotion on stage
A doha on the moth that gives its life for the light without a single watcher, and the man who does everything for show, giving nothing to the Lord unless a crowd is present.
doha: the moth circles the flame for love, not for the crowd, unlike people
doha about people doing charity only when they get their name on a plaque
A name on a plaque; a gift weighed in applause.
donor's plaque
A doha about the man who gives to the poor only if his name is carved on the wall for all to read, as if the Lord could only read marble and not the hidden hand.
The family that donated a bench to the park insisted on a big plaque with their name on it, and yet they haven't spoken to the family next to them in ten years. A doha?
He fed the crowd milk and wanted their praise; the poor child at his gate got no milk at all.
milk, charity, show
doha: giving out milk for the cameras, nothing for the poor kid at home
The mayor had milk distributed at the fair with his posters on every can, but the milkman who works every day is still unpaid. Doha?
A doha on the donor who distributes milk to the crowd in front of the cameras with his name on every cup, and walks past the hungry child at his own gate without a thought.
A doha on the parrot in a palace, taught to say holy words in front of guests, which the king shows off as a mark of his devotion, though neither the parrot nor the king knows what the words mean.
The rich family's parrot, kept in a palace-like mansion, recites prayers on cue when guests arrive, and the family brags about it. A doha for them?
In the palace the parrot recites the holy names for guests, and the master takes the praise.
parrot, palace, show
doha: the parrot in the palace says holy words for guests
The thief in my neighbourhood put up a big religious banner on his house and invites everyone to ceremonies, while he plans the next robbery. A doha?
The house of the thief is hung with holy flags, and the neighbours are invited to bow.
A doha on the thief who decorates his house with holy symbols and invites the whole street to his prayers, so that no one will suspect him of anything while his mind plans the next theft.
doha: thief with a holy house, looks pious, is not
thief, house, holy banner
piety for an audience
At the meeting, a man stood up and began to cry about his devotion, turned to see whether everyone was watching, and then cried harder. Doha for that?
He wept in public and watched who was watching.
write a doha: crying in front of people to look devout
A doha on the one who weeps and trembles in the presence of onlookers when he speaks of the Lord, whose tears dry up the moment he is alone, and who checks the crowd to see if it is moved.
At the cremation ground, the man who owns three factories rang a bell for everyone to hear as a gesture of respect, and then complained that the pyre was too small. A doha?
bell, cremation ground, show
He rings the bell at the cremation ground, so all can hear; what he hears himself is only the sound.
doha: ringing the bell at the cremation ground just so people notice him
A doha on the mourner who rings a bell very loudly at the cremation ground, performing his grief and devotion for the crowd, though his thoughts are on the will and the property of the dead.
My aunt does her puja on the balcony facing the street so the neighbours can see how devoted she is, while she skips it on rainy days. A doha?
She prays on the balcony facing the road, and on rainy days the Lord waits indoors.
balcony prayer
A doha on the person who performs his devotion at a spot where the maximum number of people will see him, and relocates the whole rite out of sight whenever the crowd is gone.
doha: praying where everyone can see
A doha on the man who sits in a famous pose of meditation on the road with a signboard announcing his silence, and whose eyes open the moment anyone offers a coin or a camera.
doha: meditating with a signboard
Eyes closed for the crowd, open for the coin.
meditation for coins
A man near the station sits in meditation with a sign saying 'silent for world peace' and opens his eyes every time someone drops a coin. Doha?
A doha on the beggar who dresses as a holy man and sits at the roadside with a sacred expression, because he has learned that people give more to piety than to need, and his holiness is a trade.
The beggar learns to look holy, for holiness sells better than hunger.
A beggar at the corner learned to chant loudly when nicely dressed people walk by and goes quiet when the street is empty. A doha for him?
beggar, holy act
doha: beggar who puts on a holy face for more money
A thread round the neck of the holy, a tree planted for the press, and no shade for anyone.
thread, tree, photo opportunity
A doha on the leader who ties a holy thread and plants a tree in front of the press cameras, and never waters it, and whose piety lasts exactly as long as the photograph.
The politician planted a tree and tied a thread round it for the cameras and never came back. The tree is dead now. Can you write a doha?
doha: tree planting with a thread tied for the camera, never watered
A doha on the one who dresses in the finest cotton of simple living and speaks of detachment before an admiring audience, while his closets are full and his heart is full of desire.
The simplest cotton for the public eye; for the private life, silk.
My neighbour wears rough cotton clothes in public and brags about his simple life, and I saw his closet full of expensive imports. Doha?
cotton, simple living show
doha: wearing simple cotton for show
A bridge of promises built for the cameras, and a net of words to catch the votes.
doha: bridge opening ceremony and net of promises, fake piety
A doha on the leader who opens a bridge with a grand prayer ceremony and holy words, casting a net of promises over the crowd, though the bridge is shoddy and his piety is only for the occasion.
bridge, net, ceremony
The official blessed the new bridge with a loud prayer ceremony, and spread a net of promises to the crowd, and the bridge collapsed in six months. A doha?
The potter in our colony is praised for his devotion at every festival, because he makes beautiful clay idols and plays a one-string lute for the crowd, but he is cruel to his apprentices. A doha?
A doha on the potter who shapes clay with great flourish before an audience and plays a one-string lute to show his devotion, though his true work is done in silence, and the show is for applause.
doha: potter and clay and a one-string lute, all for the audience
potter and clay, lute, show
He shapes the clay for the crowd, plays the one-string lute for the crowd, and for himself plays nothing.
A doha on the donor who hands out jaggery sweets in public with a loud announcement of his generosity, wanting every cheek to praise him, though the real sweetness of giving lies in doing it quietly.
jaggery, charity for show
doha: giving out jaggery and posting it everywhere
My uncle distributed jaggery sweets at the bus stop and made sure a photographer was there. He hasn't given a rupee to his own brother. Doha?
He gave jaggery to the crowd, but the sweetness was meant for himself.
In our colony the man who runs the prayer group likes to hold it right outside, so everybody sees him, and tells the neighbours about how many people attend. A doha?
He holds the prayers where the eyes are, so that the Lord may be an afterthought.
prayer group for status
doha: holding prayers in public for status
A doha on the one who organises public prayers and festivals mainly to be seen at the front, seating himself in the centre, taking the garland, and leaving before the real work begins.
holy gestures, empty heart
doha about showing off how holy you are
Folded hands, bowed head, and a heart standing straight and proud.
My friend folds his hands and bows his head dramatically when entering any room with religious people, but is rude to waiters. A doha for him?
A doha on the person who knows every gesture of piety, the folded hands, the bowed head, the lowered eyes, and performs them nicely, but who has never once lowered his pride.
He bows with his body for the world, and keeps his heart upright for himself.
doha: bowing for the crowd
bowing for show
Our local leader bows deeply to every elder at the function and then calls them fools in the car. Doha?
A doha on the man who bows deeply to every important person at a gathering and holds his head high among the humble, as though respect were something to be spent where it brings a return.
potter and clay, public show
doha: potter spinning clay for tourists, claiming it's his holy work
The potter at the heritage village makes a big show of worship before working, for the tourists, and uses a machine at night. A doha?
A doha on the potter who shapes clay in front of tourists with a flourish, saying it is a holy craft handed down for ages, while the work he sells is machine made and the holiness is a story.
The potter shapes the clay in front of tourists, with a speech about holiness he does not believe.
doha: the saint who loves cameras more than God
He dims the lights of his own devotion to shine in the cameras' glare.
saint for cameras
A doha on the holy man who arranges the camera angles before beginning his sermon, adjusts his robe for the photographs, and speaks of humility in a voice meant to carry across the crowd.
The visiting preacher checked the lighting and camera angles before his talk on humility, and posed for ten minutes afterwards. What would Kabir say?
doha about those who pray to be seen praying
They kneel where the light is best, and bend as the crowd turns.
My neighbour always chooses the front row at religious events and turns around to see who has come in. A doha for him?
A doha on the ones who choose their place of prayer by where the crowd is thickest, kneeling in the best light and glancing around to see who is watching, as though the audience were the Lord.
praying to be seen

A doha on the musk deer which carries the scent within it, quietly, never boasting, and the man who stands before a stone image in the public eye to announce his devotion to the world, with no fragrance within.
doha: musk deer carries scent quietly, human holiness is stone cold for the audience
The musk deer wears its fragrance within; the man wears his holiness on the stone for all to see.
A man in our area bows before a stone idol loudly when the neighbours pass, and a musk deer in the nearby sanctuary wanders silently, carrying its fragrance within. A doha for the contrast?
musk deer, stone, show
doha: palanquin and a lamp lit for a photo, no real devotion
lamp, palanquin, show
The lamp is lit for the photograph, the palanquin is carried for the crowd, and the Lord sits unseen.
At my cousin's reception he arrived in a palanquin and lit a lamp for a ceremony for exactly the time it took to take photos. A doha?
A doha on the groom or the leader who is carried in a palanquin and lights a ceremonial lamp in front of the cameras, and who has no thought for the Lord or the guests beyond the photograph.
devotion as theatre
A doha on the person who stages his devotion as a theatre performance, with costumes, music, and applause, forgetting that the Lord is not an audience member and was never fooled by costumes.
Our annual religious event has turned into a competition of costumes and drama, and the real prayer is lost. A doha?
doha: religion has become a drama
The stage is set and the costumes are ready; only the Lord has not been told.
The man who sits in the front row at every sermon never listens, he is busy scanning the crowd to see who is noticing him. A doha?
A doha on the man who appears in the front row at every sermon and nods vigorously at the speaker, to be noticed, and sleeps through the wisdom in the speaker's words.
doha about nodding in front-row seats to be noticed
front row piety
He nods at the words he does not hear, for the eyes he hopes will see.
The date palm bears its fruit high and quiet, while the man at its foot proclaims his devotion to the passing crowd.
A doha on the date palm that stands tall and gives sweet fruit without announcing it, and the man who stands under it proclaiming his holiness to all passers by, but who bears no fruit.
doha: date palm gives fruit quietly, people give loudly
date palm, quiet giving
Under the date palm in our village sits a man who tells everyone he gives to charity, though no one has ever seen what he gives. Doha?
doha: the yogi poses for tourists
A doha on the yogi who has learned to strike a pose of deep meditation whenever tourists arrive, and to relax the moment the buses leave, because his stillness is a performance for coin.
Still as a yogi's statue for the buses, and a talker when they leave.
The yogi at the ghat meditates dramatically as the tourist launches come in and chats happily when they leave. What would Kabir say?
yogi, posing
crow, net, pretending
The crow sits in holy silence over the net, but his eye measures the feast.
doha: crow acting like a saint beside a net of grain
A doha on the crow who sits in a saintly posture near the net, as though he has renounced all grain, but whose only thought is how to take the bait without being caught.
A man at the grain stalls sits meditating beside the net, and a crow sat next to him, and I could not tell which one was after the grain. A doha?
A doha on the skeleton of a rotting reputation, hidden behind a lavish ceremony held on the bridge to the holy place, where the host pretends to piety while the whole town knows his secrets.
A skeleton in the cupboard, a prayer on the bridge, a mask on the face.
doha: skeleton and a bridge and pretending to be holy
The man who led the ceremony at the bridge opening has a skeleton in his closet that everyone knows about, and still he speaks of purity. A doha?
skeleton, bridge, pretence
The speaker at the event used the sweetest, most holy phrases, and then insulted the cook in the kitchen. His tongue knew which audience was in front of it. A doha?
tongue, holy words, audience
A doha on the tongue that speaks sweet and holy words only when someone important is listening, and turns sour and sharp in the kitchen, so that the speech belongs to the audience and not the heart.
doha: sweet-talking holy words to the audience, nasty tongue backstage
The tongue is sweet in the hall and sharp in the kitchen.
judging others publicly
A doha on the person who stands in judgement over every other pilgrim, correcting their rituals and pointing out their flaws in a loud voice, to display his own knowledge of holiness to the audience.
He points to the dust on others' feet to hide the dust on his own.
At the gathering, one man spent the entire time correcting everyone else's way of worshipping, loudly, to impress the elders. A doha?
doha: judging others publicly to look holy
A doha on the person who gives to the poor in the morning on the steps of the holy place before everyone, and cheats the same poor in his store in the afternoon, his piety as short as the morning.
The grocer gives out free food at the holy place every morning for the crowd to see, and in the afternoon he sells spoiled grain. A doha?
morning charity, afternoon cheat
doha: fake charity in the morning, cheating in the afternoon
Charity in the morning for the crowd, short weight in the afternoon for the poor.
doha: ocean of show, jaggery of piety, sweetness only on the surface
ocean, jaggery, display
A doha on the one whose piety is an ocean of display, with waves of ceremony and speeches, but is thin as a coat of jaggery on a bitter pill, sweet only to the eye.
At the grand event by the ocean, the host gave out jaggery sweets to everyone and a long speech on devotion, but his staff say he has not paid wages for months. A doha?
An ocean of display and a lump of jaggery of piety; sweet on the surface, bitter beneath.
Write a doha about a touchstone that shows true metal only under pressure, as sorrow shows who truly remembers God, since men call on Him in suffering but forget Him in the ease of good times.
touchstone, remember God always
doha about how we only pray when things go wrong, touchstone idea
When my business collapsed I felt tested like metal on a touchstone and started praying every morning, and now that it has recovered I realised last week that I haven't said a word to God in months.
In sorrow the touchstone finds the heart bright with prayer; in joy it finds the same heart dull and forgetful.
I noticed that I only call my mother when I need money or comfort, and when things are good I forget to call for weeks, and it made me think about how I treat God too.
remember Him in comfort
doha about only praying when life is hard and forgetting when it's good
Please write a doha about the human habit of calling on the Lord in suffering and forgetting Him in comfort, and say that if we remembered Him always, in good times too, no suffering would ever come.
In grief all lips whisper His name; in gladness the lips grow dumb. Remember Him in both, O heart.
The night before the exam I prayed hard under the stars and sent a fly out the window with a vow to be devoted forever, yet by the next week I had forgotten all my promises.
stars and fly doha about only remembering God when you're in trouble
Under the stars the sufferer prays; in daylight, like a fly, he buzzes off and forgets.
stars, fly, remember in comfort
Write a doha about a man who prays to the Lord under the stars when in pain and forgets Him when the fly of daily pleasure buzzes around him, and teach him to remember always.
house and sun doha - we remember God in trouble but forget Him when happy
Please write a doha about a man whose house is full of comfort under the bright sun, who forgets God entirely, and who calls out to Him only when sorrow darkens the roof over his head.
house, sun, forgetting God
In the sunlit house of pleasure we forget Him; in the dark of sorrow we cry His name.
When the sun is bright and my house is full of guests, I forget my prayers completely, but the day the power failed and a family illness hit, I was on my knees.
furnace, well, remember always
In the furnace of sorrow all call the Lord; at the well of ease none remember to give thanks.
During the hardest year of my life in the furnace of illness I prayed constantly, and by the well of recovery I stopped, which made me ashamed.
Write a doha about the furnace of suffering in which all remember the Lord and the deep well of comfort at which they forget Him, urging us to remember Him in both.
furnace and well doha about calling on God in trouble but forgetting Him when all is fine
The fly buzzes round the mosque in happy hours; in grief it settles, trembling, at the Lord's feet.
My friend skips the mosque on every happy occasion, but when his father fell ill, the fly-infested hospital corridor saw him praying more fervently than anyone.
fly and mosque doha - people remember God in pain and forget him in joy
fly, mosque, forgetting God
Compose a doha about a man who never visits the mosque in his happy years, though flies of pleasure swarm around him, but runs there in sorrow, and teach him to remember always.
My brother promised God he'd change if the boat he was sailing in survived the storm, and now that he is safe on shore he has already broken every promise.
In the storm, the boat's captain prayed; on the calm sea, he forgot the Lord who calmed it.
boat, storm, forgotten prayer
Please write a doha about a sailor who prays loudly on a sinking boat, vows great vows, and then, once safe in harbour, forgets both vows and the Lord who saved him.
boat doha about people praying only when in danger
remember Him in joy
In sorrow all remember Him, in joy none; if one remembered Him in joy, why would sorrow come at all?
Write a doha for a person who prays only in trouble, reminding him that the Lord should be remembered in both pain and happiness, and that the one who remembers Him in joy will rarely know sorrow.
Looking back at my own life, I see that every time I turned to God was a crisis, and in every calm stretch I did not think of Him once.
doha: people only remember God when suffering, why not remember him when happy
Compose a doha about a traveler who prays on a lonely road in the dark and a physician who forgets the Lord amid his wealth, warning both that remembering God only in trouble is a poor habit.
traveler and physician doha - we only remember God in suffering
traveler, physician, remember always
The traveler prays on the dark road, the physician forgets in his comfortable room; remember Him in the light too.
The physician at our clinic treats dying patients who all beg God for help, and as a fellow traveler through life he admits he forgot Him entirely in his own healthy years.
The philosopher's stone gives treasure, the cuckoo sings in spring; yet the heart remembers God only in winter.
philosopher's stone, cuckoo, forgetting God
When the cuckoo sang in the good season of my life, I forgot all about God; it was only in the winter of my troubles that I looked for a philosopher's stone of faith.
philosopher's stone and cuckoo doha about people only remembering God when in pain
Please write a doha about the cuckoo that sings merrily in the good season and a seeker with a philosopher's stone who forgets the Lord in luck and remembers Him only in sorrow.
In the days of milk and honey no one remembers Him; in the days of famine all lips cry His name.
The baby's milk was running low and I prayed with all my heart that we would manage, and then once the money came through I never thought to say thanks.
milk doha about remembering God only when things are hard
milk, remembering God always
Write a doha about a household that has milk in plenty and forgets the Lord, and that calls on Him only when the milk runs dry and sorrow arrives, and teach them to remember always.
palanquin and cremation ground doha - people remember God only when death or grief comes
Compose a doha about a man who rides in a grand palanquin at his wedding and forgets the Lord, and who stands weeping at the cremation ground for his loved one and calls on Him only then.
At the wedding palanquin no one thinks of Him; at the cremation ground every lip calls out His name.

At my brother's wedding, as he rode in the palanquin, nobody thought of God for a minute, but at the cremation ground where we mourned my uncle two weeks later, everyone prayed as if their lives depended on it.
palanquin, cremation ground, forgetting God
When my tongue was swollen with fever I kept begging God to cure me, and the moment the sandalwood balm worked I went right back to my old careless life.
sandalwood and tongue doha about asking God for help in pain and forgetting Him in comfort
sandalwood, tongue, remember always
Please write a doha about a tongue that calls the Lord's name only when pain makes it cry, and forgets it in the fragrant ease of sandalwood and comfort, and teach it to remember in both states.
In pain the tongue cries out His name; in the scent of sandalwood it falls silent and forgets.
Write a doha about a man who rides high in a palanquin and forgets the Lord, until a snake of misfortune bites him and he calls out to God in pain, and teach him to remember in good times too.
palanquin, snake, forgetting God
My cousin, who showed off in a palanquin at his wedding and never prayed, was bitten by a snake on his honeymoon and has been praying every day since.
In the palanquin of pleasure the Lord is forgotten; when the snake of sorrow bites, the whole heart cries His name.
palanquin and snake doha - we only remember God when something bad happens
The parrot repeats the Name when the master is sad, and goes mute when his forehead mark of success is fresh: so does the heart.
Compose a doha about a parrot that speaks the Lord's name when its owner weeps, and says nothing when he is merry with the forehead mark of success, showing how we forget God in comfort.
parrot, forehead mark, forgetting God
parrot and forehead mark doha about remembering God only in sadness
My uncle wears a big forehead mark and raises a parrot that recites God's name, but he is only devout when ill, and the parrot has learned that too.
The date palm in our yard bears fruit once a year, and my father only prays during the lean months, never during the harvest, which my mother thinks is ungrateful.
In the shade of the date palm of plenty, the heart forgets; in the desert of need it remembers.
Write a doha about a date palm heavy with fruit under which men forget the Lord, and a barren desert where they remember Him, and teach us to keep Him in mind at all times.
date palm doha - we only call out to God when things are hard
date palm, remembering in plenty
winnowing fan, remember Him
winnowing fan doha about forgetting God in good times

mountain doha about people only turning to God in danger and forgetting Him afterward

mountain, forgetting God

short doha about how we only pray in hard times

pain, pleasure, remember Him

crow, ungrateful heart
crow doha about people remembering God only when in need

sorrow remembers, joy forgets
doha: remember God in good times too, not only in trouble

Whenever my father's house was full of guests and celebration, he never mentioned God, but the night the family faced a crisis he began chanting without stopping.
house, remembered in sorrow
house doha - we only remember God when it's too late or we're hurting
I want a doha about the way people cry to the Lord in times of suffering but forget Him in the good times, and about the wisdom of remembering Him in both, so that no suffering ever has to come.
Sorrow teaches the knees to bend; comfort teaches them to forget. Keep them bent, O heart.
forgetting God in comfort

doha about people only praying in hard times and forgetting in good times

Caged in debt, the heart cries to the Lord; freed by wealth, it forgets who freed it.
Compose a doha about a man caged by a moneylender's debts who cries to the Lord in despair, and who forgets Him entirely when the debt is cleared and comfort returns.
cage, moneylender, forgot God
fire, ash, remember always
In the fire of pain all call upon the Lord; in the ash of comfort, none remember the flame.
fire and ash doha about calling God in trouble and forgetting in good times
Please write a doha about the fire of suffering that makes people cry out to the Lord, and the cool ash of comfort in which they forget Him, and urge them to remember Him always.
After the fire damaged our shop, my father prayed all night, but once everything was rebuilt and only ash remained of the memory, he stopped completely.
doha about how we remember God in pain but not in comfort
Compose a doha for a person who spends joyful days in forgetfulness and sorrowful days in prayer, teaching that to remember the Lord in both is the only wise way to live.
pain remembers, joy forgets
When suffering knocks, we kneel; when pleasure comes, we rise and forget why we knelt.
It struck me at my friend's funeral that when life is easy, none of us even think about what matters, and we only wake up when something terrible happens.
Write a doha about a bridge that people cross in prayer when sorrow comes and burn behind them when comfort returns, forgetting the Lord who carried them over.
bridge, ungrateful memory
When I crossed the old bridge into the hospital to see my sick mother I prayed with all my heart, but on the way out after her recovery I did not give thanks once.
We cross the bridge of sorrow in prayer, and burn it once we reach the shore of comfort.
bridge doha about forgetting God after he helps you
Please write a doha about a fly that lands on honey and forgets everything else, as men in comfort forget the Lord, only to remember Him when they are stuck and struggling.
During a calm and happy year, I became so caught up in my pleasures like a fly in honey that I forgot to pray at all, until a shock reminded me.
fly, honey, forgetting God
fly doha - we forget God in comfort and call him in trouble
The fly sits on the honey of pleasure and is stuck; then it cries to the Lord in pain.
Compose a doha about how the Lord is forgotten in the days of ease and remembered in the days of pain, and about the truth that those who keep Him in mind through both will be spared much suffering.
Pain makes a prayer of the lips; pleasure makes a stranger of the Lord.
When I was fired I turned to God and when I was hired again I forgot Him within a week, and I only noticed this pattern yesterday while sitting in the garden.
doha about remembering God in both joy and sorrow
sorrow prays, joy forgets

cloth sheet and salt doha about crying to God in suffering and forgetting him in comfort
Wrapped in a cloth sheet of sorrow, the heart tastes salt tears and calls on the Lord; in ease it forgets.
Write a doha about a person wrapped in a cloth sheet of sorrow, whose tears taste of salt as he calls on the Lord, and who forgets Him once comfort returns, and teach him to remember always.
During the weeks of my mother's illness I wept into a cloth sheet and prayed constantly, but once she recovered and life resumed its salt and spice, I forgot all about God.
On the days when things go badly I find myself praying for hours, and on days when everything goes smoothly I do not give God one thought, and it feels hypocritical.
Only in pain do we call upon Him; in pleasure the Lord is left waiting at the gate of memory.
I would like a doha that says the Lord should be remembered in joy as much as in suffering, and that most people only turn to Him when misfortune strikes, which is why misfortune keeps coming.
remember Him in joy
short doha about only praying in hard times
Last week at the hospital I begged God for my father's recovery, but I noticed during the good times that I had hardly spoken to Him at all, and I felt ashamed.
Write a doha about a man who prays to the Lord only in the days of misfortune and neglects Him in the days of fortune, and teach him to keep God in his heart through both.
forgetting God in good times
doha about the shame of only praying when you need something from God
In sorrow I called Him Father; in joy I forgot His name. Forgive me, Lord, and keep me mindful.
The moon forgets the darkness when it shines, and men forget the Lord in the brightness of luck.

moon doha about forgetting God when things are good
Compose a doha about the moon that shines in the night sky and forgets its dark side, as men in the brightness of fortune forget the Lord they cried to in the darkness of sorrow.
moon, forgetting God
musk deer, forgetting God
musk deer doha about only remembering God when suffering
The musk deer runs frantic in pain; in ease, it forgets the scent of the Lord inside it.
Please write a doha about a musk deer that races through the woods in terror, calling on the Lord, and forgets Him the moment the danger passes and ease returns.
My neighbour was terrified when his musk deer-skin rug was stolen and turned to prayer, but once it was returned he went back to ignoring God.
Write a doha for the person who has had comfort for a long time and forgotten to pray, warning him that suffering is the Lord's reminder to those who remember Him only in pain.
I've been so busy and comfortable lately that I stopped my daily prayer, and my wife said that it takes a crisis to remind me, and she's right.
remember Him daily
doha about remembering God every day, not only when something goes wrong
If you forget Him in comfort, sorrow comes to remind you; remember Him now and spare yourself.
joy forgets, grief remembers
When I was at my lowest I prayed every hour, and now that I am comfortable I find my mind full of everything but God, and it bothers me.
Compose a doha about how people in great suffering turn to the Lord and in great happiness turn away from Him, and how a wise person keeps Him in mind at all times, equal in joy and in pain.
doha about how happiness makes us forget God
Happiness is the wine that makes the heart forget; sorrow is the sobering that brings it back to the Lord.
The cuckoo sings in the spring of plenty; in the autumn of need, it cries out to the Lord.
My cuckoo-loving grandmother says everyone is a singer in good times and a supplicant in bad, and the same goes for how we speak to God.
cuckoo doha - we remember God in hard times but forget in good
cuckoo, forgetting God
Write a doha about a cuckoo that sings in spring and goes silent in autumn, as people sing God's praises in sorrow but forget Him in the spring of their good fortune.
At the crossroads the thief calls on the Lord in fear; once he is safe, he returns to his thieving ways.

thief, crossroads, forgot God
Please write a doha about a thief at a crossroads who prays loudly to the Lord when the crowd closes in, and forgets Him the moment he escapes, as men forget God when their trouble passes.
thief and crossroads doha about people remembering God only in danger
tortoise, forgetting God
Write a doha about a tortoise that pulls into its shell when danger comes and forgets everything else once safe, as men turn to the Lord in danger and forget Him in the ease that follows.

My pet tortoise hides in its shell the moment I come near and wanders around carelessly the rest of the day, and it reminded me of how I treat prayer.
tortoise doha about running to God in trouble and ignoring Him otherwise
The sword is drawn and the net is cast; in fear we pray, in safety we forget.
Compose a doha about a man hunted by enemies with sword and net, who prays loudly to the Lord for deliverance and forgets Him entirely once he has escaped.

sword and net doha - people only call on God when in danger
sword, net, forgetting God

doha about remembering God when life is good, not just when it's bad
Be as devoted in sunshine as in the storm, O heart; the Lord is the same in both.
Write a doha reminding people that God is the same in pain and in pleasure, and that the wise person remembers Him in both, not just when suffering comes calling.
remember God always

peacock and traveler doha about forgetting God when happy and praying when scared
peacock, traveler, forgetting God

rainbird, oil press, remember Him

rainbird and oil press doha - we only call God when it's hard

remember Him, joy and sorrow

Equal in gain and loss, equal in song and tears, the lover keeps the Lord in mind.
Compose a doha for the person who prays fervently in suffering and forgets in pleasure, advising him to hold the Lord in his heart equally in joy and sorrow, and be free of both.
doha: remember God the same in good times and bad
fish doha about only turning to God when in trouble

fish, forgetting God

thread, remember Him always

dew, tree, remember Him

dew and tree doha about remembering God only in hard times

doha about how suffering makes us remember God and happiness makes us forget
pain brings prayer

cloth sheet doha about praying in hardship and forgetting in comfort
cloth sheet, remember always

diamond, forgetting God

diamond doha about remembering God only when things go wrong

spinning wheel, wicked person
hey doha pls on cruel people: they spin the spinning wheel of lies all day and you get tangled, so how to stay clear

wicked man, leaf

wicked people, stay away

yo doha on why being nice to evil people doesn't work
avoid the evil

doha idea: dont argue with cruel people, they enjoy the fight

stone-hearted, wicked
doha pls: some people are like stone, nothing you say moves them, just leave them

evil people, stay safe

doha pls: a cruel man grinds the weak like a grindstone, stay away from his mill

grindstone, wicked, cruel

heron, hypocrite

bully, avoid

doha idea about how to handle a bully without becoming one

doha pls: some people are like fake guides, they lead the traveler to the robber's place, so check before you follow

doha pls: even the philosopher's stone can't fix a wicked person, so don't try

philosopher's stone, wicked touch

doha pls on how not to get dragged into other people's evil schemes

wicked, fear not
doha pls: wicked people look powerful but they're really scared inside

envious ones, ignore

traveler, wicked company
doha pls: if the road is full of robbers it's better to wait than to travel with the wicked

doha pls: wicked people always get caught eventually, so be patient
