The bird in a cage boasts of its lineage while it cannot soar; so does the man who boasts of his caste.
doha: cage and caste, pride of birth is just another prison
A doha about the man who sits in a golden cage of caste vanity, thinking he sits on a throne, unable to see the bars, while the world outside is open to all who are free.
The shroud has no caste, the scales have no caste; at the last weighing all are equal.
shroud, scales, caste
doha: shroud and scales, in the end everyone is weighed the same

A doha on how a shroud covers the rich and the poor with the same white cloth, and the scales of judgement weigh deeds and not birth, so that the caste proud will find themselves lighter than the humble.

At my grandfather's funeral the whole village came, high and low caste together, the same shroud was put on him as on the poor man who died that week, and the doctor said scales would weigh them alike. Doha?
caste, untouchable lie
A boy in my school was not allowed to sit with us because of his surname, and the teacher said nothing. I want something for him
If the touch of one man can pollute, how pure can the maker be who made all?
doha pls on how caste prejudice is wrong
Compose a verse on a world where a man is called unclean by birth and kept apart from others, though the Creator made him with the same hands that made the proudest of the high born.
At the wedding feast the lower caste cook was praised for the food, but guests would not let him sit with them, though a fly landed on everyone's plate and dew fell on all roofs equally. A doha?
A fly sits on the king's plate and the pauper's alike, and dew falls on both roofs; who made the difference?
Compose a doha on the fly and the dew, which treat every man alike whatever his caste, landing on the high and the low in the same way, showing that purity is not a gift of birth.
doha: fly and dew don't care about caste, why do we
fly, dew, caste
I read a news item about a family that was refused service at a restaurant for their caste, and I thought of the ocean, which takes all the streams equally. Could you write something?

A doha on the ocean, which welcomes every stream, large and small, clean and muddy, high or low, without asking their origin, and so teaches us that the heart that is wide has no room for caste pride.
The ocean gathers every stream and asks no questions; why is your heart narrower than the sea?
ocean, birth snobbery
doha: ocean accepts all, but people judge each other's caste
Sand from the high dunes and the low alike, once crushed together, cannot be told apart.
sand, one caste
A doha on the grains of sand, some from the highest dune and some from the lowest, that mingle in the wind until no one can say which grain came from where, as all humanity is of one making.
doha about sand mixing together like all people really do
At the beach, my kids built a castle from sand and when I said, 'this grain is from the high dune and this from the low', they laughed. It reminded me of caste. Can you write something?
elephant, high birth
My uncle sits on his veranda like an elephant, enormous with snobbery, and shoos away a poor boy who came to deliver cream for being from another community. A doha?
The elephant is proud of its height, but a small goad rules it; so is the pride of high birth.
Write a verse on the elephant which looks down on all creatures from its great height, as a high born man looks down on those he calls low, though both have a small goad that will rule them.
doha: elephant feels high because of its height, like caste pride
Please write a doha on those who say they are of the highest birth, that their blood is pure and they must not mix with the lowly, though the same blood runs in everyone's veins.
An old man in our colony refused to attend a funeral because the family belongs to a lower caste, and said he would be defiled. I felt so ashamed. Doha?
pure blood, lie
Cut the veins of high and low, and the same red flows out.
doha on pure blood nonsense
doha: priest and washerman both have the same god, why does caste put one above the other
The priest wears his birth on his shoulders, the washerman wears his work, and the Lord sees only the heart.
Write about the priest who looks down on the washerman as impure, though the washerman cleans the very cloth the priest wears, and both are made of the same breath and the same dust.
In our village the priest will not take a glass of water from the washerman's hand, but he wears the clothes that same washerman washes every week. A doha?
priest, washerman, caste
A verse about the mirror in which the high born and the low born see the same face, with the same eyes and the same fears, though they have been taught to believe that they are not alike.
When I looked at the mirror after hearing my in laws speak about the lower caste maid, I wondered what difference they saw in the mirror. A doha?
doha: mirror shows no caste
mirror, caste
The mirror shows only a face, and no one has ever found a caste in it.
The yogi wanders with his one-string lute and asks no caste, for the Lord is not born of any family.
Write a doha on the yogi who plays his one-string lute at every village without asking anyone's caste, and sings that the Lord is found in every home and every heart, and not only in the high ones.
doha: yogi with a one-string lute, doesn't ask caste, just sings
yogi, one-string lute, caste
A wandering yogi with a one-string lute came through our village and ate in the home of a low caste family, and the upper castes were furious. Doha for that?
My daughter fell in love with a boy from a different community and my family is calling it a disgrace. I want a doha to show them how silly this is
Compose a doha about parents who break a young couple's hearts for the sake of the caste, as if the pride of ancestors were worth more than the love and happiness of their living children.
Two hearts met, and an old wall of birth stood between them.
doha on forbidding love marriages over caste
caste vs love
doha: mirror and shadow, caste is a shadow, nothing real
A doha on how caste is only a shadow, which the mirror of truth cannot reflect, for if you look at the face alone, you will find nothing but a human face that is the same as all the others.
I looked in the mirror and saw my shadow behind me, and realized my father's idea of caste is just like that, something that follows us around without being real. A doha?
The mirror holds a face, and the shadow only darkens it; caste is the shadow.
mirror, shadow, caste
At the village function, my grandmother was told to use separate glasses for milk because of her caste, though she had stitched every guest's clothes with her needle. A doha for that insult?
doha: milk and needle, the needle stitches all, milk doesnt know caste
The milk does not ask the milkmaid's caste, and the needle stitches the cloth of all.
milk, needle, caste

A doha on the milk that nourishes high and low alike, and the needle that stitches the garments of everyone without distinction, which both do their honest work without asking who is allowed to benefit.
birth, not worth
People at the party kept asking my husband about his family, his village, his gotra, and I could tell they were measuring where to place him. A doha?
He asks about the family you came from, not the heart you carry.
doha about being judged by your family background
Write a doha on the habit of asking a person his lineage before offering him a seat, as if the nobility of the guest were written in his ancestors and not in his own behaviour.
cleric, caste, pride
doha: the cleric also has caste pride, even though his faith says all are equal
The cleric at our neighbourhood prayer says everyone is equal but there are different rows for different families. A doha?
Please write a doha about the cleric who preaches that all are equal before God yet looks down on the lower born among his flock, and keeps his own community apart in the same congregation.
In the cleric's hall of equals, the rows were drawn by birth.
doha on the foolishness of caste pride
Dust on the high road and dust on the low road are the same dust, and the wind lifts them equally.
caste, empty boast
Compose a couplet for those who boast of their lineage and of what their grandfathers were, while forgetting that nobody carries inherited glory into the grave, where all lie as humble as the rest.
My cousin spent the whole dinner telling us about our great grandfather the landlord, until my father said, 'And what have you done?' A doha for dad's reply?
doha: the tongue has no caste and the forest has no caste, all are equal

A doha about the tongue, which tastes the same sweetness whether the hand that feeds it is high or low, and the forest, which gives shade to every wanderer, whatever his birth, a lesson in equal generosity.
I watched a woman of a lower caste serve food to a proud old man, and his tongue enjoyed it all the same. At the edge of the forest I thought, how absurd. Doha?
The tongue does not ask the cook's caste, the forest does not ask the traveller's birth.
tongue, forest, caste
My uncle puts a bright forehead mark on every day and says it proves our family is of the highest birth, but he cannot name a single good deed of his own. A doha for him?
The forehead mark declares your family but not your heart.
forehead mark, caste
doha on wearing a forehead mark to show your caste status
Write a verse on the forehead mark worn as a badge of high birth, a sign to proclaim one's caste, which cannot make a man better nor hide from the Lord the true colour of the heart beneath.
The upper caste man across the lane calls the lower caste families snakes behind their back, yet the venom is in his own words. Doha?
snake, caste hatred
The snake is not poisonous by caste, and neither is man; the poison is in the mind.
doha: a snake doesn't have caste but humans do
A doha on the snake which is never judged by its caste but only by whether it bites, while men judge each other by the family they were born into and never by whether they do harm.
doha: physician doesn't ask the patient's caste, cotton bandage same for all
A doha about the physician who treats the patient without asking his caste and the cotton he uses to bind the wounds, white and soft for all, teaching that kindness has no regard for birth.
The physician's cotton binds the wounds of the high and the low, and no one has found a difference in the pain.

When my father was ill, the doctor who treated him was from a lower caste, and some relatives refused to take his medicine, until the fever grew worse. A doha, please? The cotton bandage was the same.
physician, cotton, caste
What is the worth of a lineage that cannot feed a hungry child?
doha on rich families being proud of their ancestry
ancestry, worthless pride

Please write a couplet on the pride that clings to ancestry, the old names, the old land, the old titles, none of which will stand beside the one who lives with humility and truth in the here and now.
My distant relatives are always reminding us of our great grandfather's title, but they are broke and dependent on us for money. Doha?
stone, thread, caste
doha: stone and thread both are equal, caste is man made
The stone does not know its mason's birth, and the thread does not know the hand that measured.
A mason from the lower caste carved the beautiful stone for the village hall, and the same men who praised it would not share a meal with him. A doha that mentions the thread of his plumb line?
A doha on the stone shaped by a mason of low birth into a holy place, and the thread by which he measured it straight, showing that fine work is not made lesser by the caste of the maker.
door, peacock, caste
The family next door shut the door in the face of a lower caste friend of mine, while their pet peacock strutted around the yard like it owned the place. A doha for that?

A doha about the proud peacock which spreads its feathers at every door without regard to whose it is, and the high born man who closes his door to the lower born and thinks the closed door makes him taller.
The peacock struts through every door, the man of high birth shuts his against his neighbour.
doha: peacock walks through any door, but humans close doors on low caste people
doha about people changing their behavior once they learn your caste
The moment my landlord learned my surname he said the room was already taken, and I could see from his face why. A doha?
Compose two lines for those who greet you warmly until they learn the family you were born in, and then turn their faces away, as if the name of a caste could change the person standing before them.
When your name was spoken, his smile shrank to the size of his birth.
caste changes smiles
When the sacred dress and the sacred hair are taken away, all men stand as one.
stripped of caste, same
In the hospital waiting room we all wore the same plain gown, high caste and low caste, and nobody could tell the difference. It was strange and beautiful. Doha?
doha idea: strip off your name and surname and everyone is the same person
Write a doha on how once the titles, the surnames, the garments and the family names are all stripped away, a man is only a man, as naked as the day he was born, and exactly like the next.
The family that owns the grindstone workshop in our village is of a lower caste, and the others, who repeat caste talk like a parrot, still hesitate to eat from their flour. A doha?
doha: parrot and grindstone, the parrot repeats caste talk but the grindstone grinds all grain equally
The grindstone grinds every grain alike; the parrot repeats what it has been taught of caste.
A doha on the grindstone, which turns all grain into flour without knowing whose field it came from, and the parrot, which repeats its masters' proud talk of caste without ever understanding a word.
parrot, grindstone, caste
The cloth sheet covers the high and the low alike in the cold of the night; so does mercy.
cloth sheet, caste
On a winter night, a poor lower caste man was given a cloth sheet by a higher caste woman, and nobody in the street said a word. It made me smile. A doha?
doha: cloth sheet keeps all warm, doesnt ask caste

A doha about the cloth sheet that warms the shivering of any wanderer who is lucky to receive it, indifferent to his birth, and the open hand that gives it, which is the only true mark of a high family.
A doha on the beggar and the weaver at his loom, both judged by the families they came from, though the weaver weaves the cloth that clothes the proud, and the beggar teaches humility in his need.
The weaver's loom clothes the proud; the beggar's hand teaches them to be humble; neither is a matter of birth.
doha: beggar and weaver at his loom both treated as low caste but they matter
My neighbour is a weaver who works at his loom all day and a lower caste, and the beggar outside our gate gets more respect than he does from the proud ones. A doha about this?
beggar, weaver's loom, caste
parrot, caste talk
Please write a doha about the parrot kept by the high born family, taught fine words about purity and caste, which it repeats without understanding a single word of the pride it is made to carry.
doha: parrot repeating caste talk it was taught
The parrot at my uncle's home has learned to say the family's caste slogans, and I realized how much of caste talk is just repeating what we've been taught. Doha for that?
The parrot recites the pride of its master, and knows not what it says.
caste is man made

A doha on the idea that the Creator made humankind from one clay and one breath, and that the divisions of high and low, pure and impure, were invented later by men who wanted power over their neighbours.
doha: caste was invented by people, not by God
God made man; man made caste.
My grandfather always said God never wrote a surname on a baby's forehead, and we should not either. Is there a doha like that?
doha about being proud of your caste and doing nothing of worth
My cousin brags all day about his clan's glory, but he drops out of college and has never held a job. A doha for him?
He wears his ancestors like a borrowed crown.
borrowed glory
A doha on the fool who rests all his pride on the deeds of his forefathers, never doing a deed of his own, like a man who boasts of the harvest from a field he has never sown.
In our village a lower caste man built the little bridge over the stream, and the proud ones won't cross it, but they won't build their own. And the one-string lute singer crosses it freely. Doha?
one-string lute, bridge, caste
The singer with his one-string lute crosses the bridge, and the bridge asks not his caste.

A doha on the bridge that carries the high and the low across the stream with equal patience, and the singer with his one-string lute who sings of one Lord, while the proud wait on the shore rather than cross.
doha: bridge doesnt care who built it or who crosses, one-string lute guy crosses it free
jaggery, crow, caste
At the festival function, the jaggery sweets were given first to the upper castes and the crow that ate the leftover jaggery was shooed away from everyone. A doha for this?
Jaggery is sweet to the high and the low, and the crow eats it without asking whose it is.
doha: jaggery tastes sweet to all, the crow eats it, no caste

A doha on the jaggery whose sweetness is the same in the mouth of any caste, and the crow that eats where it finds food without asking about birth, teaching the proud something of ease and fellowship.
In the inn, high and low rest on the same floor, and the cotton blanket warms them all the same.

A doha about the roadside inn where wanderers of every caste sleep under one roof, share the same cotton blankets, and wake with the same morning light on their faces, teaching what the village never learned.
doha: inn and cotton blanket, no caste in an inn
inn, cotton, caste
On our long train journey, we stopped at an inn where everyone slept side by side in cotton quilts, and in the morning nobody seemed to remember the caste they came with. Doha?
tongue, caste insult
A doha on the tongue that speaks of caste to insult a neighbour and the lowly man who keeps his own tongue sweet, so that the high one is lowered by his words and the low is raised by his.
doha: harsh tongue about caste makes you low yourself
The tongue that wounds with caste has lowered itself.
A relative called our maid a low caste name at dinner, and she looked down, and my tongue was frozen with shame. Could you give me a doha to say what I could not?
doha: no one asks the caste of a doctor in an emergency
In the hour of need, no one asks the helping hand its birth.
Write a doha on how in times of flame or flood or sickness nobody asks the caste of the one who comes to rescue them, and how silly it is that they remember it again when the danger has passed.
rescue, no caste asked
When our building flooded last year, a lower caste neighbour pulled my father out, and now my father still won't sit with him. Doha?
My father said not to wear the shroud of caste to our graves, because at the end all the shrouds look the same. A doha for his thought?
doha: shroud has no caste
In the end the shroud is white for all, and no one asks which family wove it.
A doha on the shroud, which is the last garment of every man and woman, and which does not carry any caste mark or family name, a final lesson in equality that the living refuse to learn.
shroud, caste
doha: forest and crossroads, no caste there
forest, crossroads, caste

A verse about the forest where all the greenery stands together, tall and short, and the crossroads where all wayfarers meet, high and low, none asking the other's family, because the road does not belong to any caste.
In the forest all growth rises together, at the crossroads all feet meet; caste is a village thing.
I got lost in a forest with a stranger and we met at a crossroads, and he helped me find my way, and only later did I learn he was from a different community. Doha?
churn, caste
The churn takes the cream of any cow and gives butter of the same colour.
doha: churn works the same for all, butter has no caste
My mother-in-law refuses to let our maid touch the churn, and yet the butter itself is made by churning with her hands. Could you write a doha?
A doha about the churn, which is turned by hands of all families to bring the same butter to every table, and the proud woman who refuses to let a low caste neighbour touch it.
He who is born high and acts in a low way is low; he who is born low and acts with grace is high.
deeds make the man
doha on how deeds matter more than the family you are born in
The most generous man in our village is from a lower caste, and the proudest man gives nothing. People still bow to the proud one. A doha?
A doha on how a person is high or low by what he does and not by where he was born, since a good deed by a so called low person is above a cruel deed by the highborn.
doha: washerman washes everyones clothes and nobody asks his caste when the clothes are clean
washerman, caste scorn
The washerman cleans the clothes of the high born, and is not allowed to sit among them.

A doha on the washerman who cleans the garments of every family in the village, from the proudest to the poorest, yet is called unclean and kept away from the festivals and the feasts by the same families.
Our washerman's son topped his class, but at the school function other parents would not sit next to his mother. Doha for her?
Write a couplet on the great confusion of men who say they know the Lord and yet make divisions of high and low among his children, as though the Father had favourites among those he made.
doha on people claiming to worship God while divided by caste
At the satsang, everyone sang about universal love, and then the seating was arranged by family caste. I could not help but laugh in despair. Doha?
faith, caste hypocrisy
They sing of one Lord and sit in separate rows.

A doha about the cloth sheet that dresses a king in the morning and a pauper at night and passes from hand to hand without asking whose body it covers, because cloth knows no caste, and neither should men.
cloth sheet, caste
One cloth sheet on the king's shoulder, one on the pauper's: who has found the caste of the cloth?
doha: the same cloth sheet covers a rich and poor man, no caste
My aunt gave her old cloth sheet to a poor man at our gate and her husband said that the man was a lower caste, 'he'll make it impure.' I was shocked. A doha?
doha about this world being a short fair that we just visit, with a fish and a bridge
We crossed the old bridge to the village fair as kids and watched fish being sold; now I am old and the whole fair seems to have packed up while I looked away
Write a doha about the world as a fair that opens for a few days, where the fish is sold and a bridge carries the crowd across, and then everyone packs up and goes their way
fish, bridge, passing fair
The bridge brims with fairgoers and the fish glitters in the tents of a festival that closes at dusk, as the world does
I told my grandfather I had finally bought a flat, and he laughed and said, so did I, once, and the boat that brought me to this city was supposed to be temporary
Please write a doha where a boat carries the guests to a fair on an island, where they stay a few days and then sail back, as a picture of how we all just visit this world briefly
The boat brings the visitors to a fair of lights and music, and the same boat takes them home when the drums are silent
boat, world's brief fair
doha with a boat about how the world is just a fair and we leave soon
Write a doha in which a bier and a boat both wait at the edge of the fair, since everyone who comes to this world as a guest for a few days must be carried away, whatever they bought
doha with a bier and a boat, the world is a fair and we go home soon
bier, boat, passing fair
The fair is loud, the bier is silent, and the boat at the edge of the water takes every guest away
My cousin was at the village fair on Sunday, laughing on the boat ride, and on Friday they carried him on a bier; the fair is still running but he is not there
doha about the world being a fair we visit for few days
A festival of colours and voices that is taken down before the week is out: so is the world to those who linger
Please write a doha in the manner of Kabir that says this world is just a fair visited for a few days, that guests who stay too long misunderstand it for their home, and that all must leave
I overheard two old men at a wedding saying that the good thing about life is that you are only here for the festival, and that stuck with me
world is a fair
The drums of the fair are loud in the evening and the ground is bare by morning, and the guests have moved on
Kabir often said that the world is a gathering of a few days, where each takes his tent for a short while and leaves, so write me a doha in simple words about this fair
The fair came to our town last week and left yesterday, and the empty field made my mother say that is what life is, a short visit; I want a doha in this spirit
world's passing fair
doha about how the world is a short fair and we all pack up soon
My landlord keeps telling me this flat is mine for now, and I think of how everyone is a tenant on this earth; the bier at the neighbour's place last week reminded me
bier, world is a fair
Write a doha in which a bier is carried out of a crowded fair, and the guests only pause for a moment before they go back to buying and selling, forgetting that their own stay is also short
doha with a bier in it, about the world being just a fair for a few days
The bier goes out through the gate of the fair, and the fair goes on, forgetting that it is also a guest
A cloud passed over the fairground and the whole thing was packed away before night, and my uncle, who has sung with a loud tongue at fairs, said that is life
Write a doha about a cloud over a fair and a tongue that praises the day, and how every guest finds the festival over before he has finished enjoying it, so he should not call it home
A cloud crosses the fair, a tongue sings its praise, and both are gone by evening, as is the whole gathering
cloud, tongue, passing fair
doha with a cloud and a tongue about the world being a fair we just visit
My grandmother kept a parrot and wore a forehead mark every day, and she said that she had attended the fair of life long enough to know the closing time
parrot, forehead mark, brief fair
doha with a parrot and a forehead mark, the world is a fair and we leave soon
Write a doha where a parrot repeats the cries of a fair, and a woman with a forehead mark buys her trinkets, though both will leave when the drums fall silent and the field is bare
The parrot learns the fair's cries and the forehead mark shines, but by dusk the ground is empty
cremation ground, passing fair
The fair of the living ends at the cremation ground, where all guests are counted out and none are left
Write a Kabir-style doha about the cremation ground at the far edge of the great fair of the world, where each guest finally arrives after buying and selling, and from which nobody returns
doha about a cremation ground and how the world is just a fair
When we left the fair I noticed the cremation ground behind the field, and I realised that every one of us is only visiting the world; I want a doha on this
I checked into an inn for just one night in a city I've loved all my life, and I realised we live in this world the same way, guests with a short booking
doha about the world being an inn where we stay a few days
Please write a doha in which the world is an inn where travelers stop for the night, and in the morning they must pay the bill and go, though some foolishly mistake it for their own home
The inn is full of laughter tonight and will be bare tomorrow, and all the guests have somewhere else to go
inn, world's brief stay
Salt goes into every dish at the fair and is gone from the plate by night, as is the guest who tasted it
At the village fair my grandfather would always buy salt and said that is all he needed from it; he lived as a guest on this earth and died as one
salt, world is a fair
Write a doha where salt is sold at a short-lived fair and every buyer carries a little away, saying this world is only a visit of a few days and must not be mistaken for a permanent home
doha with salt in it, the world is a fair and we dont stay
Please write a doha in which a fly lands on a skeleton at the closing of the fair, and the verse says that the guests who thought the festival would last forever have gone, leaving the empty tents
fly, skeleton, passing fair
At the end of the fair a fly sat on the skeleton of a dead goat behind the tents, and the old man beside me said, that is how long it all lasts; I want a doha about this
The fly circles the skeleton at the end of the fair, where the revelry has ended and only the dust remains
doha with a fly and a skeleton, the world is just a fair and we pass through
The lamps are lit for a few evenings, the music plays, the crowd thins, and the world is a fair that pulls up its tents
doha about the world being a fair, we only visit
The tents are already coming down at the end of the festival, and my father said look, that is how we will all go, one tent after another
Write a Kabir-style doha in which the world is likened to a fair that stays only for a few days, when each person tastes a few sweets and leaves, and none can claim the ground as his own
fair, brief visit
There was a cuckoo singing near the furnace at the fair, and my grandfather said all of it was only on loan for a few days; the cuckoo and the furnace and all of us
cuckoo, furnace, passing fair
doha with a cuckoo and a furnace, the world is a short fair
Write a doha in which a cuckoo sings near a roaring furnace in the middle of the fair, though both will be gone when the festival ends, and the guests will find nothing but empty ground
The cuckoo sings above the furnace in the fair, and both fall silent when the evening comes to pack up the tents
doha about the world being a fair that we visit only for a few days
My niece looked at the balloons at the fair and asked, where do they go after, and I said to the same place we all go; I want a doha on that
The fair has its balloons and music, and the hours rush, and nobody asks where the hours go
Please write a doha in the voice of Kabir which says that the world is a fair of a few days, in which we come to look around and buy a few things and then go home empty
world is a fair
door, passing fair
There is a door at the end of the fair through which each guest must go, and it opens in only one direction
Write a doha where the fair has one door through which everyone enters and another through which everyone leaves, so no one mistakes the temporary festival for his own permanent dwelling
doha with a door in it about the world being just a short fair
The doors of the fair opened this morning and will close this evening, and I thought of how we all come in through one door and leave through another
When I visit my childhood town now, I see strangers living in the rooms where my family laughed, and I think: we were all only passing through, and the town goes on without us
doha about how everyone is just visiting this world
The fair fills the field with lanterns and noise, and the next morning finds it bare and swept
world, brief visit
Write a doha in Kabir's manner saying the world is a fair for a few days, that people come with families and sell and buy and quarrel, and then they leave, and the field is empty again
A house for the night, and by morning another guest sleeps in the bed where you slept, for the world is a fair
Write a doha in which the world is a fair and the house on the fairground is only rented for a few days, so that those who paint its walls and plant gardens are foolish, as the lease is short
house, world is a fair
We rented a house near the fair for the festival week and by the end we had become so attached to it that leaving was difficult; that is also what life feels like
doha with a house and the world being just a short fair
I spent a lifetime searching for a philosopher's stone at festivals and fairs, and at the end I understood that the whole world is a visit that ends
The philosopher's stone is sold at every fair and bought by every fool, who leaves with an empty pocket and a full heart
philosopher's stone, world's fair
doha with a philosopher's stone, the world is a fair and we leave soon
Write a doha in which a seller at a passing fair claims to have the philosopher's stone, and the guests who buy it find at the closing that the fair, the seller and their own stay were all temporary

Write a doha about the man who wears the sacred mark on his forehead and chants loudly but whose eyes follow every woman who passes, showing that outward religion without inner restraint is a deception.
The mark on the brow is bright, but the eyes below it wander; what use is the sign if the mind is not still?
doha on a tilak wearing hypocrite with wandering eyes
tilak, wandering eyes
The man who leads our evening prayers wears a big mark on his forehead yet leers at every young woman, and I am disgusted.
I stood by the well hoping to see a girl who drew water there each morning, and I realised I had come not to draw water but to feed an urge.
Compose a doha about a youth who goes daily to the well not for water but to watch a passing girl, and about how his craving wastes his hours and leaves his own thirst for truth unquenched.
He came to the well for water, but his thirst was of another kind, and it was never slaked.
doha on a guy who hangs around the well just to see a girl
well, wasted desire
doha on river and thread: lust pulls you along like a current
river, thread, craving
I got swept along like a river by an infatuation that tied my life up in a thread of lies, and now I am trying to find my way back.
Compose a doha showing that bodily craving is a river that sweeps away everything in its path, and a fine thread of lies that ties the man who is carried by it until he cannot move.
The river of craving carries the weak, and the thread of deceit binds them as they drift.
doha on a grindstone crushing a man who gave in to lust
grindstone, desire
My neighbour's affair ground his family down like a grindstone and left all of them broken.
Please write a doha about how bodily craving is like a grindstone that grinds the lives of the family, the reputation of the man and the peace of his family into dust, leaving only bitterness behind.
The grindstone of craving crushes the grain of years; what was nourishing becomes dust.
After a night of indulgence I woke to a barren feeling like sand, and I wondered how I could ever fill that emptiness by repeating the same thing.
doha on lust leaves u empty like sand
Craving is a mirage on the sand; the thirsty run to it and find only dust.
sand, empty craving
Write a doha about how the pleasures of the flesh slip through the fingers like sand, leaving emptiness and regret, and how only lasting devotion can give a satisfaction that does not run away.
gold, craving, ruin
Gold and craving are twin masters; the one who serves them both is a slave in a heavy chain.
Compose a doha about the man who gives his gold to feed his bodily cravings and finds himself poor in honour and wealth, showing that what is spent on the senses is lost forever without return.
doha on wasting gold on sensual pleasure
My cousin spent all the gold he had inherited on a life of indulgence and now has neither a friend nor a coin to his name.
A friend of mine says sensual enjoyment is life's purpose, but I see how restless and empty he looks, and I would like a verse to answer him.
doha on why chasing pleasure doesnt make u happy
Seek not joy in the senses; they promise much, and leave the seeker poorer than he began.
Please write a doha about the false promise of sensual pleasure, which appears to offer happiness but leaves the seeker emptier, and the lasting peace that comes only from mastering the urges.
pleasures that deceive
The senses run wild if untrained; the wise man holds them firm, the foolish one is dragged.
My brother never learnt to say no to his appetites, and now at forty he is exhausted, in debt and ashamed.
master your senses

Compose a doha about the five senses that run wild when not trained, dragging the unwary toward ruin, and about how the seeker must take firm hold of them through discipline and the company of the wise.
doha on controlling the five senses
Write a doha showing that anyone who allows the craving of the body to rule him cannot see truth, because desire dims judgment, and only the cool mind of a restrained seeker perceives clearly.
desire blinds
When I was infatuated I believed every lie she told me, and only when it ended did I see how blind I had been.
Where the body's hunger rules, the eyes of wisdom are closed; restraint alone gives sight.
doha on how lust makes you blind to the truth
doha on the shroud and lust, in the end it all means nothing
Write a doha about the shroud that awaits every body, the same body we spend so much of our lives indulging and decorating, to remind the seeker of how little the pleasures of the flesh are worth.
The body you adorn is soon to wear a shroud; why then squander your days on its cravings?
At my uncle's funeral, seeing the white shroud, I suddenly felt silly about all the years I had spent running after bodily pleasures.
shroud, bodily cravings
swan, pure mind
doha on swan staying pure while others fall to lust
The swan glides on muddy water yet remains spotless; so the wise live among temptations untouched.
My friend works in an environment full of temptation and yet stays clean, like a swan on muddy water, and I hope to be like him.
Compose a doha about the swan that moves among the mud of the world and remains white, showing that the seeker too can live among temptations without losing his purity if he keeps his mind watchful.
Even the strong are made weak by the hunger of the senses; mightier is the mind that does not bow.
doha on will power against urges
I have been sober and disciplined for two years, and last night an old temptation returned, but I managed to resist it with one deep breath.
resist the urge
Compose a doha showing that the seeker's real battle is not against outer enemies but against the urges of his own body, and that each time he refuses them, he becomes stronger and freer.
The physician can heal the fever of the body, yet who heals the fever of craving? Only the Name, and the patience of years.

Please write a doha about the physician who cures every bodily illness but cannot cure the disease of sensual craving, which only the seeker can heal through discipline, devotion and a wise teacher, more precious than gold.
doha on physician and gold can't cure lust, only discipline
physician, gold, restraint
My physician friend can heal almost anything for gold, but he confessed that he could not cure his own habit of chasing women.
shadow, blind man, desire
I followed the shadow of an attraction for a year like a blind man, and only when it vanished did I understand how little was there.

Compose a doha about the blind man who follows the shadow of bodily craving in the belief that it is a guide, and falls into ruin, whereas the seeker of truth turns from the shadow and finds the real light.
Craving is a shadow that leads the blind; he follows it into the pit and calls it love.
doha on chasing a shadow like a blind man, lust makes you blind
At the mosque the faithful bow, but the blind man's eyes see more clearly than the lustful who stand beside him.
doha on a blind man seeing truth better than a lustful man in the mosque
At the mosque I saw a blind man praying with such purity of mind, while the young man beside him could not stop glancing at the women.
mosque, blind man, wandering eyes
Compose a doha showing that a blind man who prays at the mosque with a clean mind sees more of God than the sighted man whose eyes and thoughts wander toward the women around him.

Write a doha about how the cravings of the body bring momentary pleasure and lasting grief, and the seeker who sees this clearly gives them up without regret and finds a calm happiness no indulgence ever gave.
doha on short pleasure vs long pain
brief pleasure, long grief
Every time I gave in, I felt great for ten minutes and awful for ten days, and finally I understood the bargain I was making.
A moment's joy, a lifetime's tears; wise is he who sees the price before he pays.
When desire rules the mind, the soul is a stranger in its own body; turn within, and be whole again.
doha on coming back to yourself after temptation
After months of being lost in an obsession, I feel like a stranger to myself, and want to find my way back to calm.
return to yourself

Please write a doha about the seeker who has strayed into sensual temptation and then returns to himself in repentance, and how the Lord receives him back without reproach and sets him on the path once more.
My teacher says that the body's cravings are the first and last enemy of a spiritual life, and I wish to understand why through a verse.
doha on why cravings are the enemy of spiritual life
Compose a doha about how the cravings of the body, left unchecked, are the first enemy a seeker meets and the last he conquers, and how patience, practice and the grace of the guru help him to win.
the seeker's enemy
The first foe and the last is in your own flesh; conquer it and no other enemy remains.
The rose of pleasure hides a thorn that pierces the unwary; do not reach for what will make you bleed.
thorn, temptation
doha on thorns in the rose of pleasure
Write a doha about the rose of sensual pleasure that attracts with its beauty but hides a thorn, and about how the wise look first for the thorn before reaching out and so remain safe and calm.
I was attracted to a coworker who seemed perfect, but the thorn of her manipulation soon showed itself, and I'm glad I stepped back in time.
Compose a doha about the sorrow of a man who gives his days to sensual pursuits and wakes in old age to find his strength, his friends and his chances gone, and nothing left of his life.
My old uncle looks back on a youth spent chasing pleasures and says he has nothing to show for it, not even a memory worth keeping.
doha on how chasing pleasure in youth leaves old age empty
wasted youth
Youth spent on appetite leaves old age with nothing; spend your strength on what lasts.
The lion roars in the wilderness of the senses, yet the single string of the lute silences him with a note of the Name.
Please write a doha about the lion of bodily craving that roars in the mind, and the single note of the one-string lute, the remembrance of God, which alone can quiet it and bring the seeker peace.
My lion of an urge woke every night until I picked up my one-string lute and sang the Name, and slowly it fell silent.
lion, one-string lute, calm
doha on lion of lust tamed by a lute and singing God's name
The tree of pleasure bears fruit that turns to dust; churn the cream of wisdom instead, and take its butter.
Compose a doha about how the tree of sensual pleasure bears sweet-looking fruit that is bitter within, while the churn of discipline and meditation turns the cream of life into the butter of peace.
tree, churn, restraint
My grandfather sat under the tree each evening, churning buttermilk, and told me that restraint is the only thing that makes any pleasure last.
doha on the tree of pleasure and churn of wisdom
doha on staying faithful to your partner when tempted
stay faithful
A colleague has been making advances toward me although I am married, and I want a verse to remind me why I must stay true.

Please write a doha about the honour of a person who stays faithful to his marriage vows in the face of temptation, and about how that loyalty brings a peace and trust that no brief pleasure can ever match.
Faithful is the one who turns from the passing temptation; his loyalty is a lasting joy.
doha on salt and crossroads: temptations at every turn, stay on track

Write a doha about the traveller who stands at the crossroads where the paths of pleasure and of discipline part, tasting the salt of bodily temptation and learning that it only makes him thirstier for more.
Standing at a crossroads in my life, I realised that chasing pleasures only left a salty taste of regret, and I chose the harder path.
At the crossroads one road is sweet and ends in salt; the other is hard and ends in peace.
salt, crossroads, temptation
pearl, restraint
My grandmother kept a single pearl all her life as a symbol of her discipline, saying that a restrained life forms its own pearl.
The pearl forms slowly in the oyster of restraint; scatter it on the senses and it is gone.
doha on pearl and self-control, treasure not wasted

Compose a doha about the pearl of a seeker's life, which is formed over long years of discipline and which he must not throw away on a moment's craving, since once lost it cannot easily be found again.
doha on a moneylender who gambled everything on pleasure

Please write a doha about the moneylender whose wealth and reputation were destroyed by his craving for sensual pleasures, showing that no amount of money can buy back self-respect once it is squandered on the senses.
moneylender, ruined by desire
He counted other men's coins, yet could not count the cost of his own desires; the account came due.
The moneylender in our town, once so respected, spent everything he had on indulgences and now begs from the people he used to lend to.
Under the stars last night I decided to stop chasing every passing attraction, and the sky seemed to nod in approval.
doha on stars and calm after giving up lust
Write a doha about how the stars shine above every human weakness in perfect stillness, teaching the seeker that when he rises above the urges of the body, he too becomes calm, clear and radiant.
stars, peace of restraint
The stars shine calm above the restless world; so shines the soul that has conquered its craving.
The tortoise moves slowly, but the grindstone of deeds grinds fine, and every grain returns to the hand that fed it.
tortoise, grindstone, karma returns
My uncle cheated his partner years ago, slowly and quietly like a tortoise, and this year the grindstone of life turned and the same fate fell on his own business.
Write a doha about the tortoise that walks slowly yet surely and the grindstone that turns without haste, teaching that every deed we do, however slow to ripen, comes back to us in its full measure.
doha w a tortoise and a grindstone about how whatever u do comes back to u eventually

My brother laughed when he tricked a customer into overpaying at the weekly stall, and ten years later he fell into a debt trap himself, while a moth beat against the bulb that last night as if warning him.
doha w a moth and a well - the one who digs a well for others falls in it himself, the moth rushes to the light and gets hurt by his own wish. u know the idea
The moth that seeks the light is undone by his own longing; he who digs a well for another falls in first.
moth, well, own deeds
Please write a doha in which the one who digs a well to trap another falls into it himself, while a moth rushes to its own ruin at the light, showing that what we do to others returns to us.
Write a doha where a man standing at the crossroads is offered the paras but chooses to pass it over for a petty profit by cheating, and learns that every choice returns its fruit to the chooser.
At a crossroads of my career I could help a colleague for a modest reward or cheat him for a big bonus, a real paras moment, and my mother said whatever I choose will come back to me.
At the crossroads the paras is offered, but only the road of fair deeds brings a rich return, and the road of tricks brings its price.
doha w crossroads and the paras - every choice you make comes back as its fruit
crossroads, paras, choices
The boy who bullied me at school lost his job last year when his own manager bullied him, and my grandmother said without surprise that what you give out is what returns.
As the giver, so the receiver one day; the hand that wounds shall one day be wounded.
doha about how ur own actions come back to u, karma is real man
deeds come back
Write me a couplet that explains that every action of a person, good or bad, must in the end return to the doer, so no one should imagine that unjust deeds will pass without their consequences.
doha w a mirror and milk, what you give is what you get back, like the milk curdles if u sour it first
The mirror gives back the face that stands before it; the milk turns sour if the hand was sour. So are our deeds returned.
Write a doha in which a mirror shows each person exactly the face they bring to it and milk turns sour if mixed with something bitter, showing that what we do comes back in the form we gave.
My landlord was harsh with his tenants all his life, and when he got old his own sons would not sit beside him, and the neighbourhood said it was like a mirror, and a bitter glass of milk.
mirror, milk, deeds returned

Write a doha for the man who spoke cruel words with his tongue and then needed a physician for the harm he himself had caused, teaching that the consequences of what we say and do return to us in time.
My uncle used his sharp tongue to hurt many people, and when he fell sick and needed a physician, none of his old friends came to the hospital, and I thought, this is what comes of it.
doha with a tongue and a physician: ur mean words come back as ur problems
tongue, physician, reap
The tongue that gave the sharpest words must beg the physician for the cure; every return is of our own giving.

My neighbour set a cage for stray birds just to enjoy their noise and then was stuck indoors for months with a broken leg, and his mother used to say the winnowing fan always separates your deeds from your wishes.
winnowing fan, cage, own deeds
doha w a winnowing fan and a cage - what ur deeds are made of is what comes back sorted out for u, even the cage u built
Write a doha in which the winnowing fan separates the grain from the chaff of a man's actions and the cage he builds for others closes around him, teaching that we reap what we have made ourselves.
The winnowing fan flings the chaff away, the cage shuts on its builder; each man is bound by what his own hands have made.
My grandmother pulled the rope of the churn every morning and said that the butter is only what you put in, just like life gives back whatever you put into it.
doha w a churn and a rope - u churn what u have and u get what u put in, simple karma
Write a doha in which one pulls a rope to turn the churn, and what comes out is the result of what was poured in, to show that the fruit of our actions is exactly what we have put in.
churn, rope, deeds returned
Pull the rope as the churn turns, and know that the butter is only what was poured; so are our deeds returned.
After my sister cheated on her exams her friends stopped trusting her and she failed even the honest ones later, and our dad said that is what consequences are, not punishment, just returns.
doha about consequences of lying, like you lie once and it just comes back and bites u
Please write a doha that says every person must eat the fruit of what he has done, that no one escapes the result of his own conduct, and that those who do good will receive good in return.
None may escape the result of their own deeds; what is done in secret returns in the open.
actions have results
A man I know made his fortune by exploiting vulnerable workers, and now his children refuse to talk to him, and my grandmother simply says what you do to others finds its way home to you.
He who gives hurt shall receive hurt; he who gives kindness shall receive kindness again.
your deeds return
Write a doha for a person who thinks that hidden wrongdoings will never be repaid, explaining that the results of our actions are certain to return and cannot be bribed or escaped by anyone.
doha about getting what u deserve based on what u did
The tree in the forest bears only what its kind decreed; as the root, so the fruit, and as the deed, so the day.
doha w a tree and a forest - whatever kind of tree u plant is the fruit u get, like deeds
tree, forest, fruit of deeds
My father planted a neem tree on a barren plot when I was born, and now the whole forest-edge colony shelters under it, and he says what you give with care returns to you.

Write a doha where a tree in the forest gives fruit exactly according to its kind, nothing more and nothing different, teaching that the results of our actions are of the very nature of the deeds we did.

Give me a doha about a traveller who treated the innkeeper rudely at the inn and found every room closed against him on his return, teaching that conduct towards others comes back to the one who gave it.
doha about an inn: be nice to the host cuz what u do comes back to u next time you stay
At the inn of the world the guest who gives scorn receives cold beds; the courteous one is welcomed always.
inn, conduct returns
I was rude to the receptionist at the inn on our last trip, and this time the same woman was at the desk and gave me the worst room, and I understood the saying about reaping what you give.
Every deed leaves a silent footprint, and it walks behind you until it overtakes you at the end.
I want a doha that tells people to think before they act, because every deed they do, whether kind or cruel, will return to them as a result, and no force in the world can stop that return.
After I forgave my brother for the money he owed, he came back years later and helped me through my worst time without being asked, and my mother smiled and said goodness always makes its way back.
think before you act
doha about how good deeds come back too, not just bad ones
Write a doha about the lotus that grows in muddy water yet is untouched by it, and the one who gives kindness in an unkind place finds it blooming for him later, because good deeds return in kind.
doha with a lotus: the good u do even in a bad place blooms later for you
lotus, good deeds bloom
From the mud of hard days the lotus rises, and the kindness once given blooms back to the giver.

I volunteered at a shelter in a bad neighbourhood as a student, and years later one of those kids, now a surgeon, saved my father, and I think of the lotus pond near that shelter whenever I recall it.
cotton, moon, deeds
My aunt spun cotton by the light of the moon for the poor every winter, and when she fell ill, strangers who owed her nothing nursed her, as though her kindness had been waiting.
doha with cotton and the moon, soft kindness comes back like the moonlight returns every month
The cotton given under the moon returns as warmth in the winter of thy own need.
Compose a doha in which the soft cotton given warm to a stranger under the moon returns as a warm comfort to the giver in a time of need, to show that every kindness is repaid by life.
My cousin threw a stone at a neighbour's window as a joke, and next year somebody broke his own car window, and the whole family said, it was bound to come back.
doha with a stone: the stone u throw lands on ur own head eventually
Need a doha about a stone thrown at another that turns in the air and comes down on the thrower's own head, teaching that harm intended for others returns to its source with added force.
stone thrown, returns
The stone thou throwest at another returns in the evening to thy own head.
Write a doha for the person who believes that nobody sees their small acts of dishonesty, explaining that every act has its consequence, which will arrive even if no human eye witnessed it.
Though no eye sees thy deed, the deed sees thee; it will find thee in its own good time.
I once let a cashier's mistake in my favour pass and kept the extra change, and a month later I lost a much bigger sum in a mistake of my own, and it felt like an account being balanced.
doha about secret bad deeds still coming back to u somehow
unseen deeds return
Whatever flower thou dost give to the world, the world will one day lay back in thy hands.
Write a doha on how the good that one does for others is never lost but comes back to the doer sooner or later, so that kindness is the safest investment a person can make in the course of life.
kindness returns
My grandfather fed hungry travellers every evening for forty years, and at his funeral hundreds of strangers came to bring food to our family, and nobody had even invited them.
doha about good deeds being repaid, i keep helping people and wondering if it matters
doha w a stone and an arrow - once the arrow leaves the bow u cant take it back, same with a deed. stone too
The arrow once loosed, the stone once thrown, return not to the hand but to the fate of the one who shot.
Could you do a doha in which an arrow once shot and a stone once thrown cannot be recalled, teaching that every deed, once done, travels on to its result, and the doer must meet it in time.
I fired off a harsh email at my boss like an arrow and could not take it back, and the consequences landed on me like a stone the following week, which taught me to weigh actions first.
arrow, stone, no recall
scales, net, deeds weighed
doha w scales and a net - everything u do gets weighed in the end, and u cant escape the net of ur own deeds
The scales weigh what the net has caught; each deed is counted, and none is lost from the account.
Write a doha in which the scales weigh every deed with perfect justice and the net of consequence gathers each person's actions, teaching that no one escapes the exact result of what he has done.
The accountant at our firm weighed each expense on the scales of honest rules and caught my boss in the net of his own false entries, and I realised nobody escapes the weighing of their deeds.
At the entrance, the pot of water given to the thirsty returns as a flood of blessings.

A doha, please, in which a pot of water given freely to a thirsty stranger at the entrance comes back to the giver many times over, teaching that kindness once done never fails to return as a blessing.
door, pot, kindness returns
doha w a door and a pot of water - give the thirsty water at ur door and it comes back to u
My grandmother kept a pot of water at the door for passers-by all her life, and when she was ill, strangers she had never met arrived to help us, and the neighbours called it her returns.
Write a doha where a king builds a palace and a mosque on the tears of the poor and finds that his deeds, not his buildings, are weighed, and what he did to the poor returns upon him.
The builder who raised a palace for the minister by cheating the workers out of their wages saw his own sons disinherited, and next to the mosque the old men remarked that it all comes back.
The palace is raised, the mosque is raised, but the deed beneath them is the one that returns.
doha with a palace and a mosque - big buildings dont save u from the results of what u did
palace, mosque, reckoning
Write a doha about the swan that takes only the pure and a furnace that tests everyone, teaching that every deed passes through the test and the doer receives only what his deeds have made him.
swan, furnace, deeds tested
The swan takes the pure, the furnace burns the dross; so every deed is sifted, and returns as it is.
doha w a swan and a furnace - actions get tested in the end and u get what u deserve
The old judge in our town was known as a swan for honesty, and he sat before the furnace of public opinion without fear, saying a clean life receives only a clean reckoning.
Write a doha about a singer with a one-string lute who sings songs of hatred and finds his own shadow singing them back at him in the evening, showing that what we put into the world returns to us.
The lute plays what the fingers choose, and the shadow carries the tune home; so we hear forever what we have played.
lute, shadow, deeds follow
doha w a one-string lute and a shadow, ur deeds follow u like a shadow
My friend played hateful songs on his one-string lute in the evenings, and now his own children sing the same abuse back at him, like the shadow of a bad tune.
I'd love a doha about the date palm that bears sweet fruit high up, and the man who gave nothing and is left with nothing, teaching that only what one has given or done will be his in the end.
date palm, fruit of deeds
doha w a date palm - u get fruits only for the work ur put into it
The date palm gives its fruit to the one who tends it; the idle hand gathers nothing, as the deed so the fruit.
My uncle planted a date palm in the dry yard after he retired and everyone laughed, but twelve years later its fruit fed half the lane, and he said you only get back what you give in time.
doha w a mirror and a diamond - ur deeds polish or dull ur face like a diamond dulls with dirt, u see it in the mirror

Write a doha in which a diamond shines according to how it was cut and a mirror shows a person the face that his deeds have made, teaching that our actions shape what we become and what returns to us.
The mirror shows the face thy deeds have carved; the diamond shines only where the cutting was true.
mirror, diamond, deeds shape you
My old teacher said that a person's deeds are cut into the face like facets in a diamond, and when I looked in the mirror after years of bitterness I saw what he meant.
doha w a needle and a furnace - each stitch of ur deeds goes into the clothes u wear later, and the furnace tests everything. karma stuff
needle, furnace, deeds sewn
The needle stitches the garment of thy fate, and the furnace tests every seam; wear what thy hand has sewn.
My grandmother, a tailor, used a needle for sixty years and said every wrong stitch comes back to you when the furnace-heat of summer shows the weak seam, and she said life is the same.
Write a doha where each deed is a stitch made by a needle into a garment that the doer must himself wear, and the furnace of time tests every seam, so we live in our own actions.
I want a doha for someone angry that bad things keep happening to them, gently reminding them that today's troubles may be returns of earlier actions and that the way out is better deeds from now on.
doha about how bad things happening might be a result of my past actions and i should do better now
Weep not at the fruit thou dost meet; change the deed, and the day will change after it.
own deeds, own results
After losing my business I blamed everyone, and then my old teacher quietly asked how I had treated my workers, and I started to see my own part in it.
doha about blame, stop blaming others for ur life, its the result of ur own choices

Write a Kabir style doha for a person who blames fate and others for his misfortune, reminding him that his actions are the cause and what he faces is only their result, so he should change his deeds.
Why curse fate and strangers? The cause was in thy hand; the result is only its echo.
My brother blames the government, his boss and bad luck for being broke, but he never saves and always spends before pay day, and I wish he could see the connection.
stop blaming, own it
My mother once put aside a single pearl from her wedding jewellery to pay for a poor girl's wedding, and in her old age that girl's family took care of her when no one else did.
Need a doha about a pearl freely given to a poor bride by a kind woman, which returns to her many times over in her time of need, to show that goodness given is goodness received in the end.
pearl given, blessing returns
The pearl given in secret to the poor returns as a necklace of blessings in the hour of need.
doha with a pearl - give something precious to someone in need and it comes back to u

Write me a doha for a businessman who has been exploiting others in secret, warning him that no profit made by hurting others stays with him, and the result of his actions will arrive to claim its due.
doha about how cheating people for money always costs u later
dishonest gain, lost
My cousin made a quick fortune by selling fake products, and three years later the lawsuits took everything he had, and my father quietly said, the account got settled.
Gain that is bought with another's tears is borrowed; the payment falls due when thou least expect it.
doha: whatever u give out in the world is what u get, positive or negative
you get what you give
As thou givest to the world, so doth the world give thee; none may take what he never gave.
I used to snap at everyone on my team, and one day my intern burst into tears and quit, and a week later three seniors followed him, and I finally saw what my tone had done.
Write a doha reminding us that the world gives back to each person according to what he gives to it, so that a person who gives love will get love and one who gives hatred will get hatred.
The fish that swallows the bait is drawn by its own hunger; the hook was only the shape of its desire.
doha w a fish - fish bites the hook cuz of its own greed, deeds bring their own results
Compose a doha about a fish that is caught by the very bait it desired, teaching that people are caught by the results of their own cravings and deeds, and that no fate is imposed from outside.
fish, greed, own fate
My uncle bought a cheap investment scheme because of his own greed and lost everything, like a fish biting a hook, and he now says it was his own deed that caught him.
My brother tied a rope around his promises and tied himself by moonlight into a pile of debts, and now says that the rope he spun for others was around his own neck.
doha w a rope and the moon - the rope u tie for others ends up round ur own neck, even the moonlit night cant hide it
The rope woven for another's neck is laid by moonlight around thine own.
rope, moon, self-bound
