Our family reciter wanted us to put a fish in a bowl and bless a sword for luck, charging a fortune. Mom just shook her head. A doha to say what she thought?
Please compose a doha on the man of rites who chants over a fish in the water and a sword in the hand, selling protection to the anxious, while the true protector sits in the heart unsought.
Over the fish and the sword the rite is recited, yet the true shield is hidden in a quiet heart.
fish, sword, empty rites

A doha about the oil press that squeezes the poor, and the owner who performs great rituals each morning and pours offerings, hoping the ceremony will cover the pressure he puts on his workers every single day.
The oil press turns all day, squeezing; at dawn the owner pours his ritual offering to wash the stain.
oil press, hollow ritual
doha: the oil press owner does a puja every day but underpays workers
Where I work, the boss does a long ceremony every morning before opening the oil press and then sacks people without notice. Please give me a doha for it
write a doha about a leaf offered in puja but the heart left out
My neighbour gets up at four to pick leaves and flowers for her ritual offerings, then spends the evening saying nasty things about everyone on the street. doha?
One green leaf is offered at the altar, but the heart that should be offered is still withheld.
leaf, offering, no devotion

Compose a doha on those who gather leaves and flowers for their ceremonies, arrange them just so, and think the offering has been made, while the one real offering, the surrender of ego, is never given.
seed, pot of water, ritual
doha: pouring water from a pot on a seed won't make it sprout if the soil of the heart is dead, ritual pointless

Write a verse about the man who pours the pot of water over the seed with elaborate ritual and speeches, hoping for a harvest, while the soil of his own mind is hardened and nothing sincere is planted.
The pot of water is poured, the seed is sown with a chant, but the ground of the heart remains dry and hard.
My father in law performed a seed sowing ceremony with a big pot of water and a hired reciter, yet cut down the village's old fields next day. I wish Kabir could comment
doha on the neighbour who attends every holy event and still hates his brother
For three years my uncle has done every fast and pilgrimage on the calendar. Last month he still would not attend his brother's daughter's wedding. A couplet for him?
devout in public only
Write a doha about the believer who joins every ritual gathering, wears the right look, and speaks the right words, yet nurses an old hatred for his own brother that no ceremony has ever touched.
Many altars he has bowed at, but one room in his own heart he has locked for years.
Write a doha about a yogi who has set up a big oil press of ceremonies, pressing out fees and offerings from followers each morning, while his own mind remains unchanged by all that grand ritual.
doha pls, yogi plus oil press metaphor for money hungry rituals
yogi, oil press, hollow rites
The yogi who came to our colony set up an elaborate ritual hall like an oil press for donations and demanded ghee, and by the end of the month he had a new car. What would Kabir say?
The yogi turns the oil press of ritual, and the people provide the oil, while the Truth he speaks of slips by.

Compose a doha about those who observe a fixed calendar of rituals, from sunrise rites to evening chants, believing that routine alone makes them holy, though not one of those rites has ever made them kinder or humbler.
My grandma follows her ritual calendar like a train schedule, never missing a single rite, but she is quite cold toward the new bahu. Could we capture that in a doha?
By the calendar they pray, by the calendar they weep, and the heart has no hour of its own.
doha about people following rituals like a rulebook
ritual calendar, cold hearts
doha: forehead mark, rainbird calling, ritual people who don't actually yearn
The rainbird calls for the true drop alone, but the forehead mark bows to every passing shower of ceremony.
My grandfather is a man with a bright forehead mark who daily recites mantras, but unlike the rainbird he never yearns for anything beyond habit. What would you write about him?
forehead mark, rainbird, no longing

Write a verse where the rainbird cries for one pure raindrop with real longing, in contrast to the person with a fancy forehead mark who attends every ritual and yearns for nothing deeper than applause.

A doha about the one who counts prayer beads from morning to night, murmuring the holy name with lips alone, while the mind runs after property and quarrels, and no devotion actually ties the heart to anything divine.
Prayer beads slide through the fingers, as years slide through the days, and the mind never once turns inward.
prayer beads, false devotion
In the bus, a lady next to me kept moving her prayer beads, but she was shouting at the conductor and cursing the driver. What a scene! Kabir doha?
doha about prayer beads and fake devotion pls
The snake sheds its skin and thinks the shedding is holiness; the poison stays in the fang.
The man who leads our weekly ritual is gentle in the hall but a snake in business, we all know it. A doha for what we all see?
snake, ritual, hidden poison
doha: snake in the grass as a ritual leader, you know the type
Write a doha about the person who changes his outer rites and clothing every season, much like a snake that sheds its skin, while the venom of cruelty and greed within remains the same.
After a huge pilgrimage trip with the whole extended family, we came home and the arguments about land started again the very same evening. Is there a doha for that?
holy trip, same quarrels

I'd like a doha about the family that takes the grandest pilgrimage together, bathes, bows, and chants in every place, and then returns to petty fights over land and money, exactly as if the journey had never happened.
Back from the sacred road with dust on the feet and old quarrels in the heart.
write something on rituals not changing the person who does them
doha: thorn in the heart even after sandalwood and rituals, pls
A friend of mine wears fragrant sandalwood to every ceremony, and still pricks everyone with sharp comments like a thorn. Could you write a verse about her?
Sandalwood cools the brow, but the thorn remains in the speech.
sandalwood, thorn, hollow ritual

Compose a Kabir style doha on the ritual devotee who applies cooling sandalwood paste and looks serene, but whose words are thorns that wound anyone who comes near, and who sees no contradiction in this.
A verse for the regular who is first in the queue at every ceremony and last to forgive anyone, who drops coins in the box with great show yet will not spare a kind word for a struggling neighbour.
Every morning my father in law stands at the front of the prayer line, and every evening he turns the neighbours' children away. A doha please
first in line, unforgiving
doha about people who show up to every ritual and are still unkind
First at the altar, last to the open hand of mercy.
bier, help others

Compose a doha showing that when the bier is lifted, the good done for others without hope of return alone accompanies the soul, so a person should spend his days helping others, not gathering for himself.
At the bier all that I gathered is left behind; only the good I did for others walks with me.
doha on helping others, since all that's left at the end is the bier
At my uncle's bier nobody mentioned his bank balance, only the countless favours he had done for strangers without ever asking anything.
doha on helping ppl without expecting anything back
Give your effort to others freely, asking no fee and keeping no account.
I spent my whole weekend helping a stranger move, and I did not even catch his name, but it was the best weekend I've had in a long time.

Please write a doha about how real goodness is helping another person with no thought of reward, thanks or recognition, and how such selfless acts are the only wealth that increases when it is given away.
do good, expect nothing
The arrow of ambition flies to its own mark, but the yogi's life is an arrow shot toward the good of all.
The yogi in our colony spends his day fetching medicines for the old and mending roofs for the poor, and says he has no time for his own liberation.
arrow, yogi, serve others
Write a doha about how a yogi who meditates for years but never lifts a finger for others is like an arrow never loosed, while service to the needy sends it to its mark.
doha on yogi who helps ppl being better than one who just meditates
doha on the ocean giving rain to the world without asking, like us helping others
ocean, giving freely

Compose a doha showing that the ocean sends its water up to become rain for fields it has never seen, and in the same way a good person works for the welfare of people he may never meet, expecting nothing.
My father worked like an ocean all his life, giving to everyone in the family and the neighbourhood and never asking for repayment.
The ocean gives itself to the sky that the fields may drink; such is the life that lives for others.

Write a doha about the leaf that shelters travellers at the crossroads from rain and heat, expecting no thanks, and how a person's life becomes holy when he serves anyone who comes along without asking whence they came.
doha on a leaf giving shade at the crossroads, serving strangers
leaf, crossroads, help others
At the crossroads outside our village an old woman gives water to every passerby from a small shed, and she has never once taken a coin.
The leaf bows to the wayfarer at the crossroads, shading all without asking who they are.
A life lived only for oneself is soon forgotten; a life given for others is remembered through the generations.
I'd like a doha about how a person who lives only for his own comfort leaves nothing behind, while one who spends his strength on others is remembered long after he is gone.
My teacher spent her entire life helping poor children learn for free, and years after her passing her students are still doing the same for others.
doha on living for others rather than just for yourself
live for others
A fisherman in our village repairs the nets of poor widows for nothing, and says it is the only prayer he knows.
doha on repairing nets for the poor, helping without payment
The net that mends for the poor catches blessings that the world itself cannot give.
net, free help
Please write a doha about the net-mender who patiently repairs the nets of those who cannot pay, teaching that to labour for another's livelihood without asking anything is the highest prayer.
The bell at the mosque rings five times, but our neighbour spends the hours between each call carrying groceries for old people, and I think that is also a kind of prayer.
mosque, bell, serve others

Compose a doha showing that a person can ring the bell and visit the mosque every day, but the real prayer is helping those in need between the calls, since service to others is worship that the Almighty never refuses.
The bell rings and the mosque fills, yet the best prayer is the hand that works unseen for others.
doha on mosque and bell, helping ppl is the real prayer

Please write a doha about how a person who does good for others without keeping a ledger of favours lives lightly and happily, while the one who counts every kindness he has done is always bitter and disappointed.
doha on helping without keeping score
My friend always reminds everyone of the favours she has done for them, and I decided to help people quietly without ever mentioning it.
The good that is counted is spent; the good that is forgotten is saved forever.
help without counting
I want a doha about the old man who applies his sacred forehead mark and then goes out to feed the hungry and carry the sick to the clinic, teaching that devotion shows in service, not outward marks.
My neighbour wears a bold forehead mark and spends every evening helping sick strangers reach the hospital, which is more than I can say for most devout people.
The mark on the brow is only a sign; the service of others is the sacred writing on the soul.
doha on a tilak person actually helping the community
tilak, selfless service
peacock, giving joy
The peacock dances for the rain-starved earth and asks no pay; so let me labour for others' joy.
doha on peacock dancing for others without payment
My neighbour's peacock-like grace shows each time she volunteers to cook for the whole building, and nobody ever thanks her but she glows.

Write a doha about the peacock who spreads his feathers in the rain to delight the village without asking for payment, and how a generous person works for others' joy and takes his own pleasure in theirs.
doha about a beggar who still helps others even though he has little
The poorest of the poor with an empty bowl may still share his smile; riches of service need no coins.
The beggar outside our station always helps the blind and the elderly across the road, even though he himself has nothing to eat.
beggar who serves
Compose a doha about the beggar who, with nothing in his bowl, still helps others cross the road and shares his last bread with a stray, proving that the habit of serving others needs no wealth.
I would like a doha about how the leaf falls to feed the soil, and the soil nourishes new growth, teaching that every ending serves a beginning and a good life gives itself to the world.
doha on a leaf falling to nourish others
The leaf gives its green to the season, then its brown to the soil; nothing in it is kept for itself.
When my grandmother's old garden shed a thousand leaves she gathered them for compost and said that is what we must do in life: give back.
leaf, giving back
doha on the forest giving everything to the world
The forest gives timber, fruit and shade, and asks nothing; this is the pattern of the noble life.
forest, selfless giving
We walked through the forest and I thought of how it gives us shade, fruit and medicine for free, and yet people go on cutting it.

Write a doha showing that the forest offers its fruit, shade and medicines to everyone, even those who come with axes, and a good person too gives his service to all without regard to who deserves it.
My friend works two jobs but still finds time to tutor neighbourhood kids for free in the evening, and says he feels richer for it.
doha on volunteering your time without pay
Compose a doha about how the best use of the time God gives us is to share it with those who need our knowledge, strength or company, since the hours spent in serving others are never lost.
give your time
Time spent on others is not spent but saved; it is stored in the hearts of those we help.
help the stranger
The one who lifts a stranger lifts himself, and no deed of service is ever small or lost.

Please write a doha showing that helping someone who has no claim on you, a stranger or a passing face, is the purest goodness, since there is no expectation of return and no weight of obligation to taint it.
doha on helping complete strangers
I paid for a stranger's medicine at the pharmacy last week and walked away before she could thank me, and felt happy all day.
Live giving all you have to the world and keeping nothing for yourself.
serve selflessly
doha on living selflessly

I want a doha that tells how a person who gives his time, skill and strength to others without asking for anything in return ends up the richest of all, because he has gathered the love of countless hearts.
Since I retired I have been teaching my neighbours' children for free, and I have never been so rich in affection.
serve before self
doha on putting other ppl first
He who serves another first has already won what matters most.
My mother always serves everyone at the table before she eats herself, and has done so for forty years without once complaining.

Please write a doha about how a person who puts the welfare of others ahead of his own comfort is the one who really lives, because the joy of helping fills him in a way that selfish pleasure never can.
Compose a doha about how the best of people never ask what they will gain from helping a neighbour, but simply see a need and meet it, and in doing so become the true benefactors of their community.
He saw a need and met it; no one asked his name, and no one needed to.
doha on those who just help without making a big deal
When the storm hit our area, a retired schoolteacher went around checking on families and quietly fixing small things, and never mentioned it afterwards.
quiet helpers
Compose a doha about the tortoise, which walks slowly but never stops, and about how a person's steady acts of kindness over many years help more people than a single grand gesture could ever do.
My grandmother carries the tortoise's patience in helping the neighbours' sick children every evening, slowly and without complaint, for thirty years now.
doha on tortoise-like slow steady kindness to others
tortoise, patient service
Slowly the tortoise walks, yet reaches all; so does patient service bless many lives.
I want a doha telling that a good deed done without hope of return comes back in unplanned ways, and those who serve the needy quietly will one day see their kindness blossom.
Do good in secret and forget it; the world will remember what you cannot.
secret good deeds
I put some money in a poor student's account anonymously years ago and recently learnt that he now treats the poor for free, and it moved me deeply.
doha on kindness coming back later in life
priest, selfless service
The priest who fasts and chants but serves no one is hollow; the one who serves is full of prayer.
doha on a priest who actually helps the villagers
Write a doha about the priest who leaves his chanting at the first cry of a neighbour in need and gives his time and strength to help, teaching that the finest rituals are acts of service.
Our village priest drops everything to carry sick people to the hospital, and I think he understands religion better than most.
In the temple of service the way is open to all, and the one who works for others needs no other altar.
temple, serve people
Outside the temple every Sunday a woman serves free meals to travellers, and I think her small kitchen is holier than the shrine behind her.
Compose a doha showing that a temple is only a building unless its devotees serve the needy, and that the person who feeds and helps others has made his own life a more sacred place than any shrine.
doha on temple vs actually serving ppl
water pot, heron, give freely
The village matron keeps a water pot outside for every passerby, and I once saw a heron drinking from it undisturbed.
doha on keeping a pot of water for passersby, heron too

Write a doha about a pot of water left at the roadside for strangers and animals alike, and the heron who comes to it, showing that giving freely without asking who drinks is the most beautiful kind of service.
The pot of water stands at the roadside for all, even the heron; thus a noble life stands for all.
doha on giving a cloth sheet to a stranger in the cold
On the coldest night of the year my father took the cloth sheet from his own bed to a homeless man shivering outside, and never mentioned it.
cloth sheet, helping stranger
Please write a doha about giving a cloth sheet to a shivering stranger on a cold night, expecting nothing in return, and how such an act warms the giver even more than the receiver.
The cloth sheet given to a shivering stranger warms the giver's soul more than the finest cloak.
To benefit another is to benefit oneself; the hands that give are always full.
do good to others
doha on how helping others helps u too

Compose a doha showing that those who spend their lives in service to others discover that service is its own reward, that giving brings more joy than receiving, and that a helpful life never feels empty.
Volunteering at the old age centre every weekend has done more for my mood than a year of therapy, and I'm grateful for it.
doha on helping a neighbour through a hard time
My neighbour's husband was in the hospital and I looked after her kids for two weeks, and I didn't even think twice about it.
I want a doha about how helping a neighbour in a hard hour without being asked is the most human duty of all, and how those who do it build a community in which no one feels alone.
help your neighbour
When trouble visits a neighbour, let your hands arrive before your words.

Write a doha about the heron who stands near the bell tower and, unlike the crowd, does not look for rewards, and about how true service is quiet, attentive and given freely like a patient watcher's care.
The heron stands at the bell tower's edge, asking nothing; the helper too keeps watch and wants no praise.
doha on bell and heron, service without wanting recognition
heron, bell, quiet service
The old gatekeeper who rings the bell at our school watches over the children like a heron and never asks for any credit.
The rope that lowers the bucket to draw water for strangers is the holiest rope of all.
rope, serving the thirsty
Please write a doha about the rope and bucket which draw water for the thirsty traveller day after day without complaint, teaching us that to serve without tiring is the highest kind of devotion.
doha on a rope and bucket giving water to travellers
My uncle spends every summer pulling the rope at the public pump, drawing water for the whole village, and he says it is his daily prayer.
cuckoo, give joy
A girl in our colony sings like a cuckoo at the community kitchen every evening and the tired workers eat with new energy.

Compose a doha about the cuckoo whose sweet voice delights everyone in the garden without asking for payment, showing that sharing one's gift with the world, whatever it may be, is the finest form of service.
doha on cuckoo giving joy to everyone
The cuckoo sings for all who pass, asking no coin; so too a gift shared is a gift doubled.
doha about a beggar who shares what little he has with other beggars
The man who begs outside our shrine split his only bread with another man who had nothing, and I felt humbled.

Please write a doha showing that the poor man who shares his meagre crust with one who has less is more generous than the rich man who gives a coin for show, because true service is measured by sacrifice.
The beggar's last crust, divided, outshines the rich man's chest of gifts, for it is given in love.
beggar sharing
My friend started a free library in his neighbourhood and refuses all donations, saying he just wants kids to read.
free service to all
Free is the service of one who gives, and no price can buy what it brings.
doha on sharing resources for free with the community

Could you write a doha about the generous person who opens his time, knowledge and belongings to the entire neighbourhood without asking a price, teaching that the best of lives are lived as a public gift?
Compose a doha about the heron who stands patiently at the edge of water in the moonlight, and about how the one who watches over others tirelessly through the night does so without need of praise.
The moon shines on the heron's watch; so does the servant's quiet vigil bless the sleeping world.
doha on heron and moon, a night watchman who serves everyone
heron, moon, silent watch
The night watchman in our colony stays awake under the moon for everyone's safety, never complaining, like a heron guarding the shore.
Write a doha about the grindstone that crushes grain to feed an entire village while asking nothing, teaching us that a life spent in humble work for others is a life of the greatest worth.
The grindstone turns for the hungry village; it asks no thanks and keeps no flour.
doha on a grindstone working for others without credit
My grandmother ground flour at the village grindstone every morning for twenty families and never took a coin for it.
grindstone, tireless service
The blind man with the forehead mark at our crossing hands out sweets to the children at festivals, and I am amazed at how he gives so freely despite his own lack.

Compose a doha about the blind man who wears the sacred mark and still finds ways to serve those around him, showing that giving does not depend on sight, wealth or strength but only on a willing heart.
tilak, blind man, serving
doha on a blind man with a tilak who helps others
Though the blind man cannot see, he serves; the mark on his brow is writ in deeds.
doha on the ocean giving to everyone, like a good person
The ocean gives its bounty and its rain to the whole coast, and my father gave the same way, freely to everyone who needed.
Please write a doha about the ocean that gives its bounty to the poor without once asking for payment, and about how a good life is an ocean of giving.
The ocean keeps nothing for itself; it rises to rain and falls to feed, a lesson of the noble heart.
ocean, generosity
doha on dew and needle, small acts of helping that add up

Write a doha about the dew that gently refreshes every blade of grass at dawn and the needle that quietly stitches what is torn, and show that small, patient acts of service quietly keep the whole world together.
dew, needle, small service
The dew refreshes the grass without a sound, the needle mends without applause; so do good souls serve.
My mother picks up a needle each night to mend the torn clothes of poor children, and each morning the dew is on the grass when they leave for school wearing them.

I'd like a doha about the elephant who carries heavy loads for the moneylender and for the village without complaint, and about how a person's strength is best used for lifting others' burdens instead of piling up his own.
doha on elephant carrying loads for others like a good person
Our moneylender's elephant carries the poor farmers' crops to town for free, and I think the animal teaches us what real strength is for.
elephant, moneylender, service
The elephant bears the moneylender's burdens and the farmer's alike; strength is a gift to be given.
doha on volunteers who clean up after floods

Please write a doha about the people who leave their own comforts to clean up after a disaster, feed the families affected and rebuild what was lost, and show that they are the living face of selfless service.
volunteers who serve
Hands that rebuild what the flood has taken are blessed; they need no name to be remembered.
After the floods our college students spent their holidays clearing mud and distributing food in the affected villages, and returned happier than from any trip.
The traveller who stops to help another on the road delays his own journey and hastens his salvation.
traveler helping travelers

Compose a doha about the traveler who pauses to help another struggling on the road, carrying his bundle or sharing his food, showing that a life of service travels farther than a life of mere pilgrimage.
doha on a traveller who helps another traveller
On my trip a fellow traveler gave me half his food and water when I ran out and refused to take any money, and I will never forget him.
stars, giving light
On a clear night the stars light the way for sleepless travellers, and I thought of my father who stayed up every night for years guiding lost villagers.
Compose a doha about the stars that shine at night for everyone without charging a price, teaching that a good person lights the path of others at the cost of his own rest and asks nothing.
The stars give light to the weary night and ask no wage; thus shines the soul that serves.
doha on stars giving light for free, like us helping others
Please write a doha about the owner of the inn who houses weary guests for free on winter nights, and the house of kindness he builds in their memory, which stays warm when all the beds are cold.
The old innkeeper at our village inn lets any stranded passenger sleep for free during the rain, and his house is always full of blessings.
The inn of the good keeps its beds for the weary, and the house of the generous never runs short.
house, inn, free shelter
doha on inn open for free for people in need
Compose a doha about the way a truly helpful person sees every other person as his own family, offering aid without checking caste, creed or status, because he knows all people are one in need.
After the earthquake, a young man in our town fed everyone who came to his place, rich or poor, familiar or stranger, and refused all thanks.
He asked not whose son you were; he saw your need and gave himself to meet it.
serve without distinction
doha on helping everybody equally

Compose a doha about the river that gives its water to fields and cities without a thought, and the philosopher's stone that changes everything it touches without keeping any wealth, showing the nature of true service.
doha on a river and the philosopher's stone, giving without pride
river, philosopher's stone, giving
Our river irrigates the whole district for nothing and my grandfather, who had a rare philosopher's stone pendant, gave out gifts the same way.
The river gives and the philosopher's stone transforms, asking nothing; so the noble life enriches without owning.
doha on the cloud giving rain without being asked, and a moneylender who doesn't
The cloud pours down on every field alike, while the moneylender counts what he has lent; learn from the cloud.
Please write a doha about the cloud that gives rain to every field without sending a bill, contrasted with the moneylender who counts every favour, and how a good person should give like the cloud.
cloud, moneylender, free giving
The village moneylender wrote down every favour he did while the old farmer who shared his water never wrote anything, and who do you think people loved more?
dew, sand, serving
doha about dew falling on sand, helping where it's hard
Compose a doha about how the dew falls gently on desert sand where nobody sees it and nobody thanks it, teaching that the best service is done in hard places and without any audience or applause.
My aunt works in a remote desert village where nothing grows but the sand shifts, and each morning the dew of her care helps the children survive.
The dew falls on barren sand, unseen; so does the servant of others give where none will thank.
The best of lives is a gift passed on; the best of hands are those that never close.

Could you write a doha showing that the purpose of strength, wealth or knowledge is to be used for the benefit of others, and that the one who holds them only for himself has wasted what he was given?
doha on using your talents to help others
I have a talent for fixing electrical things and I spend my Sundays repairing appliances for elderly neighbours who cannot afford a technician.
use gifts for others
My grandmother counted her prayer beads at dawn and tested her day at night on the touchstone of service: how many had I helped?
Write a doha about the person who turns prayer beads in the morning and then tests himself on the touchstone of service in the evening, knowing that devotion unproved by help to others is only noise.
doha on prayer beads and touchstone, service is the real test
prayer beads, service, touchstone
The beads count the Name, the touchstone counts the deed; true prayer is proved by service.
doha about a diamond and the sun, giving without taking
diamond, sun, giving
The sun gives light without a diamond's price; the diamond keeps its sparkle. Give like the sun.
Compose a doha showing that the sun gives light and warmth to all without being paid, while the diamond holds its sparkle for the few, and that a good person should choose to serve like the sun.
My grandfather, rich in diamonds, spent his last years working like the sun, quietly helping poor families rise each morning.
helping hands
After my surgery the neighbours took turns bringing meals, and I cried at how kind people can be when they see a need.
doha on neighbours who helped during my recovery
Please write a doha about the beauty of a community in which neighbours help each other through illness and hardship with no expectation of return, because such a community is a sanctuary for all.
Where hands reach out in love, no sorrow is too great, and no burden too heavy to be shared.
Give me a doha about a scholar who has read ten thousand pages yet is still as dry as cotton and as venomous as a snake in his pride, never having learned one syllable of love.
Pages turn like cotton in the wind, and the snake of pride sleeps in the learned heart; love, the one syllable, he never read.
My professor friend with four degrees speaks coldly to everyone, like a snake coiled in a bed of cotton, and I feel he never learned to love.
doha: cotton soft words, snake inside, all that reading w/o love
cotton, snake, learned fool
My uncle has a shelf of degrees and reads late into the night, yet he can't hug his own son, and I wonder what all that study gave him.
A hundred thousand pages read, and still the heart stays unlettered, for the one word of love was never learned.
doha abt how reading tons of stuff means nothing without love
I'd like a doha that says a person may read until his eyes fail and still remain unlettered, because the single syllable of love is not found on any page and is learned only in the heart.
learned yet unlettered
reading without love
I'd like a doha for the proud graduate who looks down on simple village folk, reminding him that all his reading is empty if he has not learned the one tender syllable of love.
doha on how bookish learning is useless w/o love
Though you have mastered every language, the dearest word, love, remains unread by you.
She topped her class and quotes every thinker but is lonely and cold, and I can't help thinking all that study missed the point.
Write a doha about a scholar who can untangle every line of scripture yet has not one thread of tenderness in his life, since all his reading missed the one syllable of love.
doha: tons of learning but zero thread of love in his heart lol
My cousin quotes verses all day but didn't call his sick mother once, and it felt like the thread between learning and love had snapped.
learned, thread of love

Compose a doha about a peacock dancing at ease and a fire that burns without being forced, to show that union with the Lord is also natural and spontaneous, requiring no austerity or effort of ours.
The peacock dances without a teacher, the fire burns without being told; so does the soul move into the Lord.
I watched a peacock dancing in the monsoon and a village bonfire burning by itself at night, and understood that the best things in life are spontaneous and not forced.
fire, peacock, spontaneity
doha with fire and a peacock about natural, spontaneous union
sun and leaf doha - union is natural, like a leaf turning to the sun
Write a doha about a leaf that turns toward the sun without effort or thought, as the soul turns to the Lord in its natural state, without austerity or force, simply because that is its nature.
The leaf on my desk plant leans toward the sun every day without any effort, and I thought: if only my spiritual life were that easy and natural.
The leaf turns to the sun without a plan; the soul turns to the Lord without a vow.
sun, leaf, effortless turning
After I stopped chasing achievements and spiritual goals, I discovered a quiet sweetness in simply being present at my own life, as though it was always there.
Put down the burden of becoming, and find that you already are what you sought, in the Lord.
I want a doha about the state of simple, easy union with the Lord that needs no goal, no technique and no force, because it is not something to be achieved but something already present.
already here, no striving
doha about how union with God is already here, no need to strive
crow and boat doha - union is easy, drifting not rowing
crow, boat, drifting oneness
Please write a doha about a boat that drifts with the current and a crow that rides on it without effort, showing the soul that rests in the Lord without strain, drifting in natural union.
On a ferry ride I watched a crow ride on the boat's roof all the way across, utterly relaxed, and I thought how little force it takes to arrive anywhere.
The boat drifts, the crow rests on its mast, and the Lord carries all who do not row against Him.
fish doha - union is as natural as a fish in water
Write a doha about a fish that swims in water without ever thinking about it, as the soul lives in the Lord without strain or austerity, as naturally as a fish in its element.
fish, natural oneness
My uncle, a fisherman, never thinks about how to swim and neither do the fish he catches, and he says that is how God should be known: without thinking.
The fish never seeks the water, yet lives in it; so is the soul in the Lord, effortlessly.
doha about letting things be and finding peace without trying
Compose a doha about a seeker who gave up all striving, all fasting and all hard effort, and found at last that the peace he sought was his natural condition, easy and always present.
When I finally stopped fighting my own restless mind and just let it be, the calm that settled in was greater than any I had forced through years of discipline.
let be, find peace
Let the wave be a wave and the mind be a mind; in not resisting, the Lord is found.
Sweet as the breath is union with the Lord, needing no practice but the remembering of what is.
Write a doha about the state of oneness with the Lord that is as natural as breathing, requiring no instrument, no austerity and no force, only the ease of recognizing what has always been so.
doha on union that's as easy and natural as breathing
Last night I noticed my own breath for the first time in years, and felt, with no effort at all, that I was being held by something larger.
breath, ease, oneness
yogi, effortless oneness
A yogi in our hill town gave up his hard postures and now sits laughing under the sky, and he says that is when he finally found what he had been searching for.
yogi doha - union is natural and easy, you can stop forcing it
The yogi unties his knotted limbs and finds the Lord waiting in the ease of his breath.
Write a doha about a yogi who struggled for decades with painful postures and finally relaxed, discovering the natural, effortless state of union with the Lord that required no force at all.
Write a doha about a weaver at his loom who works in effortless rhythm, neither forcing nor resisting, finding the natural union with the Lord in the simple ease of his craft.
My father works at his loom without any apparent effort, and when I asked how he stays so calm, he said the rhythm does the work and he just goes along.
weaver's loom doha about easy natural union with God
weaver's loom, ease
The loom hums and the weaver's mind goes still; in that hush, without effort, the Lord arrives.
Our fishing boat drifted all night after the engine failed, and in the quiet I heard a rainbird calling and felt a deep ease that I had never found through effort.

Please write a doha about a boat floating with no one rowing it and a rainbird singing from the shore, showing the state of ease in which the soul is united with the Lord without any force or struggle.
boat, rainbird, ease
The boat drifts and the rainbird sings; no one is rowing, and the Lord is near.
boat and rainbird doha - letting go and finding union naturally
The moneylender strains to count, the bell strains to ring, but the soul rests in the Lord with ease.
Compose a doha about a moneylender who strains all day over his accounts while a bell rings out on the hour, and the quiet soul beside them rests in effortless union with the Lord.
moneylender and bell doha - union is easy, not a hard task
The moneylender in my village works himself ragged and rings a bell to start each business day, but his quiet old mother, who does no practice, seems more in tune with God.
moneylender, bell, ease
Salt dissolves in water without effort; so the soul dissolves into the Lord, easily, entirely.
salt doha about merging with God naturally and without force
Write a doha about salt that dissolves into water without any strain or austerity, as the soul merges into the Lord in its natural, effortless state of union, leaving no trace of effort behind.
salt, effortless merging
I stirred salt into a glass of water and watched it vanish with no effort, and I thought how my own spiritual striving could have been as easy as that.
doha on the easy, natural way to find peace with God
Do nothing, force nothing, seek nothing, and the Beloved arrives of His own accord.
I used to think peace had to be fought for, but then I stopped trying on a quiet Sunday and noticed the contentment had been there waiting the whole time.
no effort, no force
Compose a doha for the weary seeker who has tried too hard and failed, telling him that union with the Lord is the easiest of all things, natural and simple, and asks nothing but ease.

Please write a doha about a beggar who sits at ease by the roadside without a worry in the world, enjoying the natural, effortless union with the Lord that kings and ascetics strive in vain to achieve.
beggar, effortless union
The beggar sits at ease while kings strain; the Lord rests in the heart that has nothing to achieve.
beggar doha about how natural and easy being one with God is
The beggar at the corner never meditates or fasts but seems so naturally content that I once found myself envying him more than the people who live by strict spiritual rules.
market, musk deer, effortless oneness
The market was loud and busy, yet a woman selling musk perfume sat in complete ease among it all, and I could tell she was naturally united with something deeper.
Write a doha about a musk deer that carries its own fragrance without effort, and a market full of strain, showing that union with the Lord is natural and needs no seeking, force or hard labour.
musk deer and market doha - union with God is natural, not forced
The musk deer never works to make its scent; so the soul in the Lord is fragrant without effort.
After the birth of my child, I stopped doing every spiritual practice I had forced myself through, and strangely found a continuous quiet joy that effort had never given me.

Compose a doha about the state of effortless union with the Lord that arrives not through disciplines or forced practice but through a natural softening of the heart, and remains in every ordinary moment.
ease, softness, union
doha on the effortless union that comes when you stop forcing the practice
When the heart grows soft as morning, the Lord moves in without a knock, and nothing is forced.
Cotton of every field goes into the furnace alike, and comes out as the same glowing ember; who then is high, who low?
doha pls: cotton from any field burns the same in the furnace, so why do we call each other high and low
cotton, furnace, no castes
At the mill where I work, the owner's son and the sweeper's son both fainted in the furnace heat during the cotton drying, and the same doctor treated both; I'd love a doha on that.
I want a doha saying that all people, rich and poor, upper and lower, are like cotton from the same field, and when the furnace of life reaches them there is no difference in how they burn.
Every drop in the ocean is kin to every other; no wave is higher in the eyes of the deep.
doha plz: every stream ends up in the ocean, so there's no high and low among people
ocean, one humanity
My neighbour looks down on our family because we are poor, but at the beach last summer his child and mine played in the same ocean and neither could tell whose waves were whose; write a doha.

Compose a doha explaining that just as every stream, clear or muddy, joins the ocean and becomes one with it, all human beings return to the same Maker, so none should be proud or look down on another.
The salt of the king's table and the salt of the pauper's bowl was gathered from the same waters.
Write a doha that says the same salt seasons the food of the rich and the poor, and the same Creator made both, so those who boast of birth or wealth have forgotten how alike they are at their root.
salt, same for all
doha pls: salt for the rich and the poor is the same salt, so why the pride
At my cousin's wedding, the cook used the same salt for the guests' plates and for the servants' plates, and I thought how silly it is that we still sit at separate tables; please write a doha.
Whether a mark is drawn on the forehead of the priestly or the labourer, the same breath moves beneath it.

Please craft a couplet that says a mark on the forehead or a sacred string on the shoulder does not raise one man above another, because the Maker looks at the heart and sees every person as the same.
forehead mark, no castes
My upper-caste friend wears a forehead mark and refuses to eat with our family, though when his father was sick it was my father who gave blood; I would like a doha for him.
doha pls: the forehead mark doesn't make you better than anyone, we all come from the same source
Write a doha saying that in the forest, when thirst comes, the tongue of the rich and poor long for the same drop, and no one asks the caste or name of the one who brings the water.
We got lost in a forest on a trek, and the tribal guide who showed us the way shared his water with a banker and a student alike, never once asking who they were; please write a doha about it.
doha pls: in the forest all animals drink the same water and no tongue asks about caste
tongue, forest, one humanity
In the forest every tongue thirsts alike, and the same stream quenches the proud and the lowly.
I want a doha saying that humans are all made of the same breath and the same light, and that titles, wealth and birth are names we ourselves invent and the Maker never recognises them.
At the hospital, when my child was born, I saw a rich woman and a poor woman crying out in the same pain and holding the same newborn joy; make a doha out of what I felt.
doha idea: everyone is the same in front of the Creator
all are equal
The Maker looks upon the lord and the labourer with the same loving eye; why then do we divide?

doha pls: a skeleton doesn't tell you caste or wealth, think about that
Strip away the skin and the silk, and the skeleton smiles the same smile for king and sweeper alike.
Compose a doha that says if you look at the bones of a rich man and a poor man there is nothing to tell them apart, so what cause has anyone to be proud of birth or wealth?
skeleton, no distinction
no high, no low
From one source we all came, to one source we go; who then can stand above another?
My grandfather was a clerk and my grandmother a farmer's daughter, and they raised us to touch every elder's feet without asking their background; write a doha in their spirit.
Make me a doha that says every human being is born the same way, cries the same first cry, and feels the same hunger and love, so the walls of caste are made by men, not by the Maker.
doha pls: stop dividing people into high and low, it's all the same human
The needle stitches silk and sackcloth alike, and the chakor loves its distant beloved without asking who is watching.

Compose a doha saying that a needle does not ask whether it is sewing a prince's robe or a pauper's shirt, and so a wise soul sees with the chakor's single-hearted love, finding no difference between persons.
chakor, needle, same maker

doha plz: even the chakor and a needle don't care who owns them, and God doesn't care who we are, all equal
The pot of water gives its coolness to the lord and the lowly, and the cotton warms both without question.
pot of water, cotton
doha pls: a pot of water is the same for everyone, the thirsty doesn't ask whose pot, cotton is the same too

Compose a doha that says the pot of water placed on the roadside quenches the thirst of the high-born and the low-born alike, and cotton covers every body without choosing, teaching us to give without discrimination.
Can you make a doha that says the bier is the last bed of the lord and the labourer, and once the heron-like silence of the cremation falls, no one remembers the caste or rank people were proud of.
The bier waits for the proud and the humble alike, and the heron stands at the water's edge, watching all pass.
Both the minister's father and the sweeper's father were carried on the same kind of bier when they died, and it was the same heron-white sky above both, I noticed; write a doha.
bier, heron, same end
doha: a bier carries everyone, the rich and poor, even a heron would see no difference
thorn, no caste
The thorn pricks the prince's foot and the pauper's foot with the same pain; pain knows no rank.
doha pls: a thorn hurts the rich and poor in the same way, we all feel pain the same
A thorn went into my friend's foot on a trip, and the village boy and the city boy cried out in the same words and bled the same red; write a doha about it.
Please write a doha showing that a thorn wounds the rich and poor equally, the blood and the pain are the same, and so we should treat each other with the same care and not with the pride of rank.

yogi, salt, all equal
Write a doha that says a true yogi sees no division between high and low, as the salt that seasons a king's meal also seasons a servant's, and the one who sees this has seen the Maker.
doha pls: a yogi sees everyone as the same, just like salt is the same in any food
doha pls: the winnowing fan separates grain from chaff, not rich from poor, God sees our hearts only

chakor, winnowing fan, no pride

doha idea: everyone's equal, no one's better
My daughter came back from school and asked why some kids won't sit with others, and I did not know what to say; I need a doha for her.

net, rainbird, same fate
doha pls: the net of fate catches everyone, rich or poor, and the rainbird drinks the same rain as everyone

salt, one humanity

doha pls: sand doesn't care who walks on it and every tongue speaks the same truth at the end
The sand on the beach holds the footprints of a rich tourist and a poor vendor, and the waves wash both away; the tongue of time, I thought, speaks the same to all. Write a doha.
tongue, sand, no rank
Compose a doha that says the sand under the feet of kings and paupers is the same, and the tongue that speaks of rank will be silenced in the end by the same dust, so speak kindly.

musk deer, no rank
doha: a musk deer's scent is the same wherever it goes, in a mansion or in a hut

doha pls: langar-style, everybody eats together, no high and low
same row, same food

Seated in one row on the floor, the lord and the labourer share a single bread.
snake, all equal

doha pls: a snake bites everyone, and death comes for everyone, nobody's special

thorn, elephant, same pain

shroud, same end

doha pls: a moneylender and his debtor both sit by the same fire in the end

The moneylender's coins and the debtor's rags both feed the same fire at the end; the blaze knows no creditor.

musk deer, oil press

Write a doha that says the oil press gives the same oil no matter whose harvest it presses, and the musk deer gives its scent to all who pass, teaching that real worth is shared with everyone equally.
I want a doha that says humans are all made of the same substance and the same breath, that no title, wealth or skin can make one soul better than another, and that kindness is the only true height.
The Maker makes no mistakes in His making; each life is as precious as the next.
equal in creation
doha pls on how we're all equal in the eyes of God
My teacher once made the whole class stand in a line to show that, when we all stand, no one is taller by birth; I'd like a doha based on that.
My mother sat at the spinning wheel every morning in the first sun and spun for any family that needed it, whether high or low, and I'd like a doha that honours her.
sun, spinning wheel, all equal

Make me a doha that says the sun gives its warmth to the rich and the poor in the same measure, and the spinning wheel makes yarn for any hand that asks, showing that the Maker gives without choosing.
doha pls: the sun shines on everyone the same, and the spinning wheel doesn't spin for the rich only
Please compose a doha showing that when the one-string lute sings the song of the Maker, the high and the low listen with the same tears, as every heart is moved by the same truth.
The one-string lute plays the same note for the lord and the poor, and the heart that hears it weeps the same tears.
doha pls: a one-string lute plays the same music for everyone, music has no caste
one-string lute, one tune

Compose a doha that says the buyer in the market does not receive a different leaf for his rank, and so we should respect one another equally, because in the final market of life all are weighed alike.
market, leaf, same respect
doha pls: a leaf in the market sells for the same price whoever buys it, so should respect
In the market every leaf is weighed alike, and so are souls in the eyes of the Maker.
My uncle plays a one-string lute at the gatherings and draws a pot of water for each person who comes, whoever they are; write a doha for him.
The one-string lute sings and the pot of water cools, for lord and servant with a single grace.
Can you make a doha that says the music of the one-string lute and the cool water of the pot are shared without rank, showing a way of life in which everyone is welcomed to drink and to listen.
doha pls: a one-string lute and a pot of water for everyone, no division
lute, pot of water, everyone

The cotton blooms white in the field of the rich and the poor, and makes the same warm garment for both.
cotton, same fibre
doha pls: cotton is cotton, whether it's worn by a queen or a farmer, so people are people

sword, scales, same justice

doha: the sword of justice and the scales see no caste, no rank

Before the sword and the scales, the king and the commoner stand alike; justice has no favourite.
tree, leaf, one root
doha pls: leaves on the same tree are different but they share the same root, people too
In our courtyard the old tree had leaves of every size, and as kids we used to say the big ones were better, until my grandmother told us they all came from one root; write a doha.
Every leaf on the tree is different, yet each drinks from the same root; so are we, children of one.
Pen a doha saying that the leaves of one tree differ in size and shade, but each draws life from the same root and falls the same way, so people of different castes and ranks are of one origin.
The sun burns on all, the pot of water cools all; neither asks for a name.
In the heat of summer, the pot of water by the road was used by farmers and officers alike, and nobody asked who touched it; write a doha about the sun and the pot.

Please write a doha that says the sun shines on all heads and the pot of water by the road quenches every thirst, and so should the human heart give without checking the caste of the person who receives.
doha pls: the sun shines and a pot of water cools anyone, they don't ask caste
pot of water, sun
everyone is the same
I want a doha saying that rank and caste are ideas that humans invented late in the story, that the Maker never wrote them into any heart, and that the true saint looks upon everyone as his own.
doha pls: no one is better than anyone else
In the Maker's eye there is no crown and no rag; every soul is a ray of the same light.
I stopped asking people their surname at work because I realised it didn't change anything about who they are; write a doha.
doha pls: the lotus and sandalwood treat everyone with the same fragrance, so should we
The lotus opens for every eye, the sandalwood scents every hand; so should the heart be for all.
lotus, sandalwood, equal love
My grandmother planted a lotus pond and a sandalwood by the gate, and she let every child, of any caste, pick the flowers and smell the wood; make a doha for her.

Write a doha that says the lotus gives its beauty and sandalwood gives its fragrance to every person without discrimination, so a good human being should give his love and kindness to all with the same generosity.
I want a doha for my school assembly, saying that the Maker made all humans from the same breath and the same light, and anyone who builds walls between persons is going against the Maker's wish.
doha pls: caste is man-made, God never made it
no caste, no rank
Who made the barrier that divides the high from the low? Not the Maker; man alone has made it.
A boy in my class was banned from the shrine because of his birth, and I felt ashamed; I need a doha for this.
doha pls: the winnowing fan blows away the chaff regardless of the farmer's caste
Compose a doha showing that the winnowing fan treats every harvest the same, and in the same way the Maker sifts every soul by its goodness, not by the family or the title it was born with.
