After the festival dip, my cousin boasted that he had washed away all his faults and promptly picked up his old quarrel with his brother. A doha for him?
The singer on the bank of the holy waters plays his one-string lute after bathing, and sings about purity, but he bullies the little boy who carries his bag. Doha about him?
A doha about the singer who bathes in the holy waters at dawn, plays a one-string lute and sings of purity to the crowd, though his mind is full of vanity and not even a note of humility.
One-string lute in tune, body bathed, mind out of tune with its Maker.
one-string lute, holy bath
doha: one-string lute and a holy dip, still not clean inside
My grandfather bathed daily in a holy tank for sixty years, and when I asked him whether it had helped, he smiled and said, 'It cleaned the dirt, not the debts.' Doha on this?
doha: bathing for sixty years and still thinking dirty thoughts
lifelong bathing, no purity
Sixty years of bathing, and not a day without a grudge.

Compose a doha on the man who has bathed daily in the sacred waters for sixty years and still holds old grudges, still envies his neighbours, still cheats the poor, and still believes himself to be a pure man.
A verse about the furnace of the mind, which burns with desire and anger even after the pot of water has been poured, and the holy bath is no more effective than pouring a pot of water on it.
furnace, pot of water, bath
Pour a pot of water on the furnace, and it only hisses; bathe in holy waters, the mind only burns.
In our village the potter's furnace roars all day, and the old men say the bath in the holy pond is like pouring a pot of water on it, it cools the skin and nothing else. Doha?
doha: pouring a pot of water on a furnace, like bathing to wash the mind
The mountain meets the mosque in the sacred waters, but the man that dips remains small.
We drove to a holy ghat at the foot of a mountain, next to a mosque, and people from both faiths were bathing and arguing over parking. It made me think. Doha?
mountain, mosque, ablution

A doha about the believers at the foot of the mountain, one group bathing in the sacred waters and the other washing before the mosque, each thinking their washing purifies, while only the mind needs it.
doha: bathing near the mountain and the mosque, rituals of washing but same dirty minds
He bathes the body in holy waters, but who bathes the mind in the waters of love?
I asked my friend why he goes to bathe at every major festival, and he said, 'To wash away sins.' But he was the one who owes me money for three years. Can you write a doha?
write a doha about dirty minds and clean bodies
A Kabir style doha: if bathing in the holy waters could end sin, it would be a bargain for every sinner, and the pious would avoid the bath most, for they most believe in it.
clean body, dirty mind
salt, potter and clay, bathing

A doha about how salt dissolves in water and the potter shapes clay with water, but no amount of water will dissolve the salt of pride or soften the hard clay of the heart that does not wish to change.
Salt melts in the sacred waters and clay softens in the potter's hands, but the salt of pride does not.
doha: potter and clay and salt, water can't fix the mind
In our colony the potter says that clay gets softer with water, and salt melts too, but my neighbour who bathes every morning remains hard and bitter. Doha for him?
The shadow bathes along with the body and emerges as dark as before.
A verse about the pilgrim who bathes and tells himself he has left his sins behind in the sacred waters, though his shadow, which is his own conduct, stays attached and follows him up the bank.
shadow, holy dip
doha: your shadow comes out of the water with you
I saw my own shadow on the wet steps at the ghat after the dip and thought, if the sins were gone the shadow might lighten too. Can you make a doha from that?
A bottle of holy water for a hot temper; the cure is quiet within.
My aunt visits the holy waters every full night of the month to wash away family sins and brings back a bottle of water for us all. She thinks it will cure my bad temper. Doha?

Write a doha about the people who carry home a jar of sacred water from the pilgrimage and sprinkle it over the family, believing it cleans them of all faults, while no one cleans the habits that make faults.
doha on bringing home holy water as a cure for sins
holy water, no cure
thief, holy dip
doha: a thief takes a holy dip and goes back to stealing
The thief bathes in sacred waters, then returns to the dark street with clean hands.
A doha about the thief who goes to the sacred waters, bathes, prays for forgiveness, and goes straight to his next robbery, thinking the bath has made him fresh and his sins forgotten.
The thief who robbed our family store last year went on a pilgrimage and bathed in the holy waters, and was back to his old tricks within a month. A doha?
doha: bathing at the well every morning and lying all day
My grandmother said the old well in our village has holy water because pilgrims used to bathe there, but the neighbour who bathes in it daily cheats at cards. A doha?
Write a doha on the man who draws water from the well every morning, bathes with great ceremony, and then tells lies all day to everyone he meets, treating the bath as a shield for his character.
Bathing at the well each dawn, he draws up nothing but the water.
well, bathing, hollow
The lion tamer in our circus bathed in the holy waters before each show and said it protected him, but the lion bit him anyway. A doha for that irony?
A doha about the lion which fears no sin and is never bathed in the sacred waters, yet lives truthfully by its nature, while the pilgrim who bathes daily lives in falsehood by his choices.
The lion needs no holy bath, and its nature is clean; the pilgrim bathes and his nature is not.
doha: lion doesn't need a bath to be pure, humans do and still fail
lion, holy bath

A doha on the elephant, which bathes in the water and throws dust on its back the moment it comes out, like the pilgrim and the priest who bathe in the holy waters and then plunge again into their sins.
elephant, priest, holy bath
The elephant bathes and throws dust on its back; the priest bathes and throws sin on his soul.
At the ghat, an elephant bathed and then threw dust on itself, and the priest next to me who had just finished his own bath laughed, then immediately cursed a rickshaw driver. Doha on this?
doha: elephant bathes and throws dust right after, like a priest after a holy dip
doha: counting prayer beads in the holy dip, mind not in it
Prayer beads dripping with holy water, a mind dry as dust.
prayer beads, bath

A doha about the pilgrim who stands in the holy waters turning prayer beads, mumbling chants, believing both the water and the beads have cleansed him, though his mind is somewhere far, busy with trade and gossip.
I saw a woman in the holy waters rolling her prayer beads with a faraway look, and then complaining loudly at the person next to her. A doha for her?

Write about the tongue that chants holy names after the sacred bath and also spreads cruel gossip before the day is over, as the pilgrim crosses the bridge to the holy bank to wash and returns the same.
doha: tongue says holy names after a holy dip then gossips, bridge to the bank
tongue, bridge, bathing
The tongue bathed and sings; the bridge to the heart remains uncrossed.
After his holy dip, my uncle's tongue was as sharp as ever and he crossed the bridge to the stalls and started bargaining for the cruelest price. A doha for him?

A verse about the pilgrim who journeys a thousand miles to bathe in the sacred waters and complains of the cost, the cold, the crowds and his companions, as though purity could be bought without patience.
costly pilgrimage, complaints
doha: he travelled for the holy bath but complained the whole way
He crossed half the land to be purified, and brought his grumbling along.
My uncle took a long train journey for the holy dip and grumbled about the food and bunks from start to finish. A doha, please?
The sand on the bank holds the pilgrims' footprints and a one-string lute's last note; the same sand holds the same sins.
doha: sand on the bank, a one-string lute playing, pilgrims washing, still sinners

A doha about the pilgrims who gather on the sand at the water's edge, listening to a one-string lute and bathing at dawn, who go home with grains of sand in their sandals and the same sin in their hearts.
On the sand by the holy waters a man sat playing a one-string lute while the pilgrims bathed, and one of them stole his bowl while he played. Can you do a doha on this?
sand, one-string lute, bathing
Wash the body, wash the body, and the mind laughs behind its mask.
doha on how rituals for cleansing dont work if your mind is dirty
My brother dips into the holy waters every year and never apologizes to our sister for the way he treated her. Is there a doha for him?
Compose a doha on the one who believes that his annual bath in the sacred waters will cancel all his debts to people and to God, though there is not a trace of repentance in his heart.
annual bath, no repentance
My friend's grandfather says he bathed in all seven holy places in his life, and still he cannot sit for a minute in peace. A doha about his journey?
seven holy baths
A doha about the old man who has bathed in all the holy places in the land, collected all the sacred water in bottles, and yet finds no peace within, because he sought it in water and not in himself.
He has bathed in every holy water, and thirsts still.
doha: bathed everywhere, still restless
In the temple waters pilgrims wash and anoint with sandalwood, but the Lord waits in the clean heart alone.
Our temple has a sacred tank where everyone bathes before darshan, then smears sandalwood on their foreheads and leaves a trail of litter. Doha for our temple?
temple, bath, sandalwood
doha: bathing at the temple tank and putting on sandalwood but being rude
Compose a doha about the devotees who bathe at the temple tank, apply sandalwood paste to their skin, and walk in to pray, though their conduct outside the temple is rude, selfish and deceitful.
doha: the cleric says wash before prayer but not the mind
Wash the hands, wash the feet, wash the face; says the cleric, and the mind sits unwashed in the front row.
The cleric near us makes everyone wash carefully before prayer but gossips about members of the congregation. A doha, please?
A doha on the cleric who insists on the correct washing before prayer, hands, mouth, and feet, but never asks how the washing can matter if the thoughts are unwashed and the speech is unkind.
cleric, washing, hollow
bier, mosque, washing
Whether the body is washed for the mosque or for the bier, the one who washes it is what matters.

A doha on how we wash before the mosque, and wash the body before the bier, all for the sake of outer cleanliness, while the one thing that needs washing, the heart, is left unwashed until the very last moment.
doha: washing before the mosque and washing the body for the bier, same thing
When my uncle died, the elders washed his body for the bier with great care and the same men washed at the mosque before prayer, and no one asked about the heart. Doha?

A doha about the yogi who bathes daily in the holy waters and fasts to keep his body pure, but who feels anger rise the moment anyone interrupts his meditation, proving that water has not touched the mind.
yogi, holy bath
A yogi at our village pond bathes every dawn and sits with eyes shut, but throws a fit if a child splashes near him. Could you write a doha?
The yogi bathed his body, and his temper bathed in the same water.
doha: yogi takes holy baths and gets angry anyway
bath, bad habits
doha: wash away sins by bathing seems too easy
My roommate takes a long bath every Sunday and says it washes away his week's mistakes. By Monday he's in the same bad habits again. Doha for this?
Sunday's bath, Monday's sin; the cycle goes on like a wheel of wash and mud.

Write a doha on the person who bathes at the start of every week believing the water washes his faults, and finds that every week the same faults return, because water does not change what the mind chooses.
At the crossroads of the pilgrim path the beggar sits unwashed; the pilgrim passes by with his clean skin and a closed hand.

A doha about the pilgrim who bathes in the holy waters and walks to the crossroads, where a beggar sits shivering and hungry, and passes him by as if the beggar did not exist, his purity being only skin deep.
doha: pilgrim after his holy dip ignores a beggar at the crossroads
crossroads, beggar, holy bath
After bathing in the holy waters, our family walked past a beggar at the crossroads without a glance, and the thought stayed with me. Could you write a doha?
The mirror shows a clean face after the bath, and the snake of anger sleeps coiled behind it.
After my holy bath, I looked into the mirror and saw a clean face, and then a snake of a thought crossed my mind about a rival. Could you write a doha for this?
A doha on how the mirror reflects the washed face of the pilgrim who has bathed in the sacred waters, but cannot show the snake of poison coiled in his mind, which has remained unwashed.
mirror, snake, bathing
doha: mirror shows clean face, snake in the heart after a holy dip
doha: stuck in a cage of bad habits wrapped in a shroud of ego even after holy baths
A doha about the bird in a cage who bathes daily in the water bowl its keeper provides, and the pilgrim wrapped in a shroud of habit who bathes daily in the holy waters, neither of them any freer.
The bird bathes in its cage; the pilgrim bathes in a shroud of habit.
cage, shroud, holy dip
My grandmother, who has hardly left her room for years like a bird in a cage, takes the longest baths and asks if a shroud would be cleaner. Doha for that?
palace, paras, bath
doha: palace bath, the paras alchemist's touch, none of it cleans the mind
Neither the marble palace baths nor the legendary paras, the alchemist's touch, can wash the mind.
The king of our local story bathed daily in his palace with scented oils and sought the paras, the alchemist's touch, to cleanse himself, but never his heart. Doha idea?

A doha on the ruler in his palace who searches for the paras, the alchemist's touch, and bathes in fragrant waters daily to be pure, though neither the search nor the bath can scrub the arrogance from his mind.
peacock, holy bath
A doha about the peacock which dances in the rain without any ritual and is more beautiful than the pilgrim who dips in the sacred waters each year, with all his rites and none of the natural joy.
The peacock in our garden dances in the rain, no bath needed, while my uncle goes to bathe in the holy waters every year and remains grumpy. Doha on that?
The peacock dances in the rain, free of the holy dip, and the bathed pilgrim does not dance.
doha: peacock in the rain is purer than the pilgrim who bathes
A doha about the one who prides himself on how many times he has bathed in the sacred waters, counts the dips like a miser counts coins, and thinks the count is the measure of his purity.
counting holy dips
Count the dips, count the sins; the number of one does not cancel the other.
doha: counting your holy dips like points
My uncle keeps a diary of every holy dip he has taken, thirty one so far, and he is rude to every waiter he meets. Doha?
A doha about the leaf which floats on the water and is never wet, like the mind of one who truly knows, while the pilgrim who bathes in the sacred waters is soaked and the mind stays dry.
doha: the leaf floats on water but never gets wet, a metaphor for holy dips
I watched a leaf float on the water at the ghat while pilgrims bathed, and the leaf looked cleaner than any of them. Can you write a doha?
leaf, holy water
The leaf floats on the water untouched; the pilgrim bathes in it and is not cleansed.
The traveler washes his feet at the holy ghat and carries a jar of milk to offer, but not a drop to the hungry on the way.
A doha on the traveler who stops at the holy waters, bathes with a clean conscience, offers milk to the sacred bank, and passes by the hungry child on the road without a word or a coin.
traveler, milk, holy dip
On our trip to the holy dip, a traveler carried milk in a pot to offer at the water, while his own child was begging for a glass. A doha for that scene?
doha: traveler pouring milk into the holy water instead of giving it to hungry people
With a needle of patience I stitch my bridal veil; the Bridegroom is coming, and my whole soul is the bride.
doha on the soul as a bride dressed for her divine groom, with a needle
the bride's needle
My grandmother still sews a little with her needle every evening and says she is readying herself for her wedding with God.
I sat all night stitching my wedding veil with a fine needle, one tiny stitch for each day I have waited for the Groom, and I feel like a bride preparing to meet the Divine. Please write that doha.
bride, mountain, sword
doha with a mountain and a sword about the soul as bride waiting for God
The bride waits at the foot of the mountain with a sword laid at her side as a sign that she is ready to give up everything; compose a doha about the soul as a bride awaiting her Lord.
Our village bride walked up the mountain path at dawn with her father's old sword in the procession, and the whole valley rang with songs.
Mountain behind and sword beside, the bride awaits her Groom, her heart a drum before the wedding.
The traveler tastes the bitter gourd and moves on, but the bride stays, for her feast is the Groom's arrival.
doha with a traveler and a bitter gourd at a soul's wedding to the divine
A traveler passing the wedding tent tasted a bitter gourd curry and said the sweetest feast is the marriage of the soul with God; write a long doha in the voice of the bride waiting for her Groom.
traveler, bitter gourd, bride
A traveler stayed for my cousin's wedding dinner and the bitter gourd was the only dish he praised, saying she would be happy with her husband.
I am the bride and the Lord is my Bridegroom, and I have put on red and applied henna, waiting at the edge of the courtyard for his arrival; please write me a doha about this longing joy.
the soul's wedding
At my cousin's wedding the aunties kept saying you are marrying the Lord when you serve him, and she smiled and sat very quietly.
Adorned with devotion, I wait for my Groom, who is the Lord of all the worlds.
doha about the soul as a bride waiting for the divine husband
My grandmother told me that in her village the bride crossed the old bridge to her husband's place with a shroud in her trunk, to show she would never return.
The bride crosses the bridge, her shroud in the trunk; she dies to her maiden self to live in the Groom's village.
doha on a bride crossing a bridge with a shroud, soul going to the divine husband
On the wedding morning the bride crosses a bridge toward her husband's village, carrying a white shroud folded in her trunk as the old custom says, for she has died to her old life; write a doha.
bridge, shroud, bride
can u do a doha about the soul as bride waiting for her husband the divine
My sister is trying on her wedding sari tonight and her eyes are wet and shining as though she were marrying God himself.
The wedding drums are beating in my heart and I feel the Bridegroom is near, so I have decorated myself with devotion and put on my finest sari; please write a doha about the soul as a bride waiting.
bride and wedding
The wedding sounds within; the bride is ready and the Groom is at the edge of the village.
The cloud parts, the sun looks down, and the bride lifts her veil for the Husband she has waited for.
The wedding was nearly rained out, but a cloud moved and the sun came out just as my cousin took the vows, and the aunties called it a sign.
doha with clouds and sun at a soul's wedding to God
cloud, sun, the bride's veil
Clouds gathered above the wedding tent and a ray of the sun broke through at the very moment the bride lifted her veil, as though the Groom himself blessed her; compose a doha.
The parrot repeats the Groom's name; the arrow of longing strikes the bride, sweetly, and she smiles.
Our parrot has learned to say the name of the Lord, and my daughter, who is to marry soon, says it hits her like an arrow of joy.
My parrot recites the Groom's name and an arrow of joy goes through me whenever I think of him, since I am the bride and he is my Lord; write a long doha that puts this into verse.
doha with a parrot and an arrow about the soul as a bride of the Lord
parrot and arrow, bride
My grandmother gave my sister a small lock for her wedding trunk and said her shadow will follow her to her husband's village; both cried.
doha with a lock and a shadow about the soul as bride going to her husband
The bride locks her trunk with a small lock and hides the key near her heart, for it holds the dowry of her devotion for the Lord, and her shadow follows her as she walks toward her Groom's village.
The bride locks her trunk and keeps the key, her shadow walking beside her toward the Groom.
lock and shadow, bride
In the mirror I looked for my face and found the Groom's; the bride has become the beloved.
bride's mirror
doha with a mirror in which the bride sees her divine groom
My niece stared into the mirror on her wedding morning, said she could not recognise herself, and then laughed that she looked like a bride of God.
The bride looks in the mirror and sees not her own face but the face of the Bridegroom looking back at her, because the soul and the Lord have already become one; write me a doha.
The bier goes by, the bride waits; she tests the Groom on the touchstone and finds he is the Lord.
Right when my aunt was being dressed as a bride, a bier went down our street, and she said every wedding is a funeral for the old self, a touchstone of the heart.
doha with a bier and a touchstone for a bride waiting for the divine groom
bier, touchstone, bride
A bier was passing by the road while the bride waited with a touchstone in her hand, to test that the Groom is true metal; write me a doha on the bride-soul's wedding, long and thoughtful.
The bride chose the lion, the others turned back; her Husband is the Lord, king of every wild place.
doha about a bride choosing the lion-hearted divine groom
Like a bride who has chosen the lion over all other suitors, I wait for the strong Groom; please write a doha in which the soul is the bride and the divine is her fearless husband, a lion among men.
bride and lion
My cousin refused every rich suitor and finally married a quiet man everyone calls the lion of our village; she says she chose rightly.
short doha: soul as a bride waiting for her husband the divine
the bride and her Husband

Please write a doha in which the soul is a bride on the eve of her wedding, trembling with expectation, adorned in bangles and vermilion, and quietly counting the hours until the Bridegroom arrives for her at last.
The bride counts the hours in joy until her Husband comes.
My sister is getting married on Sunday and every time her phone buzzes she blushes as though God himself had called.
doha with a heron and a bridge about the real bride-soul going to the husband
A heron was standing near the bridge when my cousin's wedding procession passed, and my uncle joked that the true bride has no need to pretend.

A heron stood on the edge of the bridge watching the wedding party, pretending to be calm but eyeing the sweets, while the bride passed on, serene and sincere; compose a doha in which the soul is the true bride.
heron, bridge, true bride
The heron pretends on the bridge; the bride walks over it with no pretending, for her Husband waits across.
doha with a moon and a churn at the soul's wedding to the divine groom
moon, churn, the bride sings
On the night before the wedding the village women sat churning under the moon and sang about the bride going to meet her Lord.
The moon looks down, the churn turns, and the bride sings; butter rises when the Groom is near.
Under the full moon the women churned curds and sang wedding songs of the soul as a bride, hoping the churn would bring the butter of union with the Groom; please write a doha.
The physician can find no illness in the bride; her only sickness is that the Husband has not yet come.
My cousin has stopped eating before her wedding and the physician just laughed and said she is a bride, leave her be.
doha: a physician cant cure a bride, she only waits for the divine husband
physician and bride
The physician was called to the bride who would not eat, and he said no medicine could help, for she was only love-sick for her Bridegroom; write me a doha in which the soul is that waiting bride.
tilak and ocean, bride
doha with a tilak and the ocean about a bride soul awaiting her divine husband
The tilak is on her brow, the ocean before her; the bride waits for the Husband who comes from the infinite.
With the tilak glowing on her forehead the bride stands facing the ocean as if the Groom will come across its waves, and her heart is vast as the waters; compose a doha on the soul as a bride.
The bride put on her tilak and stood at the edge of the ocean all evening, as if the Groom might appear on the waves.
touchstone for the bride
The touchstone of patience tests the bride, and she passes, for her heart is the Groom's own.
The true bride is known by the touchstone of her patience, and the Groom accepts only the one who has waited without complaint; please write a doha in which the soul passes that test as a bride.
short doha about the soul as a bride passing the touchstone of the husband's test
My grandmother said a good wife is tested by waiting, as metal is tested on a touchstone, and she waited decades for her husband.
My little sister has been dressing up as a bride all week and says she is going to marry God when she grows up.

On the day of the wedding the bride rose early, bathed, and took her place at the head of the courtyard with the whole village singing, for the Bridegroom was about to arrive; write a long doha about this day.
doha: the soul as a bride awaiting the wedding day with her husband the divine
wedding day of the soul
The village sings, the bride is seated, and the Husband approaches; this is the day she was born for.
date palm, veiled bride
doha with a date palm and a veiled bride, the soul awaiting the divine groom
The date palm in our courtyard is where my cousin sat for her pre-wedding rituals, silent, as if already listening for her husband.
Under the date palm the bride sits veiled, and the Groom's hand lifts the cloth between her and the world.
Beneath the date palm, in the evening, the bride sat shy and silent, her face covered, waiting for the Groom to lift the veil, and I felt the soul was just like her; please compose a doha about it.
Tell me a story in a doha form in which the soul is a bride and the Lord is her bridegroom, and the long wait before the wedding is full of joy and anticipation rather than sorrow, please.
My niece is preparing for her wedding and she is not nervous at all, she says she is just so sure of him.
doha about the soul as bride, calm and happy that her husband the divine will come
The bride has no complaint against the wait, for the wedding is certain, and her Husband is faithful.
the happy bride-soul
hey a doha with a cloth sheet about the bride-soul awaiting her divine husband
My mother spread a fresh cloth sheet on my bridal bed the evening before my wedding, humming the song of the bride going to her Lord.
The cloth sheet is spread and the bridal bed is made; the bride waits, clean of all but the Groom's name.
cloth sheet for the groom

Please write a doha in which the cloth sheet spread over the bridal bed is the soul's offering, clean and unwrinkled, for the Bridegroom who will come to sit upon it and bless the bride with his presence.
A palanquin waits by the mosque for the bride, who will be carried to the Groom's village, and the soul is that bride leaving her father's place forever; please write a long doha.
doha: a palanquin outside the mosque and a bride leaving for her husband
The palanquin waits by the mosque, the bride rises, and the whole world blesses her going to the Husband.
palanquin, mosque, the bride
At the wedding a palanquin stood by the mosque, and the bride's brother carried her to it, weeping, as if she were going off to God.
At my wedding a heron stood by the pond and my uncle joked that I was the real philosopher's stone, changing my husband's life.
heron, philosopher's stone, bride
doha with a heron and a philosopher's stone about the bride soul's journey
The heron fakes devotion, the philosopher's stone lies unclaimed, and the bride walks past both to her true Husband.
The heron stood by the philosopher's stone beside the pond as the bride went by to meet her Groom, and neither could touch her pure intent; compose a doha in which the soul is that bride.
My grandmother always said the only fortunate woman is one whose husband is alive and healthy, and she touches her vermilion each morning.
I want to hear a doha where the soul is the happy wife of the Lord, lucky and blessed as the wife whose husband is alive and near, so she needs no ornament, no festival, and no other protector.
Blessed is the wife whose Husband lives; she needs no ornament and no other, for he alone is her treasure.
doha: soul as a blessed wife whose divine husband is ever-present
fortunate wife of the Lord
doha with milk and dew for a bride soul on her wedding morning
Milk in her cup and dew on the grass, the bride feels the Groom in every drop of the morning.
milk and dew, bride
On the wedding morning the bride drank warm milk and watched the dew shine on the grass, feeling that she was already a part of the Groom's world; compose a doha about the soul as a bride.
My sister drank her last glass of milk as an unmarried girl and stared at the dew on the lawn, saying it felt like the end of one world.
The river runs, the spinning wheel hums, and the bride weaves her own wedding dress for the Husband she has not yet seen.
My grandmother spun her own wedding cloth at the spinning wheel by the river, singing of a Groom she had never met.
river, spinning wheel, the bride
By the river the women are spinning at the spinning wheel their own wedding clothes, singing of the Groom to come; write a long doha in which the soul is a bride waiting for the Lord.
doha with a river and a spinning wheel for a bride-soul readying for the husband
The bride has covered her face with a veil and waits behind the screen, trembling with joy, because the Bridegroom is the Lord himself; please write a long doha about the soul as that bride.
please write a doha about the soul as a bride about to meet her divine groom
the veiled bride
Behind her veil the bride trembles with delight, for the Husband she was promised has come to the edge of the village.
My cousin's wedding is tomorrow and she keeps saying she is not afraid, just so happy that her husband is such a good man.
At my wedding the first dish was a bitter gourd, and my mother-in-law said that a good wife eats what her husband gives with love.
bitter gourd for the bride
doha: bitter gourd at a bride's feast, the soul accepting all from the divine husband
The bitter gourd on the wedding plate tastes sweet to the bride, for she takes it from the Husband's hand.
The bitter gourd on the wedding plate is for the bride to taste first, a custom that teaches the soul to accept both bitter and sweet from her Bridegroom's hand; write a doha, long and gentle.
doha about cotton and a bride soul preparing the wedding bed for her divine husband
I picked white cotton from the field to stuff the pillow of the bridal bed and, thinking of the Bridegroom, sang the whole day long; write a doha in which the soul is the bride preparing.
My mother picked cotton from our own field to make my wedding quilt and said it will keep you warm like your husband's love.
cotton for the wedding bed
Soft cotton for the bridal bed, and the bride sings; the Groom is certain and the day is near.

crossroads market, humble

need a doha about being away from the person you love, cant sleep, feel empty
Without you the nights have no end and the days no meaning; the beloved is far and the heart is hollow.

doha pls, caged heart, boat leaving without me, missing my beloved so much

Every evening I light a lamp at the window for the one who has not come back, and I sit sleepless as it dies out, so please write a doha about this endless waiting in the dark.
At the cremation ground the water pot is cracked and the beloved is gone; what is left of the world is smoke.

At the cremation ground I stood with my pot of water and wept, for the one I yearned for had left me forever; compose a doha about the kind of absence that empties the whole world.
doha: lover gone forever, cremation ground and a pot of water
cremation ground, pot of water
The palanquin went and my shadow stayed, a thin companion on a road that carries nothing now.

In the afternoon heat I only see my own shadow walking beside me where the palanquin once carried my bride, and a longing deeper than words grips me. Please write a doha about the empty road without her.
doha with a palanquin leaving and a shadow staying behind, missing someone
shadow, empty palanquin

doha like a thief took my peace when my partner left, im not okay

There was a thief in the night who stole my sleep, my appetite, and my reason when my beloved walked out, and I have been bereft since. Compose a doha about this theft of everything by absence.
thief of sleep

doha about a diamond ring left behind and the heart missing its owner
diamond in an empty room
The diamond keeps its brilliance, I keep my ache; what good is a jewel when the one who gave it is far?
My fiancee left her diamond ring on the shelf before she traveled and now I sit staring at it every night.
The rooms feel like a stranger's since my daughter left for hostel, and I keep setting her plate out at dinner.
a doha for when your beloved is far away and the evenings feel so long and silent
Sleepless I count the hours of an endless night, for the beloved is far and the heart has lost its voice.
parted, sleepless
When my mother left for the long pilgrimage the whole place fell silent, the evenings stretched out and I forgot how to sleep. Write me a doha for a heart parted from the one it needs.
Honestly I stopped wearing my gold chain after my husband left for the Gulf, it just felt wrong without him to show it to.
The gold fades on the wrist of the waiting one, for her true ornament is the beloved who is far away.

doha pls: gold jewelry means nothing now that my beloved is away
gold without the beloved

bereft among the crowd
a doha about being among people yet feeling empty because the one you love isnt there

doha about the moon rising and the one i miss being far away
the moon without you

The moon rises over an empty courtyard and mocks the one who sits without her beloved.
loom and absence
The shuttle moves across the loom but the heart's weave is cut; she weaves and waits for the one who left.

doha with a loom, a woman waiting for her beloved to come back

a doha for waiting for someone who said theyd be back and isnt
he did not return

spinning wheel, cremation ground

The spinning wheel is idle, the cremation ground is quiet; the one who spun my life has gone beyond.
I came to the cremation ground to scatter her remains and the spinning wheel in our old room still stands still; I ache so deeply I cannot sleep. Compose a doha about this heart-rending absence.

We toured the palace on our honeymoon, and walking there alone this year I picked up a fallen leaf and wept quietly.

ache without end

a doha about longing so intense you cant sleep, because the one you love is far
Since my partner moved to another country the quiet in our rooms is so loud that I can barely stay in them, and the evenings are the hardest of all, so please write me a doha.

Pot of water and lit lamp, the bed is made; only the Beloved is absent, and he is everything.
doha about someone doing the daily rituals of their absent partner, lamp and pot of water
lamp, pot of water, waiting
I fill the pot of water at the village pond just as she used to, and light a lamp by the bed, but the one I wait for does not come; write a doha for a heart long left behind.

arrow and spinning wheel
