The churn turns, the butter rises; so the wise mind turns each matter until the real floats up.
churn, separating real
My aunt churns every morning and always knows the moment the butter has formed; I wish I could sense the right moment to separate fact from rumor like that.
pearl, real versus fake
My friend bought a pearl at a bargain price, and I could tell at a glance it was glass; people ask how I knew, and I want a doha on that sense.
doha: tell a real pearl from a fake one
Craft a doha about the keen eye that tells a real pearl from a glass imitation at one look, showing that the discerning person judges by what a thing is rather than how brightly it shines.
The pearl and the glass both gleam; only the clear eye knows which was born of the deep.
thief, needle, sharp judgment
I once spotted a thief pretending to be a customer because I noticed one tiny detail, as fine as the eye of a needle, and I want a doha on such sharpness.
The thief hides in honest clothes, but the sharp eye passes the needle of the real through the false.
doha w thief + needle: spotting liars with sharp eyes

Please make a doha about the sharp eye that sees through the thief's honest face, passing through the finest needle's gap of detail to tell the real from the pretended, and so protecting the household.
temple, telling true from false
A man who loudly gives at the temple gets everyone's respect in our town, but I look at how he treats his workers, and I think judgment should rest on that.
doha: dont judge by temple donations, see how they act
Not by the offerings at the temple but by the deeds of the day does the wise judge a soul.
Write a doha about the discerning person who looks beyond the show of devotion at the temple to the hidden conduct of a man, and judges his worth by what he does rather than what he displays.
doha: at a crossroads u gotta pick the real path not the flashy one
At the crossroads many voices call; the clear-eyed one walks the road that is real, not the one that glitters.
I need a doha about a person standing at the crossroads of a major decision, surrounded by tempting offers, who calmly separates the real from the showy and chooses wisely.
crossroads, choosing wisely
I am at a crossroads with two job offers, one that shines and one that is quietly right, and I would like a doha about telling them apart.
doha on wise judgment, tell good from bad
clear judgment
The sharp eye parts the true from the false as dawn parts the night from the day.
Please write a doha about the ability to look at a person, a promise or an idea and quickly see whether it is real or counterfeit, a gift that protects a person through all his life.
My grandmother never went to school but could tell in a minute who was honest, and I would love a doha about that kind of judgment.
After the village drought, my mother would sip from a pot of water, drop in a leaf, and judge by it whether it was safe, and I think of that careful sense.
pot of water, leaf, judging
Can you put together a doha about the wise person who knows by a single leaf floating in a pot of water whether the water is clean, a mind that reads small signs to tell real from false.
A single leaf upon the pot of water tells the careful eye what is clear and what is not.
doha w pot of water + leaf: reading small signs to judge
Write a doha for the one who needs to pick friends carefully, saying that real discernment is the quiet sense that separates the loyal from the merely pleasant and keeps one safe in the crowd.
choosing the genuine
Many smile at the gate; the wise one knows which smile is true.
After my business partner betrayed me, I finally understood the difference between those who flatter and those who are real.
doha on picking genuine friends over fake ones
chakor bird, moneylender, judgment
doha w chakor bird + moneylender: spotting the real deal from the fake
The chakor bird waits only for what is real, while the moneylender's smile is a price; the wise know the difference.
A moneylender offered me a friendly deal that sounded too sweet, and I remembered the loyalty of a chakor bird, and could finally tell what was real.

Give me a doha about how the chakor bird will not accept a substitute for what it longs for, while the moneylender's sweet words come with hidden cost, teaching the wise to separate genuine from calculated.
doha on knowing right from wrong clearly
I'd like a doha for the young about the quiet gift of seeing a thing as it truly is, without being fooled by its dress, a gift that grows with patience and keeps them from many a regret.
At the interview I could sense that the glowing description of the job was not matching the way people acted, and it saved me from a mistake.
seeing what's real
Dress and name may change a hundred times; the clear mind sees what lies beneath.
furnace, real versus fake
A smith told me he can tell real metal from false just by how it behaves in the furnace, and I wish people were so easy to read.
doha: furnace shows whats real, how to tell ppl apart
The furnace proves the metal; the wise mind proves every claim and keeps what survives.
Write a doha about how the furnace separates the real from the counterfeit, and how the wise person puts every claim and every character to some test so that only what is genuine remains.
A fine cloth sheet may hide a rough body; the wise look past the covering to what lies beneath.
A man in a beautifully clean cloth sheet came calling with a pious story, and my gut told me something was wrong, and it was.
Craft a doha showing that the clean cloth sheet one wears is no proof of a clean heart, and that the discerning person looks beneath the covering to tell the real from the pretended.
cloth sheet, seeing beneath
doha w cloth sheet: dont trust clothes, check the person
Please make a doha about the discerning listener who is not swayed by a smooth tongue, who listens to what is said and weighs it against what is done, and so is rarely deceived by sweet words.
The tongue may drip with honey; the wise ear weighs the deed behind it.
tongue, judging words
A smooth-talking coworker charmed everyone, but I noticed his words never matched his actions, and I would like a doha for the quiet watchful ones.
doha: dont trust sweet talk, check the actions
crow, oil press, judgment
The crow chatters; the oil press hums; the wise ear knows which is noise and which is yield.
doha w crow + oil press: tell noise from real work
In our village the crow's loud cawing and the oil press's steady hum fill the morning, and I learned to tell who in town is noisy and who actually works.
Write a doha about how the crow makes much noise and gives nothing, while the oil press works quietly and yields oil, teaching the wise to tell the loud from the productive.
doha: dont judge ppl by how often they go to the mosque, look at their deeds
Not by the prayers at the mosque but by the kindness of the hand is the true heart known.
I need a doha about the discerning mind that does not judge a man by how many times he is seen at the mosque, but by how he treats the hungry and the weak outside.
mosque, judging by deeds
Everyone in our neighborhood praises a man who is at the mosque five times a day, but I watched how he treated his workers and drew my own conclusion.
Can you put together a doha that says the sharpest eye is not the one that sees most but the one that tells real from unreal, and that such judgment outweighs any amount of information.
sharp judgment
Many see; few can tell the true from the shine.
doha on sharp judgment
I used to collect facts, but I only became wise when I learned to judge which ones were real and which were noise.
potter and clay, bell, judgment
The potter taps his work and hears the flaw; the bell rings true only if it is whole; the wise ear tells which is sound.
doha w potter and clay + bell: ear tells whats sound
A potter shaping clay taps his work and listens for the flaw, and a bell rings clear only when it is whole; I want a doha about that kind of sharp judgment.
Write a doha about the potter who works clay and listens to the ring of his work, like a bell that sounds true only when sound, teaching the wise to tell the real from the flawed by gentle testing.
ocean, bitter gourd, discernment
Give me a doha about how even the whole ocean cannot sweeten a bitter gourd, and how the wise person learns to see a thing's real nature and not be fooled by where it was bathed.
Though bathed in the ocean, the bitter gourd stays bitter; the clear eye knows the nature beneath the wash.
My relative made pilgrimage everywhere, as if bathing in the ocean, but remained as harsh as a bitter gourd, and it taught me to judge by nature and not by display.
doha w ocean + bitter gourd: judge a persons nature not their rituals
doha w lock: smart ppl know which key fits, i wanna judge right
lock, finding what fits
I tried several keys on the old lock, and watching how the right one slid in made me think of how real choices click when you see clearly.
I'd like a doha about the discerning person who knows at once which key fits which lock and which choice fits which need, because his clear mind sees what is real and what only looks like it fits.
Many keys glitter, but only one turns the lock; the clear-eyed know it by feel.
The furnace proves the metal, the ear proves the tongue; the wise mind keeps what survives the test.
A friend's sweet-tongued promise went through the furnace of a hard situation, and only then did I see which of his words were real.
doha w tongue + furnace: promises get tested by hard times
tongue, furnace, testing words
Write a doha about how a tongue can say anything, but the furnace of hardship proves which words were real, a lesson in the discerning habit of watching how people behave under heat.
furnace, physician, judgment
doha w furnace n physician: a good doctor can tell real from fake
The physician tests the fever, the furnace tests the metal; the wise test all things before trusting.
Craft a doha about the physician who tells a real illness from a pretended one at a glance, and the furnace that tells real metal from false, showing the value of trained judgment.
Our family physician can tell at once when someone is faking an illness, as a smith can read metal in the furnace, and I would love that kind of sharp judgment.
tree, judging by fruit
My grandfather used to say you know a tree by its fruit, not its shade, and that is how he judged people his whole life.
Judge the tree by its fruit, not its height; so the wise judge a soul by deeds.
doha: tree is known by its fruit, judge ppl by actions
Please make a doha showing that a tree is known by its fruit and not by its height or its bark, just as the discerning judge a man not by his claims but by what his life actually bears.
river, clear and muddy
doha w river: some flows clean, some muddy, learn to tell
The river carries clear and muddy together; the wise know which to drink.
Write a doha about the river that carries both clear and muddy flow in its course, teaching the wise to tell which source to trust and which to avoid, in people and ideas alike.
At the river I watched where the clear stream met the muddy one, and thought about how I should tell good influences from bad in my own life.
doha w temple + moth: dont get drawn to the shiny thing
My cousin gets drawn to every flashy new guru like a moth, and I keep telling him that real places like a true temple don't need to glitter; doha for him?
temple, moth, judgment
I need a doha about the moth that rushes to every bright thing and is burned, while the discerning visitor to a temple looks past the glitter to find what is truly sacred and steady.
The moth is drawn to the glitter; the wise one enters the temple's quiet and tells the real from the bright.
doha about choosing wisely between things that look alike

Please write a doha for a young person facing many tempting options, about the clear sense that separates what is lasting from what is only attractive, so that he does not spend his days chasing what fades.
I used to chase every shiny opportunity, and only after losing years did I learn to judge which ones were real.
lasting versus showy
Between the lasting and the showy, the wise choose the quiet and keep it.
The mind that tells the true from the false walks through a crowd as through an empty field.
doha about telling what is real
I could tell the moment my colleague began lying, just by something in how he spoke, and I want a doha about this inner radar.

Can you put together a doha about the keen inward sense that quietly tells a person which words are sincere and which are only polish, a sense that grows with attention and protects the one who has it.
inner judgment
The moneylender in our town is friendly and always smiling, but I learned to read his terms, not his smile, and that saved my family.
The moneylender's smile is wide and the contract narrow; the wise read the latter.

Write a doha about the discerning borrower who looks past the moneylender's friendly manner to the real terms, teaching that the sweetest voice is not always the safest and that careful judgment protects.
moneylender, reading carefully
doha w moneylender: dont trust the smile, read the terms
yogi, stone, true or false
The yogi sits as still as stone, but stillness is not always wisdom; the clear eye tells which is which.
A yogi in our area sits motionless like a stone and draws crowds, but I learned to ask what he actually knows, and not be impressed by stillness.
doha w yogi + stone: dont be fooled by looking calm
Give me a doha showing that a yogi may sit like a stone and impress the crowd, but the discerning person asks what lies behind the stillness, telling the genuinely wise from those who only appear so.
I want a doha about the person who can read a room and instantly tell who is sincere and who is acting, a quiet gift that comes from attention rather than cleverness and protects him all his life.
reading sincerity
In my first week at the new office, I could already tell who was real and who was posturing, and I would love a doha on that instinct.
Behind every mask, a quiet truth; the clear mind lifts the veil gently.
doha on spotting fake ppl
A cleric in our area gives impressive speeches, but I learned to ask who he actually helps, and the answer taught me how to judge.
doha: dont be fooled by a cleric's fancy speeches
cleric, judging by deeds
Grand is the cleric's speech, but the wise look at the hand that feeds the poor.
I'd like a doha about the discerning listener who does not judge a cleric by his fine speech or his title, but by what he actually does for the people around him, and so is never deceived.
dew, real versus fleeting
Dew shines like treasure at dawn and is gone by noon; the wise know which brightness lasts.
Write a doha about how dew shines like treasure at dawn but vanishes by noon, teaching the discerning mind to tell what is lasting from what only sparkles for a moment.
I almost invested everything in something that sparkled like dew in the morning, but judgment told me it would be gone by noon, and I stepped back.
doha w dew: shiny stuff doesnt last, learn to tell
Craft a doha about the thirsty person who tests a pot of water by its color and smell before drinking, showing how the wise do not swallow anything just because it is offered.
Before the thirsty lip touches the pot of water, the wise eye asks if it is clean.
On a long journey I was offered a pot of water by a stranger and checked it carefully before drinking, and later I thought of how we should check ideas the same way.
doha w pot of water: check before u drink it, same w ideas
pot of water, careful testing
sun, seeing clearly
Please make a doha about how the sun reveals the true colors of all things hidden in dim light, and how the discerning mind, like sunshine, shows what is real and what only seemed so in the dark.
Under the harsh afternoon sun I finally saw the real condition of the place I had been about to rent, and it taught me to look in clear light before deciding.
doha: the sun shows whats real, clear judgment
In the sun's full gaze the false loses its color, and the true stands plain.
palanquin, judging worth
A man arrived in a palanquin with great pomp, and many bowed, but I waited to see how he treated the bearers before forming my opinion.
The palanquin is gilded but the bearers are bent; the wise judge a man by his kindness to those who carry him.
Write a doha about the discerning observer who does not bow to the man in the palanquin until he sees how he treats those who carry him, judging worth by conduct and not by show.
doha w palanquin: dont judge ppl by their fancy ride
mosque, needle, judgment
I need a doha about the keen eye that passes like a needle of detail through the show at the mosque, telling the sincere worshipper from the one who performs, and judging by quiet signs and deeds.
At the mosque I could tell by the smallest detail, like the point of a needle, which of the men there were sincere and which were just performing; I want a doha on this.
The needle of the clear eye passes through the show at the mosque and finds the one who truly prays.
doha w mosque + needle: spotting sincere vs show
doha about choosing what is real over what looks good
I used to be impressed by anyone who looked successful, but life taught me to ask what is real underneath, and I want a doha about that change.
Appearance is a bright cover; the wise ask what lies behind.
separate real from fake
Can you put together a doha about the mature mind that no longer takes things at face value, that asks quietly what is real beneath what is shown, and so spends its days on what truly matters.
Write a doha about the cuckoo's sweet voice and the rope that binds, teaching that the discerning person listens to a pleasing voice yet checks whether a hidden cord of selfish intent is attached.
cuckoo, rope, careful judgment
A voice sweet as the cuckoo may hold a rope behind it; the wise listen and look.
A salesman with a sweet cuckoo-like voice almost got me to sign a contract that was a rope around my neck; I would like a doha on staying alert.
doha w cuckoo + rope: sweet voice can hide a trap
true versus false
I went through my old beliefs one by one, keeping those that held up and dropping the rest, and it felt like a spring cleaning of the mind.
doha: sorting what to believe and what to drop
Let the mind be a quiet judge, keeping the true and releasing the false without anger.
Give me a doha about the daily habit of examining each belief and each claim, keeping what is real and releasing what is false, until the mind is clear, light, and not easily fooled.
My landlord, a moneylender, fasts every Monday and proudly tells the whole building, then raises our rent the next day. His shadow looks hungrier than he does. Doha?
doha on a moneylender who fasts for show while squeezing the poor, with his shadow of guilt
The moneylender starves the body for a day and feeds the greed for a year, and his shadow grows long with both.
A doha about the moneylender who keeps a strict fast each week and boasts of his hunger, while his long shadow falls across the debtors he has ruined, and no fasting touches the greed in his mind.
moneylender, shadow, fasting

People starve themselves on the appointed days and think the tongue's restraint is holiness, but the tongue that avoids grain still slanders, and the mind that has not been fasted from anger stays fat with sin.
My aunt is on a strict fast today and has snapped at everyone, and her tongue is sharp enough to cut the vegetables she is not eating. Doha for her?
The tongue fasts from food, but feasts on gossip.
fasting, tongue, cruelty
doha about fasting but letting the tongue say nasty things
thorn, penance, show
doha: lying on a bed of thorns for show, your mind still isn't clean
A doha on the penance of the man who lies on a bed of thorns for the crowd, wounding his body to impress the watchers, though the thorn of anger in his own mind remains unremoved.
He lies on thorns to show the world, yet carries a sharper thorn within that he will not pull out.
A man in the fair lay on a bed of thorns for hours, and people threw coins at him. He went home to count them. Kabir would laugh. A doha?
Write about the woman who keeps a fast for her family's welfare, rings the bell during her rituals for hours, and then scolds the servants, as though the vow and the bell could replace kindness.
doha: fasting vow plus ringing a bell all day and still being rude to everyone
The bell rings for the vow, the stomach is empty, but the heart is quite full of pride.
fast, bell, vow
My mother-in-law does her fast every week with a bell and a long vow, and then sits all evening telling us who in the family is a sinner. What a doha that would be
arrow, blind man, penance
doha: blind man shooting an arrow, penance aimed at nothing
The arrow of penance, loosed by a blind man, flies far from the mark of the mind.
My uncle took a vow of silence and fasting for forty days to impress the village, but he was as blind to his own anger as a blind man shooting an arrow in the dark. A doha?
A doha on the blind man who shoots the arrow of penance and vow into the dark, striking everything but the target, which is the cleansing of his own restless and greedy mind.
doha pls: fasting every week but still being greedy
hunger without humility
A doha about the people who deny themselves food on the holy days and think this makes them pure, though the hunger of the body is not the same as the hunger of the soul, nor does it teach humility.
He starves the belly and spoils the soul.
Everyone in my office who fasts on Tuesdays makes sure to announce it, and none of them is any kinder than on other days. Could you write a doha?
bell, rainbird, vow
The rainbird thirsts without announcing it, the bell rings out the vow of the proud.
A doha about the rainbird that fasts from all water but the one pure drop out of true longing, and the man who rings a bell to announce his fast and vows for the world to see.
A neighbour rings a bell every time she starts a new fast and tells the building, while the rainbird on our wire seems more patient in its thirst. A doha?
doha: rainbird really fasts, the man ringing a bell about his vow is just showing off
doha: fasting with a sword in hand and salt in the wound, vow to hurt others

A doha for the man who fasts and takes a solemn vow with a sword at his side, vowing revenge, while he refuses salt in his food and all the other pleasures, as if austerity and violence could live together.
sword, salt, vow
He gives up salt and keeps his sword, and calls the vow holy.
My neighbour has been fasting without salt for a month and brags about it, then threatened his brother with a sword over some land. A doha on that?
Every month my grandfather observes a strict fast in the house, and everyone has to be quiet, otherwise he curses them for disturbing his penance. A doha?
house, fasting, strict
A doha on the fasting householder who turns his house into a prison of rules and silence for the sake of his vow, making everyone around him suffer for his own supposed holiness.
The house goes hungry with him, and no one in it is any holier for his vow.
doha about fasting at home in the house and making everyone miserable
inn, bell, vow
At the inn the vow is announced with a bell; the Lord, who lives in the silence, is not impressed.
At the inn on our trip, a fellow guest kept a loud bell on his table to mark his fast, and he refused to share the table with anyone but demanded special food. A doha?
doha: vow at the inn with a bell, showing off his fast
A doha about the guest at the inn who keeps an elaborate fast with a ringing bell, demanding special meals from the host and staring down those who eat, as if his vow made him better than them.
doha: weaver's loom keeps working, fasting people just show off
The weaver in our lane works at his loom through the day without eating much, but he doesn't call it a fast or boast about it, unlike the others. A doha?
weaver's loom, honest hunger
A doha on the weaver at his loom who goes hungry without ever calling it a fast, and the man who fasts for a day and puts it in front of everyone, wondering which of them is truly spare.
The weaver at his loom has honest hunger; the proud man's hunger is a loud ornament.
My grandmother observes a fast on special days, applies sandalwood paste to the idol, and then criticises all of us for not being devout enough. Doha for her?
Sandalwood on the idol's brow and a fast on the stomach, but a mind with no coolness in it.
doha: fasting and sandalwood but still judgmental
Write a doha on the person who keeps a fast and applies sandalwood paste and sits very straight, expecting admiration, while the heat of judgement burns within and no sandalwood can cool it.
fasting, sandalwood, pride
doha: thief takes a vow to fast but doesn't stop stealing, with his sword
A local gang leader with a sword took a vow to fast every Friday and have the whole street know it, but he is still a thief. A doha?
The thief takes a vow of fasting and keeps the sword; it is the mind that starves of mercy.
thief, sword, vow
A doha on the thief who takes a solemn vow of fasting and continues to carry his sword and rob the helpless, as though a day without food could wash away a lifetime of cruelty.
Write about the priest who orders his followers to take difficult vows and fasts, while keeping himself in a comfortable cage of luxury, where the vow is for others and the feast is for himself.
Our priest told every family to do forty days of fasting and left for a hotel stay with his own family, saying the cage of his duties wore him down. A doha?
The priest shuts them in a cage of vows, and himself in a cage of comfort.
doha: priest demands fasting from others but eats royally himself, in a cage of luxury
priest, cage, vows
A doha about the person who starves his body for a vow and sees his own shadow grow thin, believing he is purifying himself, though the shadow of a proud mind does not grow thin with the body.
After two weeks of fasting my friend looked thin as a shadow, but still acted proud as ever and criticised those who ate. A doha for him?
doha: fasting makes you thin like a shadow but not a better person
The body thins like a shadow at evening, but the pride stays tall.
shadow, fasting, pride
door, fasting, pride
My neighbour sits at his door on fast days looking very pale and sighing so everyone will ask him what's wrong, so that he can tell them about his fast. A doha?
doha: sitting at the door looking weak to show off your fast
He sits at the door pale and sighing, hoping the world will ask about his hunger.
A doha on the man who waits at his door on days of fasting with a sad, pale face, hoping the neighbours will praise his austerity, as if the Lord only counted his vows when others did.
starving for show
What the belly misses, the pride devours; what the mind needs, no fast provides.
My friend took a fast for a month to prove he was devout to his in-laws, and then dined out on his last day with great relish. Doha?
write a doha about people who fast for attention
A doha on the person who takes a fast not out of love for the Lord but out of a wish to be admired by others, parading his thinness in front of the neighbours like a prize.
doha: fasting beside a stone idol hoping it will bless you
He fasts before the stone, and the stone does not feed him; the Lord is not in the stone.
My cousin fasted for a week in front of a stone image, promising to eat only when it answered his wish. Hunger was the only thing that answered. A doha?
A doha on the one who keeps a harsh fast before a stone and swears not to eat until it speaks, in the belief that his hunger will move a thing that has never moved.
fasting, stone
physician, fasting, show
The physician told my uncle his fasting was harming his health, but he said the vow mattered more than his life, and did it for the village to see. A doha?
doha: even the physician says starving yourself is not holy
The physician warns the fasting body, but the proud mind will not listen.

A doha on the physician who tells the faster that his vow is harming him, and the faster who ignores him, vowing even to die for the show of devotion, though the Lord asks for the cleansing of the mind.
The rich man in the palace on the hill fasts publicly every festival, while the tailor who sews his clothes with a needle goes without a meal every day and is never praised. A doha?
A doha on the lord of the palace who observes the great fasts with ceremony and applause while the humble tailor with his needle fasts through the year in poverty without a single word of praise.
doha: palace man fasts for show, tailor with a needle fasts for real out of poverty
palace, needle, fasting
The palace fasts with fanfare; the needle fasts in poverty, and only one is truly hungry.
thread, one-string lute, vow
Our wandering singer with a one-string lute took a vow to eat only once a day and ties a thread around his wrist to count each day. He tells everyone. A doha?
doha: one-string lute singer and a vow thread and showing off his fast
A thread round the wrist to count the vow, a one-string lute to announce it, and the mind not bound to the Name.
A doha on the singer with a one-string lute who ties a sacred thread to mark each day of his vow and sings of his own sacrifices, while his heart has not changed at all.
My friend gave up sweets for a month, announced it daily, and after the month ended she ate a whole box in one night. Did the vow cleanse her? A doha
For a month she gave up sweets and gave nothing else; on the last day she made up for it all.
doha on giving up something for a vow and going back to it
vow, then relapse
A doha on vows taken for a season and dropped at the end, as the person who gives up a pleasure for a month only to return to it more hungrily, having learned nothing about the desire itself.
date palm, yogi, penance
A doha about the yogi who stands for years beside a date palm in a vow of penance, with his arms raised till they wither, whose fruit of austerity is no sweeter than the date, which he never reaches.
The yogi raises his arm in penance beside the date palm that gives fruit to all, and his arm withers.
In our region there's a yogi who has kept one arm raised for years beside a date palm, and tourists take his photo. I don't see how it cleans his mind. A doha?
doha: yogi doing penance next to a date palm, wasting his body
Dew hangs on the grass at dawn, soon gone, like the vows of the one who stays at the inn of the body for a night.
dew, inn, vow
doha: dew vanishes by noon, like vows made at the inn
A doha on the vow taken in the early morning like dew on the grass, glistening with promise and gone by noon, as quickly as a guest leaves an inn, leaving no trace of change behind.
At the inn on our pilgrimage, a fellow guest vowed at dawn to give up anger, and by noon he was shouting at the cook. The dew had barely dried. Doha?
A doha on the blind man who vows to fast and perform hard penance every night under the stars, never seeing that the real darkness is in his mind and no vow can bring light unless he looks inward.
doha: blind man fasting under the stars hoping for light
A blind man in our village fasts in the courtyard under the stars each week, and people praise his penance, though he has never looked within. A doha?
Under the stars the blind man fasts, and calls the dark his penance.
blind man, stars, fasting
doha: why do people starve themselves for God
What god is pleased by an empty stomach, when the pure heart is hungry only for truth?
My aunt starves for a week at each festival and then falls ill, and the whole family has to care for her. She says it's devotion. What would Kabir say?
A doha on the ones who starve themselves for a god they say loves them, and who believe that suffering is the only coin the Lord accepts, though He has asked only for love.
starving for God
The heron fasts at the water's edge, the cloud fasts from rain; but the heron's patience is hunger and not holiness.

A doha about the heron that stands without food at the water's edge, looking like a saint at a fast, while really waiting for its meal, like those who fast for show and expect blessings under the cloud.
heron, cloud, fake fast
doha: heron looks like it's fasting, the cloud too, but both want something
My neighbour looked like a heron as he stood in the courtyard under the clouds, fasting in a loud display, and I knew he wanted the street's admiration. A doha?
doha: crow doesn't fast, he eats leaf scraps, honest vs a fasting hypocrite
crow, leaf, vow

A doha on the crow which eats what it finds without pretending to fast and the faster who eats a single leaf for show in public and gorges himself in private, the crow being the more honest of the two.
The crow eats what it finds; the faster eats one leaf in public and a feast in private.
A neighbour fasted in public and ate a leaf of tulsi, but I saw a crow stealing food from his kitchen, and I wonder whose fast it was. A doha?
doha: fasting without a clean heart is useless
My cousin fasts on Thursdays and gambles on Fridays. A doha for him please?
A doha for the one who fasts to please the Lord on the appointed days and spends the rest of the days in lies, gambling and anger, as if the Lord kept account of hunger and not of the heart.
Fast from anger and from greed; the belly's hunger cleans no soul.
fast, gambling, hypocrite
doha: a vow without effort to change is empty
A doha on the vow taken with great promises on a festive day and broken the next, which leaves the person exactly where he began, for the change a vow requires cannot be made by a promise alone.
A vow is a sapling that needs the soil of effort.
Each new year my brother takes a hundred vows, and each year he breaks them all before the end of January. Doha for him?
broken vows
He seeks the paras, the alchemist's touch, through fasting and penance, and washes the washerman's cloth of his own mind in hunger.
The washerman in our lane fasts to find the paras, the alchemist's touch, he says, and tells everyone, though I think the only thing he is washing is his pride. Could you write a doha?
paras, washerman, fast
doha: fasting to find the paras, the alchemist's touch, a washerman cleaning pride

A doha on the man who fasts and does penance to find the paras, the alchemist's touch, while the washerman beside him washes clothes in honest work, and finds more truth in his labour than the seeker in his fasting.
The old tree in our colony has a ribbon tied round it by women who fast for their husbands' long life, and then they quarrel loudly under it. A doha?
The women fast and tie their wishes round the tree, and the tree stands silent in its patience.
fast, tree, wish
doha: fasting under a tree for a wish, tree gives without fasting
A doha about the fast kept beneath a great tree, the vows made and wishes tied to its trunk with ribbons, while the tree, which gives shade to all without a vow, knows what it means to give.
milk, crow, fasting
On fast days my neighbour drinks only milk and sits proudly on the porch, and a crow steals the sweets from his plate, and he curses the poor crow. A doha?
doha: fasting on milk only and cursing a crow, what a joke
A cup of milk is a feast to the crow who knows true hunger, and the proud faster mocks the crow.
A doha about the faster who lives on milk alone and calls it hard austerity, while the crow who finds a hard crust to eat in the street is the one who has truly known hunger.
doha: fasting won't change you if your heart is closed
closed heart, open stomach
A doha on the faster who refuses food for the sake of holiness, yet keeps his heart closed to the poor at his gate who would be grateful for the meal he refuses and could use his kindness.
The plate is empty, but the hand is closed.
My neighbour's family fasts once a week, but when a hungry child came to their gate, they sent him away. Could you write a doha for them?
doha: chakor bird stays up all night in love, but humans fast for a day and think they're devoted
chakor bird, true fasting
A doha on the chakor bird that spends its nights gazing at the heavens in true longing, forgetting hunger and sleep, and the man who fasts for a day and thinks that is devotion enough.
The chakor bird forgets its food in love; the man remembers his vow in vanity.
My friend fasted for a day and told me the chakor bird could learn something from her devotion, though the bird forgets food from real longing. A doha for her?
A doha on the yogi who declares that he eats nothing and drinks nothing, who sits publicly for months in a vow of fasting, while a hidden disciple brings him food by night.
yogi, fasting, fraud
doha: yogi says he doesn't eat, but he does secretly
The yogi says he lives on air, and his disciple feeds the air in the dark.
A yogi in our area claimed he hadn't eaten for years, and then a villager saw a disciple secretly bringing him meals. Kabir would have loved that story. A doha?
doha: shroud like clothes and fasting, acting dead but not changed
He wraps in a shroud, he fasts as if already dead, yet the living greed still breathes.
A doha on the man who takes a vow to live as one dead, wearing a shroud and refusing food, to impress the village, though his desires are as alive as ever.
shroud, fast, show
My uncle wore a white shroud like robe for his month long fast and posed for photos with his hungry-looking face. The next week he bought a new TV. A doha?
A doha on the person who takes a vow of silence and fasting and counts the days on prayer beads, as though each bead were a coin paid into some heavenly bank, and not a day to be lived.
doha: counting prayer beads for vow days like a debt
prayer beads, vow, counting
He counts the days of the vow on his prayer beads, but the days of his anger go uncounted.
My aunt counts the days of her vow on prayer beads and gets angry if anyone disturbs her counting. Doha for her?
A doha for the priest who preaches long fasts, standing like a heron at the edge of the pond, looking very devout, though his eyes are fixed on the offerings the faithful will bring.
Our priest looks like a heron in his stillness during the fast, but his eyes follow every plate of offerings that comes in. A doha for him?
priest, heron, fasting
doha: priest fasting like a heron, waiting for offerings
The priest stands like the heron, eyes closed, fasting, and waiting for the offerings.
My brother took a vow to climb a hill barefoot to be forgiven, and complained the whole way and was rude to the porters. A doha?
A doha about the man who walks barefoot for miles on a vow, hurting his feet and boasting of it, though he is no closer to forgiving his enemies or asking forgiveness of those he has harmed.
doha: barefoot vow without a changed heart
barefoot vow
He tortured the soles of his feet, but the sole of his soul remained untouched.
He walks through the fire of penance with a proud step, yet the fire in his heart is never put out.
fire, penance, pride
doha: walking on fire as penance, still angry
A doha on the one who sits between fires in the summer heat as a penance for sins, enduring the pain to be seen by all, though the fire of anger in his heart is left to burn.
At the fair, a man walked over fire to fulfil a vow, and afterwards got into a brawl with the man selling him water. A doha for him?
The priest fasts and the thief fasts; one steals with his mouth, one with his hands.
The priest in our area fasts every second day and then charges a fee for every blessing, while the thief who robbed the corner store prayed and fasted too. A doha?
A doha on the priest and the thief who both keep a fast on a vow, the priest to look holy and the thief to be forgiven, though neither has stopped taking from the helpless.
priest, thief, fasting
doha: priest and thief both fast, no difference
A doha about the rainbird which fasts from all water but the single drop of rain, out of true longing, and the man who fasts as a rule and complains of thirst, never asking what he truly hungers for.
doha: rainbird's thirst is honest, human fasting is for show
My aunt complains the whole day when she fasts, while the rainbird outside our window waits all season for one drop without a word. A doha?
The rainbird thirsts in silence and the faster thirsts in speech.
rainbird, true thirst
touchstone, yogi, fasting
doha: touchstone test for a yogi's fasting
Rub the yogi's fast on the touchstone of conduct, and see how little worth is in it.
A famous yogi who fasts for months was tested by a skeptical journalist and his conduct fell apart like a cheap alloy on a touchstone. A doha?
A doha on the touchstone that tests the worth of a yogi's fasting and penance, and finds that true purity is not there, though the show of austerity is bright and loud.
doha: stop starving, start serving
Better a full plate shared with the hungry than an empty plate vowed to the sky.
serve, don't starve
A doha for the faster who gives up his meal and sits in hunger for the Lord, who would be better served if he gave that meal to a hungry stranger and took his vow of kindness instead.
During Ramadan style fasting season in our colony some families waste vast amounts of food at night after their day's fast, while the street kids go hungry. A doha?
My dad does a rigid fast every week, and he nags the family to do the same, but he doesn't seem happier or kinder for it. A doha?
doha: fasting makes people grumpy not holy
A doha on the man who imposes a fast on himself and his family, forcing every household member to share his rules, making everyone irritable, and calling the misery spiritual progress.
The fast makes the home sour, and he calls the sourness holiness.
grumpy faster
A doha on the vow taken at the sacred place with great drama before a crowd, then broken quietly in the privacy of one's room, where the Lord, who sees every secret, is the only witness.
doha: vow in public, break it in private
public vow, private lapse
What is sworn aloud is forgotten in whispers.
My colleague took a vow in front of the whole office to quit smoking and I saw him sneaking out for one behind the building two hours later. A doha?
The snake charmer in our town fasts on certain days to protect his snake and show his devotion, but he starves the snake the rest of the time. A doha?
He fasts for the snake's sake and starves the snake for his own.
doha: snake charmer fasts for show, snake starves
A doha on the fasting snake charmer who pretends his vow is a sacrifice for the creature, though the poor snake is half starved and the vow is only a show for the crowd that pays.
snake, fasting

For the festival the community built a bridge of flowers and the head of the committee, wearing a white shroud-like robe, did a very showy fast, while the real bridge in the village has been broken for years. A doha?
The bridge of flowers is built for the vow, and the shroud-clad leader's real bridge stays broken.

A doha on the one who wears a white shroud for his fast and builds a fancy bridge of flowers for the festival, while the real bridge that villagers need lies broken, and his vow does nothing for them.
bridge, shroud, vow
doha: shroud and bridge, fasting for show, real needs ignored
doha: fire and door, the vow to keep the door closed to the poor
door, fire, fasting
A man in our locality sits in front of his door with a burning fire on his fast days and tells everyone his vow, yet never opens the door to the hungry. A doha?
He fasts by the fire of the door and keeps it closed on those who are hungry.
A doha on the one who sits at his door beside a fire on fast days, vowing not to eat, who keeps the door shut against the hungry who come hoping for the meal he refuses.
doha about how only your deeds and good name remain after you go, with a cloth sheet in it
My grandfather's old cloth sheet still hangs in the village hall where he used to sit, and when people speak of him they tell stories of his kindness, not his land; I want a doha about that

Write a doha about a person who leaves behind nothing but a plain cloth sheet and the memory of his kindness, and how people weep at his going, though he laughed when he came, because his deeds remain
cloth sheet, good name
The cloth sheet fades with the years, but the name of a good man is washed whiter by every telling
A seed planted in kindness outlives the one who sowed it, while the ash of the proud blows away and the name goes with it
After my father's cremation the ash blew off and my cousins argued over his savings, but the seed he planted by the road grew, and neighbours queued to tell how he helped them; that is what remains
doha with a seed and ash about how your good deeds are what's left of you
Please write a doha in which the ash of a dead man blows away and the seed he planted becomes a shade for strangers, to show that only one's deeds and good name remain after one is gone
seed, ash, good deeds
The yogi in our village never owned a thing, but when he died, the whole district came to his funeral, and I keep thinking about what he left behind
Kabir said live so the world laughs when you come and weeps when you go; write a doha about a yogi who lived like that, with only his deeds and name behind him
doha about a yogi whose good name stays behind when he's gone
The yogi walked softly through the world and left no footprints, only a fragrance of deeds that people still follow
yogi, name that remains
At my old teacher's funeral hundreds of former students stood in the rain with no one to make them, and I understood what a life actually leaves behind
doha about how only your deeds and good name stay after you die
Wealth is buried and houses fall, but a good deed lives in the mouths of strangers long after the doer is dust
good name remains
Write a doha in Kabir's voice saying that after death neither wealth nor beauty remains, only the deeds one did and the name one earned, so live in a way that makes the world weep at your going
My grandmother's churn is long gone but every woman in the lane still mentions how she fed everybody who came by; that is what is left of her
doha with a churn, about your deeds being what remains after death
The churn goes silent, the hands go still, but the sweetness of her giving still lives in every mouth in the lane
churn, kind deeds

Please write a doha in which a woman works her churn and shares the butter with every guest, and when she dies the whole village weeps, because the good name she earned remains when the churn is silent
doha with a mountain and a tortoise, about the name you leave when you die
Write a doha in which a mountain stands for ages and a tortoise lives for centuries, yet both are forgotten, while one good person's name is remembered for generations because of his deeds
mountain, tortoise, good name
The mountain village where my grandfather taught still tells stories about him, though the old tortoise shrine has crumbled; the people keep his name when the building is gone
The mountain endures and the tortoise lives long, but only the deeds of the good are carried on the lips of the living
The physician who healed the poor for nothing is gone, but every mended child carries a little of him still
Our village physician died last winter and for three days the shops were shut and everyone came to the lane; he left no money, but I now know what a life can leave
Please write a doha about a physician who treated the poor without fee, and whose name is spoken with love long after he is dead, because what remains of a person is only what he gave away
physician, good deeds
doha with a physician, your good deeds are what stays after you go
doha about how only your deeds and your name stay after death
When our headmaster died the school was closed for a week by the students themselves, and I realised that is what a good name is
Write a doha in Kabir's voice telling us to live in such a way that when we were born the world was glad and we cried, but when we die the world cries and we smile at what we leave
Live so that the world weeps at your going, though you came laughing into it
deeds that remain
gold, good name
Write a doha in which a man piles up gold all his life and is forgotten the day after he dies, while a poor man who gave freely is remembered by every child in the lane, since only deeds remain
My grandfather left no gold, only a reputation in the lane for never turning anyone away, and ten years after his death people still bring us sweets in his name
The gold rusts in the strongbox and is divided by quarrelling heirs, but the good name needs no keeper
doha with gold, but what remains after death is your name
gold, bell, good deeds
doha with gold and a bell, what remains is your name and deeds
The gold that the old landlord kept was spent in a year, but the bell he gave to the village school still rings and everyone calls it his bell
Please write a doha in which a bell given to the village rings long after the donor's gold has been spent and divided, to show that it is the deed and not the wealth which remains in memory
The gold scatters but the bell given in kindness still rings the donor's name across the fields
When you came, the world laughed and you cried; live now so that when you go the world cries and you are glad
After my uncle's funeral a stranger came and said he was the reason her children went to school, and my uncle had never mentioned it to us; that is what he left
Write a doha in the style of Kabir that says it is only the goodness we do that remains after we go, not our riches or our family, so we should live so that people weep at our departure
name left behind
doha about leaving a good name behind, thats all that stays
doha with a peacock, what remains after we go is our deeds

Please write a doha in which a peacock dances and wins the world's praise for a season, though its beauty is gone with it, while the quiet good deeds of an ordinary man are remembered by the village for generations
The peacock's colours leave with the peacock, but the deed of a good man is a feather that never falls
The peacock in our village yard died last year and nobody remembers its dance, but they still remember the old man who fed it every day
peacock, lasting deeds
The tongue that spoke kindly is silent now, and the fly settles where it once spoke, but the words are still alive in other mouths
Write a doha in which the tongue of a kind man is stilled by death and a fly rests where it lay, while his gentle words live on and people repeat them, since only good speech and deeds survive us
tongue, fly, good name
doha with a tongue and a fly, what stays is your name and good words
My grandfather's sweet tongue won him a reputation across three villages, and even when a fly landed on his cold face at the end, the people said he was the one man who never spoke ill
At my grandmother's funeral the queue of people she had helped without telling anyone went on for an hour, and I realised that is what is left after a life
The wealth is spent and the walls are sold, yet one kindly act still shelters strangers in its shade
Please write a doha in the manner of Kabir that says what remains of us after death is only our deeds and the name we have earned, and that the wise person lives to earn a good name, not wealth
doha about how good deeds are all that remain of us
good name, nothing else
doha about how your name is all that lasts when you go
remembered deeds
The principal of our school died and the cemetery could not hold the people who came; he never had money, but he has left a school full of former students who are teachers now
Write a doha in simple Kabir-like words that says a person is remembered only for what he gave and did, so a wise person lives rightly, so that when he dies the world weeps and he leaves smiling
Names carved on marble crumble, but a name carved in another's heart is never washed away
doha with a priest and a traveler, what remains is the name you leave
Write a doha in which a priest and a traveler are both remembered by a village, the priest for his sermons and the traveler for helping a stranger, and the verse says only what we do remains after us
A traveler once mended the roof of our village priest without asking for anything and left the next morning, and fifty years later people still tell the story
The priest is remembered for his chants, the traveler for his kindness, and the kindness outlives them both
priest, traveler, good deeds
bitter gourd, kind deeds
Write a doha in which an old woman grows a bitter gourd for the whole lane to enjoy for free, and after she dies the lane remembers her for it, since only the good one does remains
My neighbour planted a bitter gourd vine for everyone to share, and after she died the whole lane kept the vine alive in her name; this is what I call a good life
The bitter gourd on the neighbour's wall tastes of the woman who planted it, long after the woman has gone
doha with a bitter gourd, the good deeds are what remain
Walk gently on the path, for the thorn you move aside will be remembered in your name when your feet are still
My father always moved the thorn bushes off the village path, and after he died people moved on in their lives but the path remains clear, and his name is still spoken; I want a doha on that
thorn, good name
doha with a thorn, your deeds are what stay after you die
Write a doha in which a man removes a thorn from the road for the unknown travellers behind him, and when he is dead, it is that small deed that people remember instead of all the things he owned
The well that my grandfather dug for the village still serves a hundred families, and nobody remembers his home but everyone knows his name; I want a doha about it
Please write a doha about a man who digs a water well for strangers and is remembered for it long after his wealth is gone, so that the world weeps at his going, and he leaves smiling
well, lasting name
He dug a well for the thirsty and left the world, and the water still says his name to everyone who drinks
doha with a well, only the good you do stays after you die
The spinning wheel is silent, but the cloth she wove for strangers still keeps them warm, and her name is spoken with love

Write a doha in which a spinning wheel stands silent after the death of the woman who used it to make warm clothes for the poor, and her name remains with those she helped long after the wheel is broken
My grandmother's spinning wheel is in the corner and it has not been used for years, but whenever the winter comes, the old women of the village say her name, because of the shawls she made for them
doha with a spinning wheel, what stays is the name and the deeds
spinning wheel, good deeds
When you came the world laughed and you wept: live now so that when you go the world weeps and you smile
doha about living so that people miss you when you're gone
Write a doha in simple words saying that wealth and beauty and power vanish when we die, and only the good we have done and the name we have earned stay behind, so we should live accordingly
At the end of the farewell party for my retiring boss, nobody spoke about his salary or his title, only about how he treated them; I want a doha out of that
deeds that stay
doha with a philosopher's stone, only your name remains when you're gone
philosopher's stone, good name
He never found the philosopher's stone, but he turned a hundred hearts kind, and that is what the village remembers

Please write a doha in which a man spends his life seeking a philosopher's stone and is forgotten, while his neighbour who helped everyone without thinking of gain is remembered by name for generations
My uncle sought a philosopher's stone and died poor and forgotten, but the man nearby who fed strangers is still talked about in the village; I'd like a doha about that
The moon outlives the poet, but the poem outlives the moon in the hearts of those who loved it
doha with the moon, only your good name stays when you die
moon, good name
My teacher died under a full moon and the people who came that night said his deeds would be spoken of as long as the moon rises; I want a doha for him
Write a doha in which the moon looks down on the grave of a good man and the villagers still speak his name by moonlight, since the only thing that remains of us is what we did for others
Write a doha in which the fish in the pond and the grindstone at the mill outlast the man who owned them, but the village remembers him because he fed the poor from his own grain
fish, grindstone, good name
The old miller who ran the grindstone also fed the fish in the pond behind his place, and when he died the whole village came to say that this is the man who never charged the poor
The grindstone grinds for the poor and the fish swim in the pond, and the miller's name floats in the memory of both
doha with a fish and a grindstone, the good name is what stays
Write a doha in Kabir's voice telling people to do such good that when they die the world is sad and they themselves are glad, since only name and deeds are left when the body is gone
The one who lives for others dies only once, and lives for ever in a hundred mouths
My cousin's wedding was attended by a thousand people who all spoke about the kindness of his father who had died the previous year; I'd like a doha on the name that remains
deeds that remain
doha about how only deeds remain when we are gone
Please write a doha in which a sword rusts in its sheath after a warrior's death, but the people he protected still honour his name, since the only thing that lasts of any person is the good he did
doha with a sword, what remains is your name and your deeds
My grandfather's sword hangs on our wall but nobody in the family speaks of it; they speak instead of the time he stopped a riot in the village with just his words
The sword rusts and the fame of the sword rusts with it, but the deed of the defender never grows old
sword, good name
At my friend's funeral the elders could not complete the rites because so many people wanted to say a few words, and I thought how little we notice of what we leave until it is too late
doha about how only your good name remains after death
Kabir said that wealth and kin all stay behind but one's deeds echo in the world, so write a doha that tells the reader to live in such a way that the world is sad when he leaves
good name, deeds
When the body is dust, the name of a good life walks the village lanes and is welcomed everywhere
Live so the world is glad at your birth and weeps at your leaving, and you alone are smiling
doha about leaving a good name when you die
My neighbour was rude, rich and alone when he died, but the old woman across the road was mourned by two villages; I want a doha about that difference
name that outlives us
Write a doha in Kabir's voice saying what remains of anyone after death is not his money but the name he earned, so the wise live rightly and the world weeps when they are gone
My grandfather used to run his prayer beads between his fingers, but what people remember about him is the way he fed the whole street during the flood
prayer beads, good deeds
doha with prayer beads, what remains after death is the good you did
Write a doha in which a man tells his prayer beads all day and is forgotten, while his neighbour who quietly shared food during hard times is remembered by name and mourned when he is gone
The prayer beads rest in the box, but the memory of a kind hand still goes round the village
Please write a doha in which a priest reads sacred words to the crowd and is forgotten, while the poor man who helped the same crowd when they were hungry is remembered, since only deeds survive us
doha with a priest, what stays when we die is our deeds
The priest's sermon fades with the evening, but the grain given to the hungry is remembered for a lifetime
priest, good name
At the fair, people could not remember the priest's sermon from last year, but they all remember the farmer who gave free water to everyone
beggar, good name
Write a doha in which a beggar who shared his last bread is mourned by the whole street when he dies, while a rich man nearby passes unnoticed, since only deeds and name remain
doha with a beggar, what remains is the good name you leave
The old beggar at our corner died last month and the whole street collected money for his funeral, because he always shared what he got; I want a doha for him
The beggar's bowl was empty, yet his death filled the lane with weeping, for he had given more than the rich
When my aunt died I was surprised at how many people who were not in our family came to tell me what she had done for them, and I had never known; I want a doha on that
Please write a doha in the manner of Kabir about how the deeds of a person remain when his body is dust and his wealth divided, and how a good name is the only inheritance that cannot be taken
The deeds you do in the dark are the lamps people carry for you when you are gone
name left behind
doha about only your deeds mattering after you die
Write a doha in which an arrow and a thorn are forgotten by those they pierced, but a kind word is remembered for a lifetime, so what remains of a man is what he gave
arrow, thorn, good name
doha with an arrow and a thorn, only the good you do stays when you go
My uncle had a thorn in his foot and an arrow scar in his arm from his youth, but when he died, people spoke of how he never harmed anyone and always helped; I want a doha about that
The arrow and the thorn are forgotten before the wound heals, but a kindness stays in the heart till the end of days
Write a doha in which a well and a forest are the gifts of a good man to his village, and long after he is gone the water still serves and the trees still shade, carrying his name
doha with a well and a forest, what remains is the good name we leave
My great-grandfather dug a well and planted a forest for the village, and a hundred years later people still say his name when they drink or sit in the shade
He dug the well and planted the forest and went away, but every drink and every shade is his name
well, forest, good name
doha with a swan and a crossroads, the good you do stays after you die
swan, crossroads, good name
At the crossroads where he fed the swan and the stranger alike, a shrine of memory still stands though he is gone
Write a doha in which a man builds a resting place at a crossroads and feeds a swan and strangers alike, and the world weeps when he dies and remembers his name for generations
The crossroads near our lane has a bench that my grandfather put there and a swan pond he dug; he is long gone, but I hear people say his name
When the body burns, the name of a good life rises like incense, and the world weeps, but the soul smiles
Write a doha in Kabir's voice: live so that the world laughed when you were born and you cried, and the world cries when you leave and you laugh, since only name and deeds stay
The funeral of the man in our lane was crowded though he was poor, and I understood that what he left was something that cannot be counted; I would like a doha on that
doha about living so that people cry when you go
good name, remembered
Write a doha in which a rainbird calls for rain and a shroud covers a good man, and the people say that his deeds were like rain on a dry field and his name will outlast the shroud
At the funeral of our old farmer, a rainbird kept calling as they wrapped him in the shroud, and the whole village said his kindness was like rain; I want a doha on that
rainbird, shroud, good name
The rainbird cries, the shroud is white, and the good man who wears it is taken, but the rain of his kindness falls on
doha with a rainbird and a shroud, what stays is the name you leave
Write a doha in which a washerman does his work for poor families without charge and is remembered with love long after his death, since a person's true wealth is the good name he leaves behind
The washerman who cleaned clothes for the whole village for free during the epidemic is still spoken of, though he died long ago; what a person leaves is his deed
doha with a washerman, your deeds are all that remain
The washerman scrubbed the clothes of the poor and left his name clean in every household
washerman, good name
The temple's grand gift came from a rich man and is forgotten, but the water pot kept at the gate by a poor woman still holds her name
doha with a temple, only your name and deeds remain after you go
temple, good name
The big temple in our town was built by a king nobody remembers, but the old woman who gave water to pilgrims at its gate is still talked about; I want a doha for her

Please write a doha in which a man builds a grand temple for his own glory and is forgotten, while a poor woman who gave water to the weary at its gate is remembered, since only the humble deed remains
